CANDLE ANATOMY FOUNDATION

Every candlestick encodes 4 price points — master this before everything else

BULLISH CANDLE

Close > Open · Buyers won · GREEN

BEARISH CANDLE

Open > Close · Sellers won · RED

WICK / SHADOW MEANING

Long wick = price rejected that level.
Body = actual accepted movement.

KEY READING RULES
BODY SIZE
Large body = strong conviction. Small body = indecision.
WICK SIZE
Long wick = failed attempt. Buyers/sellers rejected.
CONTEXT
Same candle = different meaning at support vs resistance.
VOLUME
High volume confirms. Low volume = weak signal, skip.

SINGLE CANDLE PATTERNS 18 PATTERNS

How to read each card below:
· Drawing = what the candle looks like on a chart
· Coloured badge — green means bullish (price likely to go up), red means bearish (price likely to go down), yellow means neutral or reversal warning
· Description = what the candle tells you about who is winning the fight between buyers and sellers
· Action line (BUY CALL, BUY PUT, or WAIT) = the recommended intraday option-buying response

Important for beginners: A pattern by itself is not a trade signal. Always wait for the candle to fully close, then check three things: volume (was it above average?), higher timeframe trend (which direction is the daily chart moving?), and the nearest support or resistance level. A pattern that forms at the right location is high-probability. A pattern in the middle of nowhere is just a coin flip.
MOMENTUM CANDLES
BULLISH MARUBOZU
STRONG BULLISH
A full green body with no wicks at all. Buyers were in complete control for the entire candle period.
→ BUY CALL
BEARISH MARUBOZU
STRONG BEARISH
A full red body with no wicks at all. Sellers were in complete control for the entire candle period.
→ BUY PUT
OPENING MARUBOZU (BULLISH)
BULLISH
No lower wick (the candle opened at its lowest price), with a small upper wick. Buyers took control from the very first second of the candle.
→ BUY CALL
OPENING MARUBOZU (BEARISH)
BEARISH
No upper wick (the candle opened at its highest price), with a small lower wick. Sellers took control from the very first second of the candle.
→ BUY PUT
CLOSING MARUBOZU (BULLISH)
BULLISH
No upper wick (the candle closed at its highest price), with a small lower wick. Buyers won the fight by the close, regardless of how the candle started.
→ BUY CALL
CLOSING MARUBOZU (BEARISH)
BEARISH
No lower wick (the candle closed at its lowest price), with a small upper wick. Sellers won the fight by the close, regardless of how the candle started.
→ BUY PUT
When to take this trade — Bullish Marubozu
Setup
A full green Marubozu candle has just closed on your trading timeframe (5-minute or 15-minute). The candle is at least as large as the average of the last 10 candles. Volume on this candle is 1.5 times higher than the recent average. The broader trend (daily chart) is also moving up.
Entry
Buy a Call Option (At the Money or one strike Out of the Money) at the open of the very next candle. Do not wait for a pullback; momentum candles often run hard in the same direction for the next 2 to 4 candles.
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss at the low of the Marubozu candle on Nifty. For the option premium, set a hard stop at 30 to 35 percent loss of the option price.
Target
Aim for the next major resistance level above. The minimum target should be 2 times your stop loss distance. Trail your stop loss to breakeven once you are 1 times the stop loss distance in profit.
Skip if
The Marubozu forms during the lunch hour (12:30 PM to 1:30 PM IST), there is a major news event in the next hour, or the candle forms right into a strong resistance level (price might run out of room).
DOJI FAMILY
STANDARD DOJI
INDECISION
The opening price equals the closing price, with roughly equal upper and lower wicks. Perfect indecision — buyers and sellers are evenly matched.
→ WAIT
DRAGONFLY DOJI
BULLISH REVERSAL
Long lower wick with no upper wick. Buyers absorbed all the selling pressure and pushed price back up. Strong signal when this appears at a support level.
→ BUY CALL
GRAVESTONE DOJI
BEARISH REVERSAL
Long upper wick with no lower wick. Sellers rejected the highs and pushed price back down. Strong signal when this appears at a resistance level.
→ BUY PUT
LONG-LEGGED DOJI
EXTREME INDECISION
Very long wicks on both sides. There was massive intraday volatility but no clear winner. The market is confused.
→ WAIT
FOUR-PRICE DOJI
NO MOVEMENT
The open, high, low, and close are all the same price. Zero movement. Usually seen in illiquid stocks or when the market is halted.
→ AVOID
RICKSHAW MAN
MAXIMUM INDECISION
A Doji with equal long wicks and the body sitting exactly in the middle. The highest level of uncertainty in candle patterns.
→ WAIT
When to take this trade — Dragonfly Doji at Support
Setup
A Dragonfly Doji has formed exactly at a known support level (such as the previous day's low, the 20 period Exponential Moving Average, or a Volume Weighted Average Price). The lower wick is very long and the body is tiny at the top.
Entry
Buy a Call Option (At the Money or one strike Out of the Money) only after you see a green confirmation candle close above the high of the Dragonfly Doji. Do NOT enter on the Doji candle itself.
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss below the lowest point (the bottom tip of the lower wick) of the Dragonfly Doji. For the option premium, exit if you lose 30 to 40 percent of the option price.
Target
Aim for the next resistance level above. Minimum target is 2 times your stop loss distance. The Dragonfly often signals a multi-candle reversal, so book half the position at the first target and trail the stop on the rest.
Skip if
The Doji forms in the middle of nowhere (not at a known support level), the daily trend is strongly downward, or the confirmation candle never appears within 1 to 2 candles after the Doji.
REVERSAL CANDLES
HAMMER
BULLISH REVERSAL
Small body at the top, with a lower wick that is at least 2 times longer than the body. Signals a bullish reversal when it appears at a support level.
→ BUY CALL
HANGING MAN
BEARISH REVERSAL
Same shape as a Hammer but appearing at the top of an uptrend. Warns that a bearish reversal is likely.
→ BUY PUT
INVERTED HAMMER
BULLISH REVERSAL
Long upper wick with a small body at the bottom. A bullish reversal signal when it appears at a support level.
→ BUY CALL
SHOOTING STAR
BEARISH REVERSAL
Long upper wick with a small body at the top. A bearish reversal signal when it appears at a resistance level.
→ BUY PUT
BULLISH BELT HOLD
BULLISH
Opens at the session low (no lower wick) and closes near the high. A strong single-candle bullish reversal.
→ BUY CALL
BEARISH BELT HOLD
BEARISH
Opens at the session high (no upper wick) and closes near the low. A strong single-candle bearish reversal.
→ BUY PUT
When to take this trade — Hammer at Support (the most reliable single candle)
Setup
A Hammer candle has formed at a known support level on the 15-minute or hourly chart. The lower wick is at least 2 times the size of the body. The body sits in the upper third of the candle. Volume on the Hammer candle is above the average of the last 10 candles.
Entry
Buy a Call Option (At the Money or one strike Out of the Money) when the very next candle opens above the Hammer's high. The next candle must be green; if it opens lower or red, skip the trade entirely.
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss 5 to 10 points below the bottom tip of the Hammer's lower wick on Nifty. For the option premium, exit if you lose 30 to 40 percent of the option price.
Target
Aim for the next resistance level above. Minimum target is 2 times the size of the Hammer candle (measured from low to high). Book half at the first target and trail the stop on the rest of the position.
Skip if
The Hammer forms in the middle of nowhere (no clear support nearby), the broader market trend is strongly downward, the next candle does not confirm with a green close above the Hammer's high, or the Hammer formed during the lunch hour.
When to take this trade — Shooting Star at Resistance
Setup
A Shooting Star candle has formed at a known resistance level. The upper wick is at least 2 times the size of the body. The body sits at the bottom of the candle. Volume is above average on the Shooting Star candle.
Entry
Buy a Put Option (At the Money or one strike Out of the Money) when the next candle opens below the Shooting Star's low. The next candle should be red. If it opens higher or green, skip the trade.
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss 5 to 10 points above the top tip of the Shooting Star's upper wick. For the option premium, exit if you lose 30 to 40 percent.
Target
Aim for the next support level below. Minimum target is 2 times the size of the Shooting Star candle. Book half at the first target and trail the stop on the rest.
Skip if
The Shooting Star forms in the middle of nowhere, the broader trend is strongly upward, the next candle does not confirm with a red close, or the formation happens during the lunch hour.
INDECISION CANDLES
SPINNING TOP
INDECISION
A small body with roughly equal wicks on both sides. Neither buyers nor sellers were able to dominate.
→ WAIT
HIGH WAVE
HIGH VOLATILITY
A tiny body with extremely long wicks on both sides. A wild, directionless session with high emotion and no clear winner.
→ AVOID
SHORT CANDLE
LOW VOLATILITY
A short body with short wicks. Indicates low volume sideways consolidation or a quiet choppy market.
→ WAIT

BEGINNER PRIORITY — MASTER THESE FIRST

  • Bullish and Bearish Marubozu — Unmistakable strong-trend candles. Easy to spot, and very reliable when they close at the top or bottom of a visible range.
  • Hammer and Shooting Star — The two most reliable single-candle reversals. A Hammer at support means you can buy the next candle's open with a Call Option. A Shooting Star at resistance means you can buy a Put Option.
  • Doji — The universal indecision signal. Never trade a Doji on its own — it is a warning to pay attention, not an entry signal. Wait for the next candle to break in one direction, then take action.
Common beginner mistake: Buying the MOMENT you see a pattern. The pattern must appear at a meaningful location (previous day high or low, Volume Weighted Average Price line, Central Pivot Range edge, or trendline) with above-average volume. Patterns that form in no-man's-land in the middle of the range are mostly noise and should be ignored.

TWO-CANDLE PATTERNS 16 PATTERNS

Why two candles are better than one: A single candle can fool you. The second candle is the confirmation that the move is real. In an Engulfing pattern, the second candle must completely cover the first candle's body. In a Piercing Line, the second candle must close above the midpoint of the first one. This "two-candle rule" filters out many of the false signals that single candles can produce.

How to use these patterns: Wait for the second candle to fully close before taking action. Enter on the open of the next candle. Place your stop loss at the lowest point of the whole pattern (for bullish setups) or the highest point of the whole pattern (for bearish setups).
ENGULFING FAMILY
BULLISH ENGULFING
BULLISH REVERSAL
A green candle's body completely covers (engulfs) the previous red candle's body. A powerful reversal signal at a support level.
→ BUY CALL
BEARISH ENGULFING
BEARISH REVERSAL
A red candle's body completely covers (engulfs) the previous green candle's body. A powerful reversal signal at a resistance level.
→ BUY PUT
When to take this trade — Bullish Engulfing at Support (the gold standard)
Setup
A clear Bullish Engulfing pattern has formed at a known support level (such as the previous day's low, the 20 period Exponential Moving Average, or a Volume Weighted Average Price line). The green engulfing candle's body fully covers the red candle's body, AND it closes above the red candle's open. Volume on the green candle is at least 1.5 times the average of the last 10 candles.
Entry
Buy a Call Option (At the Money or one strike Out of the Money) on the open of the very next candle after the engulfing candle closes. Do not wait for a pullback — engulfing patterns often run hard for the next 3 to 5 candles.
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss 5 to 10 points below the lowest point of the entire two-candle pattern on Nifty. For the option premium, exit if you lose 30 to 35 percent of the option price.
Target
Aim for the next major resistance level above. The minimum target is 2 times your stop loss distance. Book half the position at the first target and trail the stop loss on the rest.
Skip if
The engulfing forms in the middle of nowhere (no clear support nearby), volume on the green candle is below average, the green candle has a long upper wick (sellers were still active), or the broader market trend is strongly downward.
HARAMI FAMILY
BULLISH HARAMI
BULLISH REVERSAL
A small green body sits inside the body of a large red candle. The selling pressure is slowing down. Always wait for the next candle to confirm before taking the trade.
→ CALL (after confirm)
BEARISH HARAMI
BEARISH REVERSAL
A small red body sits inside the body of a large green candle. The buying pressure is slowing down. Always wait for the next candle to confirm before taking the trade.
→ PUT (after confirm)
BULLISH HARAMI CROSS
STRONG REVERSAL
A Doji candle sits inside the body of a large red candle. This is even stronger than a regular Bullish Harami because the Doji shows complete indecision after the big red candle.
→ BUY CALL
BEARISH HARAMI CROSS
STRONG REVERSAL
A Doji candle sits inside the body of a large green candle. Even stronger than a regular Bearish Harami because the Doji signals complete indecision after the big green candle.
→ BUY PUT
PIERCING / COVER FAMILY
PIERCING LINE
BULLISH REVERSAL
A green candle opens below the previous red candle's low, then closes above the midpoint of the red candle. A partial bullish recovery showing buyers are stepping in.
→ BUY CALL
DARK CLOUD COVER
BEARISH REVERSAL
A red candle opens above the previous green candle's high, then closes below the midpoint of the green candle. The mirror image of the Piercing Line.
→ BUY PUT
When to take this trade — Piercing Line at Support
Setup
A Piercing Line pattern has formed at a known support level. The green candle opens below the previous red candle's low (showing initial weakness), but recovers strongly to close above the midpoint of the red candle. Volume on the green candle is above average.
Entry
Buy a Call Option (At the Money or one strike Out of the Money) on the open of the next candle, but only if that next candle opens at or above the close of the green candle.
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss 5 to 10 points below the lowest point of the green candle. For the option premium, exit if you lose 30 to 40 percent.
Target
Aim for the next resistance level. Minimum target is 2 times your stop loss distance. Piercing Line is slightly less reliable than a full Bullish Engulfing, so consider booking full profit at 2 times risk rather than holding for more.
Skip if
The green candle does not close above the midpoint of the red candle (then it is not a real Piercing Line), volume is below average, or the next candle gaps down below the green candle's close.
TWEEZER FAMILY
TWEEZER BOTTOM
BULLISH REVERSAL
Two candles share the exact same low price. The support level was tested twice and held both times — a strong floor.
→ BUY CALL
TWEEZER TOP
BEARISH REVERSAL
Two candles share the exact same high price. The resistance level was tested twice and rejected both times — a strong ceiling.
→ BUY PUT
When to take this trade — Tweezer Top at Resistance
Setup
Two candles in a row have made nearly the exact same high price (within 5 points on Nifty). The level matches a known resistance (such as previous day high, a swing high from earlier, or a round number). Ideally the second candle is red and rejected the high more strongly.
Entry
Buy a Put Option (At the Money or one strike Out of the Money) on the open of the third candle, only if it opens at or below the second candle's close.
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss 5 to 10 points above the matching highs. If the third candle pushes above this level, the resistance has broken and your trade thesis is wrong.
Target
Aim for the nearest support level below. Minimum target is 2 times your stop loss distance. Tweezer reversals usually start a clean down move that lasts 3 to 5 candles.
Skip if
The two highs are not close enough (more than 10 points apart on Nifty), there is no clear resistance at this level, or the volume on both candles was very low.
NECK / GAP PATTERNS (TREND CONTINUATION)
ON-NECK PATTERN
BEARISH CONTINUATION
A small green candle closes exactly at the previous red candle's low. The buyers tried but failed. Sellers remain in control.
→ BUY PUT
IN-NECK PATTERN
BEARISH CONTINUATION
Like the On-Neck pattern, but the green candle closes slightly inside the red candle's body. The downtrend is still intact.
→ BUY PUT
THRUSTING PATTERN
BEARISH CONTINUATION
A green candle closes below the midpoint of the previous red candle — the recovery was not deep enough to reverse the trend. Downtrend continues.
→ BUY PUT
MATCHING LOW
BULLISH REVERSAL
Two consecutive red candles close at the same low price. Buyers are actively defending the level and refusing to let price drop further.
→ BUY CALL

BEGINNER PRIORITY — MASTER THESE FIRST

  • Bullish and Bearish Engulfing — The gold-standard two-candle reversals. The second candle must completely cover the body of the first AND close beyond it. Reliability is above 70 percent when this happens at major support or resistance.
  • Piercing Line and Dark Cloud Cover — The "partial engulfing" cousins. Slightly lower reliability than full engulfing patterns, but still strong when they appear at support or resistance with above-average volume.
  • Tweezer Top and Tweezer Bottom — Easy to spot (just two matching wicks) and excellent at confirmed support and resistance levels. Very common at the previous day's high or low.
The squint test: Picture closing your eyes and reopening them. Can you still clearly see the pattern on the chart? If you have to squint or force-fit the pattern, skip the trade. Clean, obvious two-candle patterns are the ones that actually make money.

THREE-CANDLE PATTERNS 14 PATTERNS

Why three-candle patterns are the most reliable: Every reversal has three phases — the old trend (candle 1) → indecision and transition (candle 2) → new trend confirmation (candle 3). All three candles must be present for the pattern to be valid. This structure filters out the most false signals, which is why classic trading research (by authors like Bulkowski and Nison) ranks these patterns the highest in reliability.

How to use these patterns: Wait for the third candle to fully close. Enter on the open of the fourth candle. For bullish patterns, place your stop loss below the lowest point of the second candle. For bearish patterns, place your stop loss above the highest point of the second candle. Set your target as either the next major support or resistance level, OR a minimum risk-to-reward ratio of 1 to 2 (your reward should be at least 2 times your risk).
STAR PATTERNS (THE MOST POWERFUL REVERSALS)
MORNING STAR
VERY STRONG REVERSAL
Big red candle, then a small "star" candle, then a big green candle. The classic bottom reversal pattern. Highly reliable when it appears at a support level.
→ BUY CALL
EVENING STAR
VERY STRONG REVERSAL
Big green candle, then a small "star" candle, then a big red candle. The classic top reversal pattern. Highly reliable when it appears at a resistance level.
→ BUY PUT
MORNING DOJI STAR
STRONGEST BULLISH SIGNAL
A Morning Star with a Doji as the middle candle. The Doji shows maximum indecision right before the bullish takeover, making the reversal even stronger.
→ STRONG BUY CALL
EVENING DOJI STAR
STRONGEST BEARISH SIGNAL
An Evening Star with a Doji as the middle candle. The Doji shows maximum indecision right before the bearish takeover.
→ STRONG BUY PUT
ABANDONED BABY (BULLISH)
EXTREMELY RARE
A Doji that gaps away from BOTH neighboring candles (a gap below it AND a gap above it). The rarest and strongest bullish reversal pattern. Very uncommon in Indian markets.
→ STRONG BUY CALL
ABANDONED BABY (BEARISH)
EXTREMELY RARE
A Doji that gaps away from BOTH neighboring candles at the top. The rarest and strongest bearish reversal pattern.
→ STRONG BUY PUT
When to take this trade — Morning Star at Support (textbook bullish reversal)
Setup
A clear Morning Star pattern has formed at a known support level on the 15-minute or hourly chart. The first candle is a large red one. The second candle has a small body that gaps below (or close to) the first candle's close. The third candle is a large green one that closes above the midpoint of the first red candle. Volume on the third candle is at least 1.5 times the average of the last 10 candles.
Entry
Buy a Call Option (At the Money or one strike Out of the Money) on the open of the fourth candle, only if it opens at or above the third candle's close.
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss 5 to 10 points below the lowest point of the second (star) candle on Nifty. For the option premium, exit if you lose 30 to 35 percent.
Target
Aim for the next resistance level above. Minimum target is 2 times your stop loss distance. Morning Star reversals usually trigger 5 to 10 candle moves, so book half at the first target and trail the stop loss on the rest.
Skip if
The third candle does not close above the midpoint of the first candle (then it is not a valid Morning Star), volume on the third candle is below average, or the broader market trend is strongly downward.
SOLDIER AND CROW PATTERNS (TREND IGNITION)
THREE WHITE SOLDIERS
STRONG UPTREND
Three green candles in a row, where each candle opens inside the previous candle's body and closes higher than the previous candle. A clear sign that an uptrend has started.
→ BUY CALL
THREE BLACK CROWS
STRONG DOWNTREND
Three red candles in a row, where each candle opens inside the previous candle's body and closes lower than the previous candle. A clear sign that a downtrend has started.
→ BUY PUT
ADVANCE BLOCK
BEARISH WARNING
Three green candles in a row, but each one has a smaller body than the previous one and a longer upper wick. The uptrend is running out of steam.
→ Get ready for PUT
DELIBERATION
BEARISH WARNING
Two strong green candles followed by a tiny third green with a wick. The uptrend is stalling and a reversal is likely soon.
→ Get ready for PUT
When to take this trade — Three White Soldiers (trend ignition)
Setup
Three consecutive green candles, each closing higher than the previous one, each opening inside the previous candle's body. The candles should have similar body sizes (no shrinking, no long upper wicks — that turns into the bearish "Advance Block" pattern). Volume should be steady or rising across all three candles.
Entry
Buy a Call Option (At the Money or one strike Out of the Money) on the open of the fourth candle. If the fourth candle opens lower than the third candle's close, wait one more candle to confirm momentum.
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss below the lowest point of the first soldier candle. This is the start of the new uptrend — if price falls below this, the entire setup has failed.
Target
Trend ignition patterns usually run for 5 to 15 candles. Aim for at least 3 times your stop loss distance. Book one-third at 1 times risk, one-third at 2 times risk, and trail the rest with a moving stop loss.
Skip if
The third candle has a long upper wick (this is a Deliberation or Advance Block warning), volume is shrinking instead of growing, the pattern formed against a strong daily downtrend, or the third candle closes right into a major resistance level.
INSIDE / OUTSIDE PATTERNS (REVERSALS WITH CONFIRMATION)
THREE INSIDE UP
CONFIRMED REVERSAL
A Bullish Harami (small green inside large red) followed by a third green candle that confirms the reversal. More reliable than a Harami pattern alone.
→ BUY CALL
THREE INSIDE DOWN
CONFIRMED REVERSAL
A Bearish Harami (small red inside large green) followed by a third red candle that confirms the reversal. More reliable than a Harami pattern alone.
→ BUY PUT
THREE OUTSIDE UP
VERY STRONG BULLISH
A Bullish Engulfing pattern followed by a third green candle that closes even higher. A high-conviction reversal that combines two confirmations.
→ STRONG BUY CALL
THREE OUTSIDE DOWN
VERY STRONG BEARISH
A Bearish Engulfing pattern followed by a third red candle that closes even lower. A high-conviction reversal combining two confirmations.
→ STRONG BUY PUT
When to take this trade — Three Outside Up (engulfing plus follow-through)
Setup
The first candle is red. The second candle is a green Bullish Engulfing candle that fully covers the body of the first one. The third candle is another green candle that closes higher than the second candle's close. The pattern appears at a clear support level. Volume on candles 2 and 3 is above average.
Entry
Buy a Call Option (At the Money or one strike Out of the Money) on the open of the fourth candle. Because this pattern is already very confirmed, you do not need extra waiting time.
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss 5 to 10 points below the lowest point of the first red candle.
Target
Aim for the next major resistance level. Minimum target is 2.5 times your stop loss distance because this is one of the highest-quality 3-candle patterns. Book half at the first target and trail the stop loss on the rest.
Skip if
The third candle has a long upper wick (sellers were active near the highs), volume is below average on the third candle, or the pattern formed during the lunch hour (12:30 PM to 1:30 PM IST).
RARE THREE-CANDLE PATTERNS
TRI-STAR BULLISH
VERY RARE
Three Doji candles in a row, with the middle one positioned lower than the others. A rare bullish reversal pattern.
→ BUY CALL
UNIQUE THREE RIVER
RARE REVERSAL
A big red candle, then a Hammer-like red candle that makes a new low, then a tiny green candle. A rare bottom reversal pattern.
→ BUY CALL

BEGINNER PRIORITY — MASTER THESE FIRST

  • Morning Star and Evening Star — The textbook reversal patterns. The middle "star" candle MUST be a small body or a Doji — that small candle IS the indecision moment that signals the reversal.
  • Three White Soldiers and Three Black Crows — Pure trend ignition. Three strong candles in a row in one direction means a new trend has started. The best pattern type for riding a continuation move.
  • Three Inside Up and Three Inside Down — A Harami plus a confirmation candle. The highest reliability of all three-candle patterns because it combines two separate confirmation signals.
Why these work best on 15-minute and higher timeframes: Three candles on a 5-minute chart form in just 15 minutes — often that is just market noise, not a real reversal. Three candles on a 15-minute chart form across 45 minutes of real market activity, which gives the pattern real weight. Trade these patterns mainly on the 15-minute and hourly timeframes.

MULTI-CANDLE PATTERNS 10 PATTERNS

What counts as a "multi-candle" pattern: A small set of rare, classic textbook patterns — most are 3 to 5 candle reversals (with a couple of 2-candle cousins included here because they belong to the same classical family). Because their structure is so specific, these patterns have the highest statistical reliability when they actually appear (the trading author Bulkowski rates several of them above 80 percent reliability at major support and resistance levels).

The downside for intraday traders: These patterns are rare on 5-minute and 15-minute charts. You will see them most often on the daily and swing timeframes. When you DO spot one intraday at a major level, increase your position size — these patterns deliver the highest risk-to-reward ratio of any pattern category.
RARE REVERSAL PATTERNS
THREE STARS IN THE SOUTH
BULLISH REVERSAL
Three red candles in a row, each one smaller than the previous one. The selling pressure is exhausting itself — a reversal is near.
→ BUY CALL
TWO CROWS
BEARISH REVERSAL
A green candle, then a small red candle that gaps up, then a bigger red candle that engulfs the small one. A bearish top signal.
→ BUY PUT
UPSIDE GAP TWO CROWS
BEARISH REVERSAL
A green candle, then two red candles that both gap up, with the second one engulfing the first. The sellers are overwhelming the buyers.
→ BUY PUT
STICK SANDWICH
BULLISH REVERSAL
Red, then Green, then Red — with both red candles closing at the same price. The support level has been confirmed as solid.
→ BUY CALL
HOMING PIGEON
BULLISH REVERSAL
A small red candle's body sits entirely inside a larger red candle's body. It is essentially a Bullish Harami pattern made of two red candles.
→ BUY CALL
CONCEALING BABY SWALLOW
RARE REVERSAL
Four red candles in a row, where the last one engulfs a wicked third candle. The selling pressure is completely exhausted.
→ BUY CALL
When to take this trade — Three Stars in the South (rare but powerful)
Setup
Three red candles in a row, each one progressively smaller than the previous. The pattern forms after a clear downtrend at a strong support level (such as a daily swing low or weekly support). Volume is shrinking on each successive candle (showing exhausted sellers).
Entry
Buy a Call Option (At the Money or one strike Out of the Money) only after the next candle (the fourth candle) closes green and above the high of the third (smallest) red candle.
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss 5 to 10 points below the low of the very first (largest) red candle. For the option premium, exit if you lose 30 to 40 percent.
Target
Aim for the next major resistance level above. Minimum target is 2.5 times your stop loss distance. Three Stars patterns often signal a 5 to 15 candle reversal, so book half at the first target and trail the stop loss on the rest.
Skip if
The candles are not progressively smaller (then it is not a valid pattern), volume is growing instead of shrinking, the pattern forms in the middle of nowhere with no clear support, or the broader daily trend is strongly downward.
EXTENDED REVERSAL PATTERNS (4 to 5 candles)
BULLISH BREAKAWAY
5-CANDLE REVERSAL
Four red candles stepping lower, then a big green reversal candle. A panic-selling bottom that exhausted sellers.
→ BUY CALL
BEARISH BREAKAWAY
5-CANDLE REVERSAL
Four green candles stepping higher, then a big red reversal candle. A euphoric top where buyers got exhausted.
→ BUY PUT
LADDER BOTTOM
5-CANDLE REVERSAL
Three red candles stepping down, then a fourth red candle with an upper wick (buyers starting to push back), then a big green candle. A rare bottom reversal.
→ BUY CALL
KICKING (BULLISH)
MOST POWERFUL
A Bearish Marubozu candle, then a gap up, then a Bullish Marubozu candle. A complete reversal of market sentiment. Very rare.
→ STRONG BUY CALL
KICKING (BEARISH)
MOST POWERFUL
A Bullish Marubozu candle, then a gap down, then a Bearish Marubozu candle. A complete reversal of market sentiment. Very rare.
→ STRONG BUY PUT
When to take this trade — Bullish Kicking Pattern (the most powerful reversal)
Setup
The first candle is a full Bearish Marubozu (a strong red candle with no wicks). The next candle gaps UP and is a full Bullish Marubozu (a strong green candle with no wicks). There is a clear visible gap between the two candles' bodies. Volume on the second candle is at least 2 times the recent average.
Entry
Buy a Call Option (At the Money or one strike Out of the Money) on the open of the second candle. This pattern is so powerful that you do not wait for confirmation — the gap and full Marubozu IS the confirmation. Use a market order if needed; the slippage is worth it.
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss below the low of the second (green) Marubozu candle. If price drops back to fill the gap, the entire reversal has failed.
Target
Aim for at least 3 times your stop loss distance. Kicking patterns usually trigger multi-day moves, so consider holding for 3 to 5 days if the pattern formed on the daily chart. Book one-third at 1 times risk, one-third at 2 times risk, and trail the rest.
Skip if
The gap closes within the first 30 minutes of the next session (failed kicking), the second candle has visible wicks (then it is not a true Marubozu), or volume on the second candle is below average (no real conviction behind the move).
MULTI-CANDLE EXHAUSTION AND WARNING
Patterns that play out over 3 to 5 candles. These take longer to form, which is exactly why they are more reliable — the market is showing its hand slowly. Excellent for swing setups on daily and 60-minute charts.
LADDER BOTTOM TOP (BULLISH)
5-CANDLE REVERSAL
Three bearish steps, then a fourth candle with an upper wick (showing buyers stepping in), then a fifth big green candle. The bottom has formed.
→ BUY CALL
DOJI STAR
WARNING SIGNAL
A Doji that gaps away from the previous candle. Signals exhaustion. The next candle decides the direction.
→ WAIT for next candle
SHOOTING STAR WITH GAP
STRONG BEARISH
A Shooting Star candle that gaps above the previous candle. An even stronger bearish reversal signal than a regular Shooting Star.
→ BUY PUT

CONTINUATION PATTERNS 12 PATTERNS

Continuation versus Reversal — the most important difference:
A reversal pattern says "the trend is about to change direction." A continuation pattern says "the trend is just taking a breath, then continuing in the same direction." Mistaking one for the other is the number-one cause of stop losses being hit.

How to tell them apart:
· Continuation patterns appear inside an existing trend (where higher highs and higher lows for an uptrend, or lower highs and lower lows for a downtrend, are still being made).
· Reversal patterns appear at the end of a trend (after an extended move, usually with fading volume).
· If you are unsure, check the higher timeframe chart. If the larger trend is still intact, treat the current pattern as a continuation.

Why these patterns matter for option buyers: Continuation patterns are where you ADD to a winning position or re-enter after the previous wave booked profit. They also signal "the trend has more energy left in it" — which produces the best risk-to-reward trades of the day.
BULLISH CONTINUATION PATTERNS
RISING THREE METHODS
BULLISH CONTINUATION
A big green candle, then 3 small red candles staying within the green candle's range, then another big green breakout candle. The classic Bull Flag pattern.
→ BUY CALL on 5th candle
MAT HOLD (BULLISH)
BULLISH CONTINUATION
Like the Rising Three Methods, but the second red candle gaps up. Very bullish — the trend will resume strongly.
→ BUY CALL
BULLISH TASUKI GAP
BULLISH CONTINUATION
Two green candles with a gap between them, then a red candle that fails to close that gap. This means the buyers are still in control.
→ BUY CALL
SIDE-BY-SIDE WHITE LINES (BULLISH)
BULLISH CONTINUATION
A green candle, then two more similar green candles side by side at the same price level. Brief consolidation, then the move continues higher.
→ BUY CALL
BULLISH SEPARATING LINES
BULLISH CONTINUATION
A red candle, then a green candle that opens at the SAME price as the red candle's open. The uptrend resumes with force.
→ BUY CALL
GAP UP (CONTINUATION)
BULLISH CONTINUATION
A gap up that happens during an existing uptrend signals acceleration. Do not try to fade (bet against) the gap — ride it instead.
→ BUY CALL
When to take this trade — Rising Three Methods (the textbook bull flag)
Setup
The pattern forms during an existing uptrend (visible higher highs and higher lows on the chart). The first big green candle has volume above average. The 3 small red pullback candles stay within the range of the first green candle (the deepest low does not break the green candle's low). Volume on the pullback candles is BELOW the average (showing healthy consolidation, not real selling).
Entry
Buy a Call Option (At the Money or one strike Out of the Money) when the fifth candle (a new big green) closes above the high of the first green candle, with volume at least 1.5 times the recent average.
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss below the lowest point of the 3-candle pullback. If price falls below this level, the pullback has turned into a real reversal and your trade is wrong.
Target
Use the height of the first green candle as your minimum target, projected from the breakout point. For example, if the first green candle was 80 points tall and the breakout happened at 23,500, your target is 23,580 (80 points up). Book half there and trail the stop on the rest.
Skip if
The pullback breaks below the first green candle's low (then it is a reversal, not a continuation), volume is rising on the red pullback candles (showing real selling pressure), or the pattern forms against a strong daily downtrend.
BEARISH CONTINUATION PATTERNS
FALLING THREE METHODS
BEARISH CONTINUATION
A big red candle, then 3 small green candles within its range, then another big red breakdown candle. The classic Bear Flag pattern.
→ BUY PUT on 5th candle
BEARISH TASUKI GAP
BEARISH CONTINUATION
Two red candles with a gap between them, then a green candle that fails to close that gap. The sellers are still in control.
→ BUY PUT
SIDE-BY-SIDE BLACK LINES
BEARISH CONTINUATION
A red candle, then two more similar red candles side by side at the same price level. The downtrend will resume.
→ BUY PUT
BEARISH SEPARATING LINES
BEARISH CONTINUATION
A green candle, then a red candle that opens at the SAME price as the green candle's open. The downtrend resumes with force.
→ BUY PUT
GAP DOWN (CONTINUATION)
BEARISH CONTINUATION
A gap down that happens during an existing downtrend signals acceleration. Do not try to catch the falling knife (do not buy a Call here).
→ BUY PUT
MAT HOLD (BEARISH)
BEARISH CONTINUATION
The bearish version of Mat Hold. Three small green candles fail to reverse the downtrend, then a big red candle resumes the move down.
→ BUY PUT

BEGINNER PRIORITY — MASTER THESE FIRST

  • Rising and Falling Three Methods — The textbook continuation pattern. Trend candle, then small counter-trend pullback (3 candles), then the trend continues. Ideal for options — enter on the breakout candle that exits the pullback range.
  • Flag and Pennant patterns — A mini-consolidation after a sharp move. The tighter the pullback, the stronger the continuation will be.
  • Separating Lines — A gap in the trend direction followed by a same-direction candle. Easy to identify and clean to trade.
Rule of thumb: The pullback inside a continuation pattern should NOT exceed 50 percent of the previous trending move. If it does, the pattern is broken — the trend is likely ending, not pausing.

EXOTIC & ADVANCED PATTERNS 10 PATTERNS

These patterns appear infrequently on intraday charts. When you spot them with volume confirmation at key levels, treat them as high-conviction signals. Always wait for the candle to fully close before entering a trade.
Why "exotic" does not mean "complicated": These patterns are rare because the specific sequence of candles needed to form them does not happen often — not because they are hard to read. Once you know the shape, you will spot them instantly. The real skill needed is patience: do not force-fit a pattern. If it does not match the template exactly, skip it.

Why exotic patterns have the highest reliability: The market rarely prints these by accident. When they DO form, they signal that a large institutional player has taken a clear side in the market. This is why their resolution rates (according to the trading author Bulkowski) often cross 75 to 85 percent.
GAP-DRIVEN REVERSALS (HIGHEST CONVICTION)
Why these are the "nuclear" reversal signals: A Kicker pattern requires a gap that moves AGAINST the previous candle's direction. Institutions do not create such gaps by accident. When you see a Kicker pattern at a major support or resistance level WITH volume, it is one of the highest-conviction signals in all of candlestick trading.
BULLISH KICKER
MOST POWERFUL BULLISH
A bearish candle, then a gap up, then a strong bullish candle. A complete reversal of market sentiment. Enter on the open of the second candle.
→ STRONG BUY CALL
BEARISH KICKER
MOST POWERFUL BEARISH
A bullish candle, then a gap down, then a strong bearish candle. A complete reversal of market sentiment. Violent move usually follows.
→ STRONG BUY PUT
MATCHING HIGH (BEAR TRAP)
BEARISH REVERSAL
Two green candles with the exact same high price. The resistance has been tested twice at the same level — this is a reversal warning.
→ BUY PUT
When to take this trade — Bullish Kicker at Support (highest conviction signal)
Setup
The first candle is a strong bearish candle (preferably with a long body and minimal wicks). The next candle gaps UP and is a strong bullish candle. There is a clear visible gap between the two candle bodies. The pattern forms at or near a known support level. Volume on the second candle is at least 2 times the recent average.
Entry
Buy a Call Option (At the Money or one strike Out of the Money) on the OPEN of the second candle. This is one of the few patterns where you do not wait for confirmation — the gap and reversal IS the confirmation. Use a market order; the slippage cost is worth it for this quality of setup.
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss at the low of the second (green) candle. If price drops back to fill the gap, the entire reversal has failed and your trade is wrong.
Target
Aim for at least 3 times your stop loss distance. Kicker patterns usually trigger multi-day moves. If the pattern formed on a daily chart, consider holding for 3 to 5 days. Book one-third at 1 times risk, one-third at 2 times risk, and trail the stop on the rest.
Skip if
The gap closes within the next 30 minutes (a failed Kicker), the second candle has long wicks (showing sellers were still active), volume is below average on the second candle, or the pattern is in the middle of nowhere with no clear support.
BREAKOUT AND BREAKDOWN MOMENTUM
The cleanest trend-starting candles. These are not subtle — just one large candle closing decisively through a key level with strong volume. Perfect for beginners because there is nothing to interpret: either price broke the level, or it did not.
BREAKOUT CANDLE
BULLISH BREAKOUT
A large green candle that closes above a key resistance level with strong volume. A strong Call Option entry signal.
→ BUY CALL
BREAKDOWN CANDLE
BEARISH BREAKDOWN
A large red candle that closes below a key support level with strong volume. A strong Put Option entry signal.
→ BUY PUT
COUNTERATTACK REVERSALS (SAME-CLOSE FIGHT-BACK)
The "fight-back" pattern. The second candle opens strongly against the first, but closes at exactly the same closing price as the first — like two armies meeting at the same frontline. This signals a transfer of momentum from one side to the other. More reliable than a simple Engulfing pattern when they appear at major support or resistance.
BULLISH COUNTERATTACK
BULLISH REVERSAL
A red candle, then a green candle that opens lower (gap down) but closes at the SAME closing price as the red candle. The buyers are fighting back hard.
→ BUY CALL
BEARISH COUNTERATTACK
BEARISH REVERSAL
A green candle, then a red candle that opens higher (gap up) but closes at the SAME closing price as the green candle. The sellers are fighting back hard.
→ BUY PUT

MORE CANDLESTICK PATTERNS 16 RARE PATTERNS

These patterns appear less often but are statistically very reliable (according to Thomas Bulkowski and Steve Nison’s research). When you spot them at a key support or resistance level with high volume, treat them as a high-conviction signal.
HIGH-RELIABILITY RARE PATTERNS
BULLISH THREE LINE STRIKE
VERY HIGH RELIABILITY
Three red candles in a row, followed by ONE massive green candle that covers (engulfs) all three. Bulkowski classifies this as one of the most reliable bullish reversals, with around an 84 percent success rate.
→ STRONG BUY Call Option
BEARISH THREE LINE STRIKE
VERY HIGH RELIABILITY
Three green candles in a row, followed by ONE massive red candle that covers all three. An extreme bearish reversal — a major top signal.
→ STRONG BUY Put Option
ISLAND REVERSAL (BOTTOM)
MAJOR REVERSAL
A gap down into a cluster of candles, then a gap up out of it. The "island" is isolated by two gaps moving in opposite directions. Rare but decisive bottom.
→ STRONG BUY Call Option
ISLAND REVERSAL (TOP)
MAJOR REVERSAL
A gap up into a cluster, then a gap down out of it. The island at the top = distribution → reversal. A violent move down follows.
→ STRONG BUY Put Option
TOWER BOTTOM
BOTTOM REVERSAL
A tall red candle → a cluster of small indecision candles → a tall green candle. The two "towers" flank a basing phase. A clear capitulation → accumulation → breakout sequence.
→ BUY Call Option
TOWER TOP
TOP REVERSAL
A tall green candle → a cluster of indecision candles → a tall red candle. Distribution is happening between the towers — smart money is selling to retail traders who are chasing the highs.
→ BUY Put Option
FRY-PAN BOTTOM
GRADUAL REVERSAL
A slow, rounded decline of small candles that gradually shift from red → doji → green. Unlike a sharp V-bottom, this is patient accumulation.
→ BUY Call Option on the breakout
DUMPLING TOP
GRADUAL REVERSAL
An inverted fry-pan. A slow rounded top with shrinking green candles → dojis → growing reds. A distribution pattern — slow but reliable top.
→ BUY Put Option on the breakdown
BULLISH MEETING LINES
REVERSAL (WEAK)
A big red, then a green that opens lower but closes at exactly the same level as the red’s close. Similar to a piercing pattern, but it only "meets", it does not pierce through.
→ Call Option with confirmation
BEARISH MEETING LINES
REVERSAL (WEAK)
A big green, then a red that opens higher but closes at exactly the same level as the green’s close. Weaker than a dark cloud cover.
→ Put Option with confirmation
IDENTICAL THREE CROWS
STRONG DOWNTREND
A stricter version of Three Black Crows — each red candle opens at exactly the prior candle’s close (no gap, no upper wick). Ruthless, mechanical selling.
→ BUY Put Option
Trap-variant patterns (Last Engulfing Top / Bottom, Nison’s traps, fake-outs) are taught in Patterns → Traps and Failures with full setups and stop-loss rules.
TWO-BAR REVERSALS — PIPE PATTERNS
Named by Thomas Bulkowski. Two nearly identical tall bars that stand out on the chart like a "pipe" sticking out of the surrounding price action. The highest historical reliability of any two-bar pattern: about a 77 percent reversal rate on weekly charts. Strongest on the weekly and daily timeframes, usable on the 60-minute timeframe.
PIPE BOTTOM
HIGH-RELIABILITY REVERSAL
Two adjacent tall candles (one red, one green) making nearly identical lows. The lows must stick out below the surrounding price — they look like the legs of a pipe.

Confirmation: The third candle closes above the higher of the two pipe highs. Ideally, the volume on the second bar is greater than the volume on the first bar.

Statistics (Bulkowski): 77 percent reversal follow-through on the weekly chart, about 65 percent on the daily. The average rally is 46 percent in bull markets.

Target: Project the pipe-height (the distance from the low to the highest pipe high) upwards from the breakout point.
→ BUY Call Option on the 3rd-candle close above the pipe high
PIPE TOP
HIGH-RELIABILITY REVERSAL
A mirror image — two adjacent tall candles with nearly identical highs that stick out above the surrounding candles. The twin spikes act as exhaustion markers.

Confirmation: The third candle closes below the lower of the two pipe lows.

Statistics: About a 75 percent reversal follow-through on the weekly chart. Used by swing traders as a major top-marker.

Target: The pipe-height projected downwards from the breakdown point.
→ BUY Put Option on the 3rd-candle close below the pipe low
VOLATILITY-CONTRACTION PATTERNS — SETUP FOR BREAKOUTS
These are not directional signals — they are compression markers. They tell you "a big move is coming", but not in which direction. Pair them with a directional trigger (a support / resistance break, or a trend) for a high-probability entry.
INSIDE BAR
CONSOLIDATION
What it is: A candle whose entire range (the high AND the low) sits inside the previous candle’s range. It signals a temporary pause — the market is digesting the previous move.

How to trade: Buy a break of the mother-bar high (Call Option) or buy a break of the mother-bar low (Put Option). The stop loss is the opposite side of the mother bar.

Best when: It appears at a support / resistance level, at a trendline, or after a strong impulse move. Multiple inside bars in a row (Inside Bar 2, Inside Bar 3) = extreme compression, with an explosive break ahead.
→ Trade the mother-bar break
NR4 (NARROW RANGE 4)
VOLATILITY CONTRACTION
What it is: A candle whose range (the high minus the low) is the narrowest of the last 4 bars. The term was coined by Toby Crabel and extensively studied by Linda Raschke.

Why it matters: Volatility is mean-reverting — periods of contraction are nearly always followed by periods of expansion. Narrow Range 4 = a "coiled spring" signal.

How to trade: Place a BUY-stop just above the Narrow Range 4 high, and a SELL-stop just below the Narrow Range 4 low (a one-cancels-the-other order pair). Whichever side breaks first decides the direction. Works on daily and 60-minute timeframes.
→ One-Cancels-the-Other stops on both sides of the Narrow Range 4 bar
NR7 (NARROW RANGE 7)
EXTREME CONTRACTION
What it is: Narrow Range 7 = the narrowest range of the LAST 7 bars. A stricter cousin of Narrow Range 4 — it is rarer, but when it triggers, the expansion is usually larger.

Statistics (Raschke): After a Narrow Range 7 bar, the next-day range expands beyond the prior average in about 70 percent of cases. The follow-through in the break direction is about 60 percent.

Inside Bar combined with Narrow Range 4 / Narrow Range 7 (Inside Day / Narrow Range 4, Inside Day / Narrow Range 7): A single candle that is BOTH an inside bar AND a Narrow Range 4 or 7 bar. The most powerful compression setup — trade the mother-bar break.
→ Wait and trade the break

USING COMPRESSION PATTERNS (INSIDE BAR / NARROW RANGE 4 / NARROW RANGE 7) IN INDIAN OPTIONS

  • Best time of day: 11:00 AM to 1:30 PM IST (the "dead zone") is where compression patterns form most often. Mark them during the lunch break, then trade the 2:00 to 3:00 PM expansion.
  • Best contracts: Nifty and Bank Nifty on 15-minute and 60-minute charts. Compression on the 5-minute chart is too noisy. Daily compression on Futures and Options stocks often precedes multi-day moves.
  • Risk management: Because the stop loss is well defined (the mother-bar low or high), you can size precisely using Calculator 1. Compression trades typically have a TIGHT stop loss — so you can afford more lots than usual within your risk percentage.
  • Avoid: A compression pattern that runs into a MAJOR event (the Union Budget, the Reserve Bank of India policy, or the US Federal Reserve). The break direction is then dictated by news, not by price structure — effectively a 50/50 coin flip. Stay flat.
When to take this trade — The Pipe Bottom Reversal at a major support level
Setup
Nifty has fallen 3 to 5 percent over the last 1 to 2 weeks. On the daily chart, the current candle and the previous candle have nearly identical lows (within 0.2 percent of each other), and these lows touch a major support zone (the previous swing low, or the 200-day Exponential Moving Average, or the Volume Profile Point of Control). The volume on the second candle is higher than on the first candle (a sign of buying absorption). The Relative Strength Index is below 35 (oversold).
Entry
Wait for the THIRD daily candle to close above the higher of the two pipe highs (the confirmation candle). Buy a slightly In The Money or At The Money Call Option of the current-month expiry on the next-day open. Use the spot price level as your reference (not the option premium).
Stop Loss
10 to 15 points below the lower of the two pipe lows on the spot index. On the option premium itself, set a hard stop at 35 percent loss. Use a Stop-Loss-Market order on the broker.
Target
Project the pipe-height (the distance from the pipe low to the pipe high) UPWARDS from the breakout point. Book 50 percent at the first target, then trail the rest with a stop at the previous swing low on the daily chart. Hold for 5 to 15 trading days.
Skip if
The two lows are NOT at a major support zone (then the pipe is just random consolidation), OR the volume on the second bar is lower than on the first (no absorption is happening), OR the India Volatility Index is above 25 (the Implied Volatility crush will hurt your option premium even if you are right on direction), OR a major event (the Reserve Bank of India policy, Union Budget) is scheduled within the next 5 trading days.

CHART PATTERNS 30 PATTERNS + FORMULA TABLE

What is a chart pattern? (And how is it different from a candlestick pattern?)

Both are pictures on the chart that hint at the next move — but they are very different in size and time:

· A candlestick pattern = 1 to 5 candles. It forms in MINUTES or hours. It tells you about IMMEDIATE buyer / seller behaviour.
· A chart pattern = 20 to 100+ candles. It forms over HOURS, DAYS, or even WEEKS. It tells you about a BIGGER shift in who is buying and selling.

Why chart patterns are useful for option buyers: A chart pattern gives you a "measured move target" — meaning, you can MEASURE the size of the pattern and project EXACTLY where price is likely to go. This is a HUGE advantage — you know your profit target BEFORE you even enter the trade.
How to read each pattern card below:
· The DRAWING shows the shape of the pattern.
· The DASHED line is usually the "neckline" (the level that price must break for the pattern to be confirmed).
· After the break is confirmed, you measure the height of the pattern and project it from the break point — that gives you the TARGET.
· Each card has an ACTION (BUY a Call Option / BUY a Put Option) and the exact trigger.

Quick term reminders: "CE" = Call Option. "PE" = Put Option. These are the Indian symbols you see on every option chain.

HOW TO TRADE ANY CHART PATTERN — 5 SIMPLE STEPS

  • STEP 1 · SPOT THE PATTERN — The pattern must look CLEAN and obvious. If you have to squint or force-fit the shape, it is NOT really there. Use the DAILY or 60-MINUTE charts — chart patterns do NOT work well on the 5-minute chart (too much random noise).
  • STEP 2 · DRAW THE BREAKOUT LINE — This is the line that price must CROSS for the pattern to confirm. It is called the "neckline" in Head and Shoulders / double tops, or the upper trend line in triangles. Draw this line CLEARLY before the break happens, not after.
  • STEP 3 · WAIT FOR A FULL CANDLE CLOSE BEYOND THE LINE — An intra-candle wick that pokes through is NOT a real breakout. Wait for a full candle to CLOSE on the other side of the line, on HIGHER than usual volume. No volume = it is probably a fake-out.
  • STEP 4 · MEASURE THE TARGET — Take the height of the pattern (from the highest top to the lowest bottom). Then project that same distance from the breakout point in the direction of the break. That is your Target 1.
  • STEP 5 · PLACE STOP LOSS JUST INSIDE THE PATTERN — Place your stop loss just INSIDE the pattern boundary (below the neckline for upside breakouts, above the neckline for downside breakouts). If price comes BACK inside the pattern, the breakout has failed — EXIT immediately, do not wait.
REVERSAL PATTERNS (END OF TREND)
HEAD & SHOULDERS
MAJOR TOP REVERSAL
Three peaks, middle highest. Volume falls on right shoulder. Break below neckline = reversal.
Target: head-to-neckline distance projected DOWN from neckline break.
→ BUY PE on neckline break
INVERSE HEAD & SHOULDERS
MAJOR BOTTOM REVERSAL
Three troughs, middle lowest. Volume surges on right shoulder. Break above neckline = reversal.
Target: head-to-neckline distance projected UP from neckline break.
→ BUY CE on neckline break
DOUBLE TOP (M)
BEARISH REVERSAL
Two equal highs separated by a pullback. Second peak fails = bulls exhausted. Breakdown below pullback low confirms.
Target: pattern height projected DOWN from neckline.
→ BUY PE on neckline break
DOUBLE BOTTOM (W)
BULLISH REVERSAL
Two equal lows with a bounce in between. Second low fails to break = bears exhausted. Breakout above bounce high confirms.
Target: pattern height projected UP from neckline.
→ BUY CE on neckline break
TRIPLE TOP
STRONG REVERSAL
Three failed attempts at same resistance. Very strong rejection signal. Break of support = high-conviction short.
Target: height × 1 projected down.
→ BUY PE
TRIPLE BOTTOM
STRONG REVERSAL
Three successful defenses of same support. Very strong buyer interest. Break of resistance = high-conviction long.
Target: height × 1 projected up.
→ BUY CE
ROUNDING BOTTOM (SAUCER)
SLOW REVERSAL
Gradual U-shaped transition from down to up over many sessions. Volume forms matching U shape. Patient but reliable.
Target: bowl depth projected up from breakout.
→ BUY CE on breakout
ROUNDING TOP
SLOW REVERSAL
Inverted U — gradual topping. Volume declines near peak, rises on breakdown. Often precedes extended decline.
Target: dome height projected down from breakdown.
→ BUY PE on breakdown
CUP & HANDLE
CONTINUATION REVERSAL
Saucer-shape + short consolidation (handle). Classic O'Neil setup. Handle should be <1/3 of cup depth.
Target: cup depth projected up from handle breakout.
→ BUY CE on handle break
INVERSE CUP & HANDLE
BEARISH CONTINUATION
Inverted cup + small upward handle. Sellers re-enter at top of handle.
Target: cup height projected down from handle breakdown.
→ BUY PE on handle break
RISING WEDGE
BEARISH REVERSAL
Converging up-sloping lines. Despite higher highs, momentum fades. Breakdown of lower trendline = reversal.
Target: wedge widest-part height projected down.
→ BUY PE
FALLING WEDGE
BULLISH REVERSAL
Converging down-sloping lines. Despite lower lows, downside momentum fades. Breakout of upper trendline = reversal.
Target: wedge widest-part height projected up.
→ BUY CE
DIAMOND TOP
RARE REVERSAL
Broadening then contracting range at tops. Rare but reliable. Combines megaphone + triangle.
Target: widest part projected down.
→ BUY PE on break
BROADENING TOP (MEGAPHONE)
CHAOS REVERSAL
Diverging highs and lows. Each swing larger than the last. Signals climactic top. Very volatile — wide SL required.
Target: last low × swing height.
→ BUY PE
DIAMOND BOTTOM
RARE REVERSAL
Mirror of Diamond Top at a downtrend bottom. Broadening then contracting range ends with a sharp upside break. Rare but highly reliable (~69% hit rate).
Target: widest part projected UP from breakout.
→ BUY CE on upside break
BROADENING BOTTOM
CHAOS REVERSAL
Diverging highs and lows at a downtrend bottom. Violent two-sided swings mark capitulation + aggressive accumulation. Break above last swing high = reversal confirmed.
Target: swing height projected UP from break.
→ BUY CE on upper-line break
CONTINUATION PATTERNS (DURING TREND)
BULL FLAG
BULL CONTINUATION
Sharp rally (pole) → slight down-sloping consolidation (flag) → break UP = trend resumes.
Target: pole length projected UP from flag breakout.
→ BUY CE on flag break
BEAR FLAG
BEAR CONTINUATION
Sharp decline (pole) → slight up-sloping consolidation (flag) → break DOWN = trend resumes.
Target: pole length projected DOWN from flag breakdown.
→ BUY PE on flag break
BULL PENNANT
BULL CONTINUATION
Sharp rally → converging triangle consolidation → breakout. Like flag but symmetrical.
Target: pole length projected UP.
→ BUY CE on break
BEAR PENNANT
BEAR CONTINUATION
Sharp decline → converging triangle → breakdown. Fast, reliable continuation.
Target: pole length projected DOWN.
→ BUY PE on break
ASCENDING TRIANGLE
BULLISH (USUALLY)
Flat upper resistance + rising lows. Buyers getting aggressive, sellers trapped at same level. Breakout up is the higher-probability outcome.
Target: triangle height projected up.
→ BUY CE on break
DESCENDING TRIANGLE
BEARISH (USUALLY)
Flat lower support + falling highs. Sellers getting aggressive, support held weakening. Breakdown down is the higher-probability outcome.
Target: triangle height projected down.
→ BUY PE on break
SYMMETRICAL TRIANGLE
NEUTRAL — WAIT
Converging highs and lows. No directional bias. Trade the breakout direction — do not anticipate.
Target: triangle height projected in break direction.
→ Wait for break
RECTANGLE (RANGE)
RANGE-BOUND
Horizontal S/R tested multiple times. Trade bounces at boundaries OR wait for breakout.
Target: range height projected in break direction.
→ Fade bounds or trade break
ASCENDING CHANNEL
UPTREND
Parallel up-sloping lines. Buy at lower boundary, sell at upper. Breakdown of lower line = trend reversal warning.
→ CE at lower boundary
DESCENDING CHANNEL
DOWNTREND
Parallel down-sloping lines. Sell at upper boundary, cover at lower. Breakout of upper line = reversal warning.
→ PE at upper boundary
POPULAR BONUS PATTERNS
Two extended patterns widely used by Indian equity swing traders: High-Tight Flag (O'Neil's most explosive bullish continuation — the pattern behind many multibaggers) and Dead Cat Bounce (the classic trap that fools buyers after a large decline).
HIGH-TIGHT FLAG (O'NEIL)
MOST EXPLOSIVE BULLISH CONTINUATION
What: Stock rallies ≥ 90–100% in 4–8 weeks (the "pole"), then consolidates tightly — correction < 25% — for 3–5 weeks (the "flag"). Break above flag high = resumption.

Why it's rare: Very few stocks rally 90%+ in 2 months. When they do, institutional accumulation is happening — operators are defending every dip.

Historical stats (O'Neil, Minervini): Pattern precedes many multibagger runs; in India — spotted on small/mid-cap breakout stocks. ~75% follow-through.

Target: Pole length + projected from flag breakout. Many runs exceed 2–3× pole length.
→ BUY CE on flag-high break with volume
DEAD CAT BOUNCE
BEAR TRAP — FADE THE RALLY
What: After a sudden sharp decline (> 15–20% in days), price bounces 30–50% of the drop. Bargain hunters pile in thinking "bottom is in" — only for price to roll over and make a new lower low.

Why it works: Shorts cover + retail buys the dip = short-term rally. But institutions are still distributing. Bounce dies at the 38–50% retrace of the original drop.

Warning signs:
· Bounce on declining volume
· Rally stops at prior support (now resistance)
· RSI stalls below 50

Target: New low below the initial drop's bottom. Typical: prior-drop low − 0.5× drop height.
→ FADE the bounce, BUY PE
PRICE-STRUCTURE NUANCES (ADVANCED)
These are pattern behaviours that most books skip — but Bulkowski, Kirkpatrick, and Fidelity research show they materially change the trade plan. Each one answers: "what if the pattern looks right but price is behaving oddly?"
RECTANGLE SHORTFALL — HIDDEN TREND INSIDE THE RANGE
BREAKDOWN BIAS
What it is: Inside a rectangle, price fails to reach the opposite boundary on each swing — each high is LOWER than the last (or each low is HIGHER). The range LOOKS intact but a trend is forming inside it.

Reading:
· Lower highs inside the box → sellers gaining, breakdown likely
· Higher lows inside the box → buyers gaining, breakout likely
· Shortfall pattern precedes the eventual break ~70% of the time (Bulkowski)

Action: Bias your entry in the direction of the shortfall. On an apparent bullish-sweep to the upper edge with lower highs, fade it — target lower boundary & the breakdown.
→ Fade the weaker side, trade the eventual break
EXPLOSION GAP PIVOT — RUNAWAY GAP AS SUPPORT
CONTINUATION
What it is: A breakaway or runaway gap that occurs mid-trend. The gap-low becomes a pivot level: as long as price stays above it, the trend is confirmed and accelerating.

Why it matters:
· Runaway gaps rarely get filled — holding them = institutional defence
· A held gap gives you the best trend-stop in any playbook: beneath the gap low
· Kirkpatrick: runaway gaps mark the 50% point of the total move on average — doubles the remaining distance from the gap

Action: BUY CE on any pullback that tests (but doesn't close below) the gap-low. SL just under the gap. Target = 2× distance from breakout-point to gap.
→ BUY CE on retest of gap-low
TARGET-PRICE FORMULA REFERENCE — MASTER TABLE
The measured-move projection is the #1 reason chart patterns beat candlesticks. You know where to book profits before the trade is on. This is every major pattern's target formula in one place — bookmark this table.

Formulas follow the Fidelity & Bulkowski standard (the same convention used in the CFA / CMT curriculum). Where the PDF rule differs from the extended "widest-part" rule (Rising/Falling Wedge), both are shown — PDF rule is labelled (PDF). Hit-rate statistics are from Bulkowski's Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (3rd ed.).

Important caveat for Indian F&O: Bulkowski's success-rate percentages are computed on US & global equity cash charts over decades. On Indian index options (Nifty/Sensex), theta decay, weekly-expiry gamma, IV crush and narrower lunchtime ranges can compress or expand these numbers. Treat the hit-rates as directional reference, not guaranteed probabilities. Always backtest on your own instrument + timeframe.
PATTERN BIAS HOW TO MEASURE HEIGHT TARGET FORMULA TYPICAL FOLLOW-THROUGH
Head & Shoulders Bear reversal Head-peak to neckline (vertical distance) Neckline − height (project DOWN from break point) 83% hit T1; avg 18–22% decline
Inverse Head & Shoulders Bull reversal Head-trough to neckline Neckline + height (project UP from break point) 74% hit T1; avg 38–45% rally
Double Top (M) Bear reversal Peak high to middle trough (neckline) Subtract high-to-trough height from the neckline breakout (PDF) 70% hit T1; avg 19% decline
Double Bottom (W) Bull reversal Trough low to middle peak (neckline) Add trough-to-peak height to the neckline breakout (PDF) 71% hit T1; avg 40% rally
Triple Top Bear reversal Highest peak − lowest trough (between peaks) Subtract height from the lowest trough (PDF) = neckline − height ~65% T1 hit rate
Triple Bottom Bull reversal Highest peak (between troughs) − lowest trough Add height to the highest peak (PDF) = neckline + height ~65% T1 hit rate
Ascending Triangle Bull continuation Widest part (base) vertical Flat top + height 77% hit T1; avg 35% rally
Descending Triangle Bear continuation Widest part vertical Flat bottom − height 64% hit T1; avg 17% decline
Symmetrical Triangle Direction of break Widest part at start of triangle Break point ± height 54% T1 hit rate (direction matters)
Bull Flag Bull continuation Pole length (start of rally to flag start) Flag break-up + pole length 67% hit T1; avg 23% rally
Bear Flag Bear continuation Pole length (start of decline to flag start) Flag break-down − pole length 68% hit T1; avg 16% decline
Bull / Bear Pennant Direction of prior pole Pole length Pennant break ± pole length Similar to flags (~65% T1)
Rectangle / Range Direction of break Rectangle top minus rectangle bottom Break point ± rectangle height ~70% T1 hit rate when volume confirms
Cup & Handle Bull continuation Cup depth (rim to lowest cup point) Handle breakout + cup depth 74% hit T1; avg 34% rally
Inverse Cup & Handle Bear continuation Cup height Handle breakdown − cup height ~63% T1 hit rate
Rising Wedge Bear reversal Mark the lowest trough inside the wedge pattern Target = lowest trough of the pattern (PDF rule) · conservative alt: break point − widest-height 60% T1 hit rate
Falling Wedge Bull reversal Mark the highest peak inside the wedge pattern Target = highest peak of the pattern (PDF rule) · conservative alt: break point + widest-height 68% T1 hit rate
Rounding Bottom (Saucer) Bull reversal Depth of bowl (rim to lowest point) Rim breakout + bowl depth 61% T1; avg 43% rally (long-term)
Rounding Top Bear reversal Dome height Breakdown − dome height ~55% T1 hit rate
Ascending / Descending Channel Reversal on break Channel width (perpendicular) Break point ± channel width ~60% after clean break
Diamond Top Bear reversal Widest part of diamond Breakdown − height 69% T1 hit rate
Broadening Top (Megaphone) Bear reversal Last swing low → last swing high Break point − swing height ~55% T1; wide SL required
Failed Breakout (Stop & Reverse) Opposite of original Original pattern height Opposite-break point ± 1.5× height Kirkpatrick: 68% follow-through, larger moves
Explosion Gap Pivot Direction of gap Distance from prior breakout to gap-low Gap point ± 2× distance (gap = 50% of total) ~60% of runaway gaps unfilled
Pipe Bottom / Top Reversal (both) Height of the taller of the two pipe bars (low-to-high of that bar) Taller-bar height added from taller-bar top (Bottom) or subtracted from taller-bar low (Top) — PDF rule ~77% reversal on weekly; 65% daily
Island Reversal Opposite of prior trend High-gap to low-gap distance of the island Second-gap side ± island height ~70% follow-through (rare pattern)
Diamond Bottom Bull reversal Widest part of diamond Upper-line break + height ~69% T1 hit rate
Broadening Bottom Bull reversal Last swing high minus last swing low Upper-line break + swing height ~55% T1; wide SL required
High-Tight Flag Bull continuation Pole length (≥ 90% rally in 4–8 weeks) Flag break + pole length (often 2–3× exceeded) ~75% follow-through (rare)
Dead Cat Bounce Bear continuation (trap) Original drop: pre-drop high to drop-low Prior drop-low − 0.5× drop height ~65%: secondary decline continues below prior low
Fibonacci Extension Trend direction Original impulse leg (low to high) Swing point ± (impulse × 1.272 / 1.618 / 2.618) 1.272 most common; 1.618 golden

HOW TO USE THIS TABLE

  • 1 · Identify the pattern — only proceed when structure is clean (daily or 60-min charts preferred).
  • 2 · Mark the breakout/break-down level precisely — this is the anchor for all measurements.
  • 3 · Measure the height as described in column 3 — use the widest vertical distance of the pattern.
  • 4 · Apply the formula — project the height from the break point in the break direction.
  • 5 · Set T1 = measured target, T2 = 1.5× measured target. Book 50% at T1 and trail the rest to T2.
  • 6 · Follow-through stats are from Bulkowski's Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (3rd ed.) — averages across US & global equities. Indian indices broadly match these numbers.
Critical caveat: A measured target is the MINIMUM follow-through that statistically happens. It is NOT the maximum — don't exit the full position at T1. Equally, a target being "on the chart" does NOT guarantee it will be hit — expected hit rates above range 50–85%. Always use a stop. Target = planning tool, not prediction.

BEGINNER PRIORITY — MASTER THESE CHART PATTERNS FIRST

  • Double Top (M) & Double Bottom (W) — the most frequent and most reliable reversal pattern on Indian index charts. Easy to spot, clean entry (neckline break), clear target (pattern height).
  • Rectangle / Range — most of the trading day is sideways. Knowing the range boundaries = knowing where to fade, where to buy, and where the breakout will come. The single most useful day-trading pattern.
  • Bull Flag / Bear Flag — the highest-R:R continuation pattern. Sharp trend → tight pullback → trend resumes. Perfect for adding to winners.
  • Ascending / Descending Triangle — directional triangles are more reliable than symmetrical ones. Ascending = bullish bias, Descending = bearish bias.
  • Head & Shoulders — the textbook major reversal. Takes longer to form but when confirmed, the follow-through is large. Best on daily charts for swing traders.
Common beginner mistake with chart patterns: jumping in before the breakout happens. "It looks like it's about to break!" is not a signal. Wait for the candle to close beyond the level with volume — trading pre-breakout hopes is the single biggest loser in chart-pattern trading. Patience pays — you may catch 10–15% less of the move, but your win rate doubles.
Combining chart patterns with candlesticks = A+ trades: A Double Bottom (chart pattern) that completes with a Bullish Engulfing (candlestick) on the neckline break, with volume expansion — this is the gold-standard setup. You will only see 2–4 of these per month on any given index, but they almost always pay out. Wait for them.
5 TYPES OF GAPS — NOT ALL GAPS ARE EQUAL
Gaps look identical on the chart but mean completely different things depending on WHERE they occur. Knowing the type tells you whether to fade it, follow it, or ignore it.
1 COMMON GAP
LOW SIGNAL
Where: Inside a sideways range, no trend context.
Fills: ~80%+ within 1–2 days.
Action: Usually a non-event. Fade with caution or wait for the fill and re-plan.
2 BREAKAWAY GAP
TRADE IT
Where: OUT of consolidation, breaking a well-defined S/R.
Fills: Rarely — the old S/R flips and holds.
Action: Strong directional signal. Enter on retest of the broken level + volume confirmation. Gap itself becomes new support.
3 RUNAWAY / MEASURING GAP
MIDDLE OF TREND
Where: Mid-trend, usually halfway to the final top/bottom.
Fills: Rarely during the trend.
Measuring rule: Project the distance from trend start → gap onto gap → target. Often gives a precise 2× move target.
4 EXHAUSTION GAP
REVERSAL WARNING
Where: After a long trend — last thrust, often on euphoria/panic news.
Fills: Usually YES, within days.
Action: Do NOT chase. Look for reversal candle the next 1–3 sessions. High-volume exhaustion gap + bearish engulfing = top signal.
5 ISLAND REVERSAL
RARE · POWERFUL
Where: Exhaustion gap UP + cluster of 1–5 candles + exhaustion gap DOWN (or mirror for bottoms).
Fills: Often yes, eventually — but the reversal is almost always sharp.
Action: One of the highest-conviction top/bottom signals in TA. Position aggressively with tight SL just above/below the island high/low.

GAP TRADING RULES (INDIA-SPECIFIC)

  • First 15-min after gap usually retests the gap edge — wait for it before entering.
  • Gap < 0.3% of index → treat as noise, often fills the same session.
  • Gap > 1% on news → breakaway candidate, don't fade blindly.
  • Monday gaps (after weekend) often fade by lunch as traders digest weekend news.
  • Check global cues (SGX Nifty, Dow futures) before classifying any gap.
  • VIX > 20 with gap → volatile fill likely, widen your SL.
GAP UP / GAP DOWN OPENING STRATEGY
GAP UP OPENING
STRATEGY
Small gap (less than 0.5 percent): Wait for the Opening Range Breakout, then trade in the breakout direction.

Large gap (greater than 0.5 percent): Wait for the gap-fill attempt. If price holds the Previous Day Close as support → BUY a Call Option. If price fills the gap and breaks the Previous Day Close → BUY a Put Option.
GAP DOWN OPENING
STRATEGY
Small gap (less than 0.5 percent): Likely to fill. Wait for Opening Range Breakout confirmation.

Large gap (greater than 0.5 percent): If the Previous Day Close acts as resistance on the bounce → BUY a Put Option. If the gap fills and price sustains → a potential Call Option setup.
When to take this trade — The Head and Shoulders Breakdown (the most reliable bearish chart pattern)
Setup
On the daily or 60-minute chart, Nifty has been in an uptrend, and now it has formed a clear Head and Shoulders pattern: a left shoulder (a peak), then a higher peak (the head), then a right shoulder (a peak that is roughly the same height as the left shoulder). The neckline (the horizontal line connecting the two valleys between the three peaks) is clearly drawn. Volume is shrinking from the left shoulder to the head to the right shoulder (a sign of weakening buying). The Relative Strength Index shows a bearish divergence (a lower high while price made the head’s higher high).
Entry
Wait for a daily / 60-minute candle to CLOSE below the neckline, with volume greater than 1.5 times the recent average. BUY one lot of an At The Money Put Option of the current-month expiry on the next-day open. If you missed the breakdown candle, wait for a pullback to the broken neckline (now resistance) and BUY at the rejection.
Stop Loss
Just above the right shoulder’s peak (5 to 10 points buffer above the wick). On the option premium itself, set a hard stop at 30 to 35 percent loss. Place a Stop-Loss-Market order on the broker.
Target
Measure the pattern height (from the top of the head down to the neckline). Project this distance DOWN from the neckline-break point — that is your Target 1 (book 50 percent here). Target 2 = 1.5 times the pattern height (book 30 percent). Trail the rest with the previous swing high. Hold for 5 to 20 trading days.
Skip if
The right shoulder is significantly higher than the left shoulder (the pattern is distorted, low edge), OR there is no volume confirmation on the neckline break (likely a fake-out), OR the pattern formed in less than 4 weeks (it is too small to be a structural top), OR the higher-timeframe weekly chart is still bullish (the daily pattern may be just a deep correction, not a true top).

TRAP & FAILURE PATTERNS 6 PATTERNS

What is a "trap"? A trap is when price BREAKS a level (looks like a real breakout) → retail traders rush in → and then price COMES BACK and traps them on the wrong side. The retail traders panic-sell, and that panic-selling fuels a big move in the OPPOSITE direction.

Why traps happen: The big players (operators) need a lot of buyers to enter at a certain price so that they can SELL into them. So they push price ABOVE a key level, lure retail buyers in, then crash the price. The retail traders are now "trapped" with losing positions.

How to confirm a trap: Look for a candle that CLOSES BACK INSIDE the broken range with high volume. That close-back is your signal that the breakout was fake.

Why these are gold-mine trades: When a trap is confirmed, FLIPPING YOUR DIRECTION is one of the highest reward-to-risk trades available to a retail trader — because all the trapped traders are forced to exit, fueling the move.
BULL TRAP (FALSE BREAKOUT)
BEARISH REVERSAL
Price breaks above resistance → Call Option buyers jump in → price falls back below the resistance within 1 to 2 candles. Those Call Option buyers are the "trapped" longs. The stop-loss hunt has been completed — a big move down follows.
To confirm: a candle closes back BELOW resistance with strong volume.
→ Flip to BUY PUT on the close-back
BEAR TRAP (FALSE BREAKDOWN)
BULLISH REVERSAL
Price breaks below support → Put Option buyers jump in → price rallies back above the support within 1 to 2 candles. Those Put Option buyers are the "trapped" shorts. A short squeeze follows — a violent up-move.
To confirm: a candle closes back ABOVE support with strong volume.
→ Flip to BUY CALL on the close-back
LIQUIDITY SWEEP / STOP HUNT
SMART MONEY SIGNAL
Price briefly spikes past a well-known swing high or swing low (where retail traders' stop losses are clustered), then reverses sharply. Big players fill their orders against the trapped retail traders. Look for a single-candle wick through the level, followed by a V-shape recovery.
→ Take a reverse-direction entry
FAILED BREAKOUT (THROWBACK)
REVERSAL SIGNAL
Genuine breakout happens, but price drifts back through the breakout level and closes inside the range. Differs from bull trap only in speed — slower but same bearish outcome.
Action: Stop following the breakout story. Flip bias.
→ FADE the breakout
FAKE BREAKDOWN
REVERSAL SIGNAL
Price breaks support on weak volume → drifts back above → strong up-candle closes above broken level. Bears who shorted the breakdown now cover.
Action: Flip bias after close-back confirms.
→ FADE the breakdown
RANGE EXPANSION TRAP
CHOP WARNING
Price repeatedly pokes just outside a range and then snaps back inside. Both Call Option and Put Option breakout traders get stopped out. Do NOT trade breakouts in this state — trade the range boundaries instead, until you see a full-candle close outside.
→ AVOID — chop mode

HOW TO IDENTIFY A TRAP (CHECKLIST)

  • Volume first: Genuine breakouts have expanding volume. Fake ones have declining or just average volume — suspect a trap.
