  • Speed: Trap reversals happen within 1 to 3 candles. If price does not hold the break within 3 candles on your signal timeframe, treat the breakout as failed.
  • Close versus wick: A wick above resistance that closes below it = trap. A body that closes above resistance and holds = a genuine breakout.
  • Context: Breakouts that go into round numbers, into option Open Interest walls, or into prior swing highs / lows are most likely to be liquidity grabs (traps).
  • Confirmation candle: Wait for the close-back candle to complete. Enter on its break to avoid being the next trapped trader.
WHY TRAPS HAPPEN — THE PSYCHOLOGY
The simple truth: Traps exist because large orders need liquidity. Institutions cannot buy or sell huge quantities without someone on the other side. That "someone" is the retail trader chasing the obvious breakout.

The anatomy of a trap — step by step:
STEP 1 · THE OBVIOUS LEVEL
Resistance or support gets tested 2–3 times. Every retail trader, every YouTuber, every WhatsApp group is now watching the same level. Stop-losses pile up just above resistance (for shorts) / just below support (for longs).
STEP 2 · THE BAIT
A small push breaks the level. The breakout is now "live" on every screen. Retail option buyers rush in with Call Options (or Put Options for a breakdown). The trailing stops of existing shorts get triggered, adding fuel to the move.
STEP 3 · THE REVERSAL
With no real buyers left above, price has no fuel. Institutional algos start fading the move. Price closes back inside the range — the "close-back" candle. This is the trap confirmation.
STEP 4 · THE UNWIND
Trapped retail traders see their Call Option / Put Option premium collapse. They exit at a loss. Their exit orders add more selling pressure, accelerating the reversal. The "real" move is now in the opposite direction — often 2 to 3 times bigger than the fake break was.
HOW TO PROFIT FROM TRAPS — FLIP THE BIAS
The trap trade is one of the highest risk-to-reward setups available to retail option buyers. Once you learn to spot the close-back, you can flip from being the trapped victim to being the trader who gets paid when retail panics out.

THE TRAP-FLIP ENTRY CHECKLIST (6 STEPS)

  • 1 · Identify an obvious level — Previous Day High or Low, a round number (24,000 / 24,500), the Volume Weighted Average Price line, the edge of the Central Pivot Range, or an option Open Interest wall.
  • 2 · Watch for the break — price pokes past the level and may even make a new high or new low. Volume is weak or only average.
  • 3 · Wait for the close-back candle — the candle MUST close back inside the range. A wick alone is not enough.
  • 4 · Confirm with a second candle — the next candle should NOT reclaim the broken level. If it does, skip the trade — it might be a pullback rather than a trap.
  • 5 · Enter in the opposite direction — Bull Trap → Buy a Put Option. Bear Trap → Buy a Call Option. Enter on the next candle's open after the close-back candle.
  • 6 · Stop Loss is tight — above the trap high (for a Put Option trade) or below the trap low (for a Call Option trade). If price goes back to test the break, you are wrong — exit immediately. The risk-to-reward is often 1 to 3 or even better.
When to take this trade — The Bull Trap fade at the Previous Day High (highest risk-to-reward in trap trading)
Setup
Nifty has rallied near the Previous Day High in the morning session. Volume has been shrinking on each push higher (a tell-tale sign of weak buying). Price pokes 10 to 30 points above the Previous Day High, but only with a wick.
Entry
Buy an At The Money Put Option ONLY when a 5-minute candle closes BACK BELOW the Previous Day High, AND the next candle does NOT reclaim Previous Day High (this confirms the trap). Volume on the close-back candle should be at least 1.5 times the recent average.
Stop Loss
10 points above the trap's wick high. On the option premium, set a hard stop at 30 percent loss. If price reclaims Previous Day High, you are wrong — exit immediately.
Target
The first target is the Volume Weighted Average Price line (book 50 percent there). The second target is the Previous Day Low or the Day Open. Trail the rest with a 20-point stop on Nifty.
Skip if
The break of Previous Day High happens with strong volume (more than 2 times the average) — that is most likely a real breakout, not a trap, OR it is between 12:00 PM and 1:30 PM (lunch hour fakeouts are mostly noise, not setups), OR it is the day before expiry (Theta makes Put Option buying very risky).
HOW NOT TO BE THE VICTIM — DEFENSE RULES

5 RULES TO AVOID GETTING TRAPPED

  • 1 · Never buy the wick break. If price pokes above resistance but the candle is still open, DO NOT enter. Wait for the candle to close above. 90 percent of retail losses come from buying the spike before the close.
  • 2 · Volume is non-negotiable. A breakout without expanding volume is suspect by default. No volume = no conviction = a likely trap.
  • 3 · Avoid the first 5 minutes. Opening-range fakeouts are the number 1 trap zone. Wait until 9:30 AM or later for the first clear break.
  • 4 · Expiry day traps are brutal. On expiry Tuesday or Thursday, the move near the Max Pain level is often a trap designed to expire option buyers worthless. See the EXPIRY DAY tab for details.
  • 5 · If you are already in a trade — respect the close-back. If your Call Option position is tested by a close-back below support within 1 to 2 candles of your entry, exit immediately. Don't "hope" for a recovery — hope is not a strategy.
Mental model: Think of traps as "the market paying you to not be greedy". The trader who chases the breakout loses. The trader who waits 2–3 candles and enters on confirmation makes money either way — either the breakout is real (and they catch the second leg safely) or it's a trap (and they flip and catch the reversal). Patience is the single highest-paid skill in option trading.
FALSE BREAKOUT vs FAILED BREAKOUT — THE CANONICAL DEFINITION
These two terms are used interchangeably in most Indian blogs — they are NOT the same. Kirkpatrick & Dahlquist (the academic standard) distinguish them precisely, and each carries a different trade plan. Learn the distinction once and you will never misread a breakout again.
FALSE BREAKOUT
QUICK FADE (1–5 BARS)
Definition: Price breaks the level, but returns back through the breakout price within a few bars — the move dies at birth.

Signature:
· Break & close back inside within 1–5 candles
· Volume on the break is weak or average
· Price stays within the prior range afterwards

Outcome: Range-bound — no fresh trend, just trap + fade.
→ FADE the break, target opposite range edge
FAILED BREAKOUT (KIRKPATRICK)
STOP & REVERSE
Definition: Breakout happens, fails, AND then price breaks the opposite side of the pattern. The structure fully inverts.

Signature:
· Break → close back inside → price travels across range → breaks opposite boundary
· Usually 5–20 bars from first break to second
· Volume expands on the opposite break

Outcome: HIGHEST-EV reversal in technical analysis. Kirkpatrick's data: ~68% follow-through, 2× the measured target of normal breakouts.
→ BIG trade: ride the inverted trend
SUCCESSFUL BREAKOUT (FOR COMPARISON)
HEALTHY CONTINUATION
Definition: Break with volume, brief return to test the level from the OTHER side, then trend continues.

Signature:
· Wide-range break candle with volume
· Price holds above/below the broken level
· Throwback (1–8 bars) touches level & bounces
· Breakout target reached within typical time window

Outcome: Textbook follow-through. Second entry on throwback is often safer than chasing the break.
→ Enter on throwback, not the break

DECISION TREE — WHICH OUTCOME IS IT?

  • Break happens — now wait & observe the next 3–5 candles. Do not enter yet.
  • Price closes back inside within 1–5 bars? → FALSE BREAKOUT. Fade it: buy opposite option, target the other range edge. SL beyond the trap high/low.
  • Price closes back inside, then breaks the OPPOSITE boundary within 20 bars? → FAILED BREAKOUT. This is the A+ trade. Enter on the opposite-side break with volume. Target = 1.5–2× the pattern height.
  • Price holds past the breakout level and throws back without closing inside? → SUCCESSFUL BREAKOUT. Enter on the throwback bounce, ride the trend.
  • Practical tip: On Indian index charts, false breakouts cluster at 09:15–09:30 (opening volatility) and 14:30–15:15 (closing hunt). Failed breakouts often crystallize after lunch (13:00–14:00) on low-conviction days. Time-of-day matters.
FAILED BREAKOUT — THE STOP-AND-REVERSE PLAYBOOK
STEP 1 · ENTRY
Enter on the candle that closes beyond the opposite boundary with volume > 1.3× 20-bar average. Do NOT anticipate — wait for the close.
STEP 2 · STOP
SL placed just beyond the failed-break extreme (the original false high/low). If price can reclaim that level, your reversal thesis is wrong — exit.
STEP 3 · TARGET
T1 = pattern height projected from the opposite-side break. T2 = 1.5× height (Kirkpatrick's average follow-through). Book 50% at T1, trail the rest.
Why failed breakouts pay so well: Two groups are caught offside simultaneously — the original breakout buyers AND the traders who faded the false break expecting range continuation. Both groups must exit in the same direction when the opposite boundary breaks. That forced flow is what powers the outsized move.

TECHNICAL ANALYSIS OPTIONS-TRADER EDITION

What is technical analysis (in simple words)? Technical analysis is just the study of CHARTS. You look at the price and the volume of past trades, and you use them to GUESS where price will go next. That is it.

It rests on 3 basic beliefs:
· Price knows everything — whatever the news, whatever the rumour, it is already reflected in today’s price.
· Prices move in trends — once Nifty starts going up, it tends to keep going up for some time.
· History repeats — because humans always feel the same emotions (greed, fear, hope), the chart patterns also repeat.

Important reminder: You are NOT predicting the future. You are simply estimating the CHANCE of the next move — and then deciding how much money to put on the trade.

Why technical analysis matters MORE for option buyers than for stock investors: If you buy a stock and the price moves UP a week later, you still make money. But if you buy an option and the price moves UP a week later, you might LOSE money — because time decay (Theta) ate the premium while you were waiting. So getting the TIMING right matters more than getting the direction right. Technical analysis helps you with that timing.
THE 4 PILLARS OF TECHNICAL ANALYSIS (KEEP THESE 4 IN MIND)
1 · PRICE ACTION
PRIMARY
What it is: The actual movement of price on the chart — candles, trend lines, swing highs and swing lows, and chart patterns.

What it answers: "Where is price going? And how FAST?" This is the single most important question for option buyers.
2 · VOLUME
CONFIRMS THE MOVE
What it is: The number of shares (or contracts) traded in a given period.

What it tells you: Is the move REAL or fake?
· Price UP + Volume UP = real trend.
· Price UP + Volume DOWN = suspect, often a fake-out.
Volume confirms or rejects every price signal.
3 · MOMENTUM (Speed of move)
SPEEDOMETER
What it is: Indicators that measure how FAST price is moving — like the Relative Strength Index (RSI), Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD), and Stochastics.

What it tells you: Is the trend still alive, getting tired, or about to flip? When momentum slows down BEFORE price does, that is the EARLIEST warning of a reversal. (This is called "divergence".)
4 · MARKET STRUCTURE
THE BIG PICTURE
What it is: The skeleton of the chart — support and resistance levels, the Central Pivot Range, and trend lines.

What it tells you: Is the market in an UPTREND (Higher Highs and Higher Lows) or DOWNTREND? A trade setup is only valid INSIDE the right structure. A bullish pattern in a clear downtrend usually fails.
TOP-DOWN TECHNICAL ANALYSIS WORKFLOW FOR OPTION BUYERS
Never trade a stock in isolation. The index sets the weather, the sector sets the wind, and the stock is the ship. If the index is trending up, fighting it with a Put Option is a low-probability trade no matter how good the stock chart looks.
STEP 1 · INDEX BIAS
Check Nifty and Bank Nifty on the daily and 1-hour charts. Are they above or below the 20-period Exponential Moving Average? Above the Central Pivot Range or below it? This is your directional filter. Trade WITH it, not against it.
STEP 2 · SECTOR ROTATION
Open the sectoral indices (Nifty IT, Nifty Bank, Nifty Auto, Nifty Fast-Moving Consumer Goods, Nifty Pharma). Which sectors are leading? Which are lagging? Trade the leaders long, the laggards short — never the opposite.
STEP 3 · STOCK SELECTION
Pick a liquid Futures & Options stock from inside the leading sector. Check its daily trend, the last 5-day high and low, and today's opening gap. Only trade setups aligned with the stock's own daily trend.
STEP 4 · SETUP CONFIRMATION
Look for at least 3 confluences: candle pattern + a key level + volume confirmation, or Open Interest / Relative Strength Index confirmation. Less than 3 confluences means it is not a trade. This filter alone removes 80 percent of bad trades.
STEP 5 · STRIKE SELECTION
Choose your strike based on the technical analysis context: In The Money for high-conviction swing trades, At The Money for intraday momentum trades, slightly Out Of The Money only for fast breakouts. Never deep Out Of The Money, unless you fully accept the lottery-ticket math.
STEP 6 · EXPIRY CHOICE
Match the expiry to your view's time horizon. Same-day move expected → use weekly. 3 to 5 day swing → use the next-week expiry. Multi-week trend → use monthly. Never buy an expiry that is shorter than your trade plan.
When to take this trade — Top-Down Confluence Setup (the highest hit-rate technical entry)
Setup
Nifty (the index) is trending up on the daily chart (price above 20 Exponential Moving Average AND above the Central Pivot Range top). The Nifty Bank sector is the day's leader (up more than 0.5 percent while Nifty is flat). Your chosen stock is trending up on the daily chart, has retraced to a previous resistance that became support, and now shows a bullish candle pattern (Hammer / Bullish Engulfing) with volume above 1.5 times the 20-period average.
Entry
Buy the At The Money Call Option of that stock, with the next-week expiry. Use a limit order at the mid-price.
Stop Loss
Just below the bullish candle's low (NOT a percentage of the option premium). On the premium itself, set a hard stop at 35 percent loss as a safety net.
Target
The first target is the next prior swing high (book 50 percent there). Trail the rest with a daily 20-period Exponential Moving Average stop. Aim for at least a 1 to 2 risk-to-reward.
Skip if
Nifty is trending DOWN on the daily chart (you are fighting the index), OR the stock's sector is the day's worst performer (sector is acting as a drag), OR you cannot find at least 3 confluences (candle + level + volume).
WHY TECHNICAL ANALYSIS IS CRITICAL FOR OPTION BUYERS (NOT OPTIONAL)
DIRECTIONAL EDGE
Options give you 5 to 10 times leverage on direction. Getting direction wrong half the time still leaves you profitable, IF your winners are 2 to 3 times the size of your losers. Technical analysis gives you that directional hit-rate.
TIMING EDGE
A stock can take 10 days to move where you expected. By then Theta decay has eaten your premium. Technical analysis narrows the entry window so you catch the first 60 percent of the move.
LEVEL-BASED RISK
Technical analysis defines where you are wrong — the price level that invalidates your thesis. Your stop loss is set from that level, not from a random 30 percent drop in the option premium.
STRIKE SELECTION
The distance to the nearest support / resistance tells you how far price is likely to travel. That, combined with Delta, tells you which strike gives you the best rupee payoff per rupee risked.
EXIT DISCIPLINE
Targets based on technical analysis (next support / resistance, prior day high / low, Central Pivot Range edges) are objective. Without them, profit-taking becomes an emotional coin-flip between "hold more" and "book now".
CONTEXT FOR IMPLIED VOLATILITY
Technical analysis tells you when a move is "about to happen" — which is exactly when Implied Volatility is low. Buying options when both price AND Implied Volatility are low is the highest expected-value setup in the book.
6 CORE TECHNICAL ANALYSIS TOOLS YOU MUST MASTER
1 · MULTI-TIMEFRAME TREND
Use the daily, 15-minute, and 5-minute charts together. The daily chart is for bias, the 15-minute for the setup, and the 5-minute for the entry trigger. Never trade if the 15-minute and the daily charts disagree.
2 · SUPPORT & RESISTANCE
Previous Day High / Low, swing points, the Central Pivot Range. All technical analysis entries must happen NEAR a level — mid-range setups are coin-flips.
3 · VOLUME CONFIRMATION
Breakouts need 1.5 times average volume or more. Breakdowns on rising volume are real. No volume = no trade, no matter what the chart looks like.
4 · MOMENTUM (RSI & MACD)
A Relative Strength Index reading between 40 and 60 is neutral. Above 70 is overbought, below 30 is oversold. Divergence is the gold signal — price higher but the Relative Strength Index lower means the trend is dying.
5 · CANDLESTICK AT A LEVEL
A Hammer or Bullish Engulfing at a key level is far more meaningful than the same candle in the middle of a range. Pattern + level + volume = the trifecta of a valid technical analysis trade.
6 · OPTION CHAIN / OPEN INTEREST
Maximum Open Interest strikes, Put-Call Ratio, Open Interest change, and the Max Pain level are taught in their own dedicated section → Futures & Options Playbook → Option Chain.

PRE-TRADE TECHNICAL ANALYSIS CHECKLIST (7 ITEMS)

  • Index direction — Is Nifty / Bank Nifty aligned with my trade direction?
  • Sector momentum — Is the stock's sector leading or lagging today?
  • Daily trend — Am I trading with the stock's daily higher-timeframe trend?
  • Key level nearby — Is my entry within 0.3 to 0.5 percent of a prior support / resistance, the Central Pivot Range, or a pivot point?
  • Candle confirmation — Has a closed candle signalled my direction at that level?
  • Volume — Is the breakout or rejection backed by above-average volume?
  • Option chain agreement — Is the Open Interest change supporting the same directional view?

Fewer than 5 of these 7 = skip the trade. Options are expensive; half-formed setups are how accounts bleed.

BEGINNER PRIORITY — LEARN IN THIS ORDER

  • Price action first — candles, swing structure, support and resistance. 70 percent of your edge lives here.
  • Volume second — add volume as a confirmer; it filters out 80 percent of failed breakouts.
  • One indicator third — pick ONE momentum tool (Relative Strength Index OR Moving Average Convergence Divergence). Resist the urge to stack 5 indicators — that is noise, not signal.
  • Option chain last — once your technical analysis is solid, overlay Open Interest, Put-Call Ratio, and Max Pain to add conviction — never as the primary signal.
Three technical analysis mistakes that wreck option buyers: (1) trading a setup that ignores the higher-timeframe trend, (2) stacking 5 indicators and rationalising any direction from them, (3) entering mid-range without a clear invalidation level. Fix these three and your hit-rate jumps significantly.
HOW TO COMBINE INDICATORS WITH CANDLES

INDICATOR STACKING FOR A+ ENTRIES

  • Minimum confirmations: Never enter on just ONE indicator. Require at least a candle pattern + 1 indicator + volume.
  • Do not stack duplicates: The Relative Strength Index, Stochastics, and Moving Average Convergence Divergence are ALL momentum tools — they will always agree with each other. Pick ONE momentum tool + ONE trend tool + the Volume Weighted Average Price line.
  • The A+ checklist: Candle pattern + at support/resistance + volume spike + Volume Weighted Average Price aligned + Exponential Moving Average aligned + Relative Strength Index not at an extreme. Hit 5 of 6 → high conviction.
  • Lagging versus leading: Price action and volume are leading indicators. Moving averages and Moving Average Convergence Divergence are lagging indicators. Use leading to enter, and lagging to confirm direction.
  • Beware curve-fitting: Adding a 7th indicator because your backtest failed is noise. Keep your setup to a maximum of 3 tools.

SUPPORT & RESISTANCE FOUNDATION

What is Support and Resistance?

Think of it like a ball bouncing inside a room:
· The FLOOR is the SUPPORT — the price level where the ball stops falling and bounces UP. Buyers are waiting at this level.
· The CEILING is the RESISTANCE — the price level where the ball stops rising and falls DOWN. Sellers are waiting at this level.

Why does this happen? Because traders REMEMBER price levels. If Nifty bounced from 24,000 last week, the moment Nifty comes back to 24,000 again, those traders rush to BUY again — thinking "it bounced last time, it will bounce again". Their buying actually CAUSES the bounce. This is called a self-fulfilling prophecy.

Why this is the FOUNDATION of all trading: Every other technical analysis tool — candlestick patterns, chart patterns, indicators — works MUCH better when used at a Support / Resistance level. A bullish candle in the middle of nowhere is just noise. A bullish candle AT a support level is a high-quality trade.
WHAT IS SUPPORT & RESISTANCE (in pictures)
SUPPORT LEVEL

A price level where buyers keep stepping in and pushing the price back UP. The more times the price bounces from this level, the stronger the support becomes.

RESISTANCE LEVEL

A price level where sellers keep stepping in and pushing the price back DOWN. The more times the price gets rejected at this level, the stronger the resistance becomes.

When to take this trade — Bounce from Support
Setup
Price has bounced from the same level at least 2 times before. The level shows up on a higher timeframe (daily or weekly chart). Today's price is approaching that level from above.
Entry
Wait for a green reversal candle (such as a Hammer, Bullish Engulfing, or Morning Star) to form right at the support level. Buy a Call Option at or near the spot price (At the Money or one strike Out of the Money) the moment that reversal candle closes.
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss 10 to 15 points below the support level on Nifty. For the option premium itself, set a hard stop at 30 to 40 percent loss on the option price.
Target
Aim for the next resistance level above. The minimum target should be at least 2 times your stop loss distance (this is called a 1 to 2 risk-to-reward ratio).
Skip if
The broader trend is strongly downward (do not catch a falling knife), volume is dead at the support level, or the bounce candle has a long upper wick (showing sellers are still active).
HOW TO IDENTIFY KEY LEVELS
SWING HIGHS & LOWS
Swing Highs (peaks on the chart) become Resistance levels. Swing Lows (valleys on the chart) become Support levels. Connect the peaks and troughs on your chart to find them.
ROUND NUMBERS
Numbers like Nifty 26,000 or 26,500, BankNifty 57,000 or 58,000, and Sensex 85,000 act as natural support and resistance because traders mentally focus on these levels. Always mark them on your chart.
PREVIOUS DAY HIGH AND LOW
The Previous Day High (PDH) and Previous Day Low (PDL) are the most important intraday levels. Mark these on your chart before the market opens every single day.
OPENING RANGE
The Opening Range is the high and low of the first 15-minute candle of the day. If price breaks above this range, buy a Call Option. If price breaks below, buy a Put Option. This is a high-probability intraday setup.
MOVING AVERAGES AS SUPPORT & RESISTANCE
The 20 period Exponential Moving Average acts as moving support during an uptrend. The 50 period Exponential Moving Average is even stronger support. When a candle reversal pattern forms right at one of these moving averages, that is a high-probability trade.
VOLUME PROFILE / POINT OF CONTROL
The Point of Control is the price level where the most volume traded during a session. It acts as strong support and resistance. A candle reversal pattern at the Point of Control is one of the highest-probability trade setups available.
When to take this trade — Previous Day High Breakout (intraday)
Setup
Yesterday's high is clearly marked on your chart. Today's market opened below yesterday's high. Price is now approaching yesterday's high from below with rising volume. Nifty is in an uptrend on the daily chart.
Entry
Buy a Call Option (At the Money or one strike Out of the Money) when a 15-minute candle closes above yesterday's high with volume at least 1.5 times the average of the last 20 candles.
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss just below yesterday's high (10 to 15 points back inside on Nifty). For the option premium, exit if you lose 30 to 35 percent of the option price.
Target
Aim for the next resistance above (often a round number like 23,500 or 24,000) or 1.5 times yesterday's range. Book half at the first target and trail the stop on the rest.
Skip if
The breakout happens during the lunch hour (12:30 PM to 1:30 PM IST), volume is below average, or the broader market index is moving in the opposite direction.
SUPPORT BECOMES RESISTANCE (ROLE REVERSAL)

When price breaks below a support level, that level flips its role and becomes resistance instead. The price often comes back up to test the broken level from below before falling again. This retest is a high-probability Put Option entry point. The same principle works in reverse: when price breaks above a resistance level, that level flips to become support, and a pullback to retest it is a high-probability Call Option entry.

When to take this trade — Role-Reversal Retest (very high success rate)
Setup
Price has clearly broken through a major support or resistance level on strong volume in the last few candles. The break candle had a body close past the level, not just a wick poke. Now price is slowly coming back to test the broken level from the new side.
Entry
For a broken support (now resistance), buy a Put Option when price touches the level and forms a red candle. For a broken resistance (now support), buy a Call Option when price touches the level and forms a green candle.
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss just on the wrong side of the level. For example, if support flipped to resistance at 23,500, your stop loss for the Put Option goes at 23,520 (above the level by 20 points).
Target
Aim for the next major support or resistance level. The retest entry usually gives you the best risk-to-reward ratio of any trade setup, often 1 to 3 or better.
Skip if
The retest takes more than 5 to 10 candles to happen (momentum is gone), the retest candle has a long wick on the wrong side, or volume is dead during the pullback.
FINDING THE BEST TIMEFRAME FOR SUPPORT & RESISTANCE
A key rule: Higher timeframe support and resistance is stronger than lower timeframe support and resistance. A level visible on the daily chart will hold better than a level visible only on the 5-minute chart. Always mark your levels top-down — start from the highest timeframe (weekly) and work your way down to the lowest (15-minute).
WEEKLY / MONTHLY CHART
LONGEST-TERM LEVELS
What to mark: All-time highs, 52-week highs and lows, major quarterly swing points, and psychological round numbers (26,000, 27,000, 50,000 and so on).

Why it matters: These levels are watched by big institutions and Foreign Institutional Investors. They rarely fail on the first test (more than 80 percent reaction rate). You only need to mark these once a month.
DAILY CHART
MASTER TIMEFRAME
What to mark: The last 10 to 15 swing highs and lows, the last month's high and low, the open price of the current month, and the most obvious horizontal levels where price has bounced or reversed at least 2 times.

Why it matters: This is the most important timeframe for intraday option buyers. Daily levels act like magnets for intraday price action. Mark these every night before the next trading day.
60-MINUTE (HOURLY) CHART
INTRADAY TREND
What to mark: The last 5 to 7 swing highs and lows of the past 5 trading days. Also mark Previous Day High, Previous Day Low, and Previous Day Close.

Why it matters: Connects daily levels to intraday action. Great for spotting the trend direction and where the day's range is likely to end.
15-MINUTE CHART
SIGNAL TIMEFRAME
What to mark: Today's Opening Range (the high and low of the first 15-minute candle), the Volume Weighted Average Price line, the 20 period Exponential Moving Average, and the day's developing high and low.

Why it matters: This is where candle reversal patterns form for your actual trade signal. A level on the 15-minute chart must line up with a level on a higher timeframe to be tradeable.
5-MINUTE AND BELOW
AVOID FOR DRAWING LEVELS
Do NOT draw support and resistance levels from these timeframes. 5-minute swings are mostly noise, with too many fake levels. They will confuse you and make every single candle look like a "reversal at support".

Correct use: Only use these timeframes to fine-tune your entry AFTER the 15-minute, 60-minute, and daily levels have already given you a signal.
CONFLUENCE = TOP-QUALITY SETUPS
GOAL
The magic number is 3: A price level that is a key support or resistance on 3 different timeframes (for example, weekly support and daily support and 60-minute swing low all at the same price) is almost unbreakable on the first test.

This stacking of levels is called confluence. Only trade options at confluence levels. The rest are noise.

THE TOP-DOWN WORKFLOW (DO THIS EVERY NIGHT — 10 MINUTES)

  • Step 1 — Weekly chart (1 minute): Zoom out. Mark 2 to 3 horizontal lines at major multi-month highs and lows. Use one colour (such as gold) for these.
  • Step 2 — Daily chart (4 minutes): Mark the last 10 swing highs and lows. Mark Previous Day High, Previous Day Low, and Previous Day Close. Mark the monthly opening price. Use a different colour (such as orange) for these.
  • Step 3 — 60-minute chart (3 minutes): Mark the last 5 swing highs and lows of the past week. If any of these match your daily marks, make the line thicker (this is confluence).
  • Step 4 — 15-minute chart (2 minutes): Tomorrow morning, wait for the 9:15 AM to 9:30 AM Opening Range candle to close. Add its high and low as today-only intraday levels.
  • Only take a trade when: Price approaches a level that shows up on 2 or more timeframes, you see a clear candle reversal pattern, and volume confirms the move. One timeframe alone is not enough — skip those setups.
COMMON MISTAKES WHEN DRAWING LEVELS
TOO MANY LINES ON THE CHART
More lines does NOT mean more accuracy. If every single candle is touching a "support level", you have drawn too many lines. The rule: If you cannot explain a line in one sentence, delete it. Target 4 to 6 lines per timeframe at the most.
OBSESSING OVER THE EXACT PRICE
Support and resistance is a zone, not a single pixel-perfect line. Draw a faint band of 10 to 20 points around the level for Nifty. The price can overshoot by 0.2 to 0.3 percent and the zone can still be respected.
USING ONLY ONE TIMEFRAME
Drawing levels on 5-minute chart only means trading noise. Drawing only on the daily chart means missing intraday precision. You need at least 2 timeframes marked at the same time.
IGNORING OLD LEVELS
A level from 3 months ago is STILL relevant. The market has memory. Do not erase a level just because price went past it. Instead, flip the level to the opposite role (broken support becomes resistance, and vice versa).

Pivot Points and the Central Pivot Range — India's most popular intraday tool — have their own dedicated tab.

BREAKOUTS THE OPTION BUYER'S BREAD & BUTTER

What is a breakout? A breakout is when the price firmly closes past a level it has been stuck below or above for a while. The level can be a horizontal line, a slanted trendline, the edge of a chart pattern, or a tight quiet range. To count as a real breakout, the move needs strong volume, Open Interest changes that match the direction, and the next candle should keep going the same way.

Why option buyers love breakouts: Options need fast, one-direction moves to make money before time decay (Theta) eats the premium. A slow back-and-forth market kills options that are slightly Out of the Money. A clean breakout can double or triple your option price in just one or two candles. But fake breakouts are the number-one reason option buyers lose money. This page exists to teach you how to tell the real ones from the fakes.
THE 4 TYPES OF BREAKOUT
1 · RANGE BREAKOUT
HORIZONTAL LEVEL
Price escapes a flat range it has been stuck in for several days. Common range edges include the previous day's high or low, the weekly high or low, and round numbers (like 23,500 on Nifty). This is the simplest and most reliable breakout type for beginners.
2 · PATTERN BREAKOUT
CHART PATTERN
Price exits a known shape on the chart. Common shapes are Triangle, Flag, Wedge, the neckline of a Head and Shoulders pattern, Double Top or Double Bottom, and Cup and Handle. The size of the pattern tells you roughly how big the next move should be.
3 · TRENDLINE BREAKOUT
SLOPING LINE
Price breaks through a slanted line that connects at least 3 touches on the chart. This usually signals that the existing trend is changing direction.
4 · VOLATILITY BREAKOUT
QUIET RANGE EXPLODES
The Bollinger Bands squeeze tight (price moves in a very small range), then suddenly explode outward. Quiet markets always come before big moves. This is the best type of breakout for option buyers because Implied Volatility is low at entry (so options are cheap) and high at exit (so options become expensive).
When to take this trade — Range Breakout (the easiest one)
Setup
Price has been moving sideways for at least 5 to 10 candles between a clear high and clear low. Volume is calm. The same level has been touched 3 or more times without breaking.
Entry
Buy when a candle closes above the high (for an upward breakout) or below the low (for a downward breakout). The close must be at least 0.2% past the level on Nifty. Volume on this candle should be 1.5 times higher than the average of the last 20 candles.
Stop Loss
Place your stop loss just inside the broken level. For example, if Nifty broke above 23,500, put your stop loss at 23,485 (about 15 points back inside the range).
Target
Use the height of the range as your target. If the range was 100 points wide (23,400 to 23,500), aim for 23,600 (100 points above the breakout). Book half your position there and trail the stop loss for the rest.
Skip if
Volume is below average on the breakout candle, the broader market index is moving in the opposite direction, or the breakout happens during the lunch hour (12:30 PM to 1:30 PM IST) when fake moves are most common.
5 SIGNS OF A REAL BREAKOUT (CONFIRMATION)
Any single sign on its own can be noise. You want at least 3 out of 5 signs to agree before taking the trade. If you have all 5, increase your position size.
1 · VOLUME SURGE
NON-NEGOTIABLE
The breakout candle's volume should be at least 1.5 times the average of the last 20 candles. No volume means no real interest from buyers or sellers. Skip every breakout that does not have this.
2 · DECISIVE CLOSE
CLOSE BEATS WICK
The candle must actually close past the level, not just poke through with the wick. The close should be at least 0.2 to 0.5 percent past the level for an index like Nifty, and 0.3 to 1 percent past for individual stocks.
3 · FOLLOW-THROUGH
NEXT CANDLE
The candle right after the breakout should stay on the new side of the level. If the very next candle pulls back inside the range, that is a warning sign that the breakout might be fake.
4 · INDEX AND SECTOR ALIGN
CONTEXT
When trading a stock breakout, check that Nifty and the stock's sector are also moving in the same direction. Stocks that break out alone, against the broader market, succeed less often.
5 · OPEN INTEREST CONFIRMS
F&O EVIDENCE
For an upward breakout, you want Put options to be adding Open Interest (sellers writing puts shows confidence in the move). For a downward breakout, you want Call options to be adding Open Interest. The Put-Call Ratio should also be moving in the same direction.
Detailed Open Interest, Put-Call Ratio, and Max Open Interest strikes are taught in Futures and Options Playbook → Option Chain. Fake breakouts and bull or bear traps are covered in Patterns → Traps and Failures.
3 BREAKOUT ENTRY STRATEGIES
A · AGGRESSIVE (BUY ON THE BREAK)
HIGH RISK / HIGH REWARD
Buy as soon as the candle closes past the level. You catch the full move when it works, but 40 to 50 percent of these breakouts fail and reverse. Only use this entry style when volume and Open Interest both confirm the move. Use a smaller position size because the failure rate is higher.
B · CONSERVATIVE (WAIT FOR RETEST)
BEST RISK TO REWARD
After the breakout candle, wait for price to come back and touch the broken level (now flipped from resistance to support, or support to resistance). Buy when you see a bounce candle from that level. The success rate goes up and the risk goes down, but you will miss about 20 percent of the fastest breakouts that never come back to retest.
C · HYBRID (SPLIT YOUR SIZE)
RECOMMENDED
Buy 50 percent of your planned position on the breakout candle, and the other 50 percent on the retest. This way you get a piece of every breakout, and a full position only on the ones that come back to retest. Most professional traders use this approach.
When to take this trade — Retest Entry (highest hit-rate)
Setup
A clean breakout has already happened with strong volume. The breakout candle closed firmly past the level. Now price is pulling back toward the level it broke through.
Entry
Buy when price touches the broken level and forms a bounce candle (a green candle for an upward breakout, or a red candle for a downward breakout). The bounce candle should ideally have a long body and a small wick on the side facing the level.
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss just past the bounce candle's low (for upward) or high (for downward). Usually 10 to 20 points away on Nifty. Tight stop because if the retest fails, the whole breakout was fake.
Target
Same as the original breakout target. The retest does not change the target; it just gives you a better entry price and a tighter stop. Aim for at least 2 times your stop loss distance.
Skip if
Price falls all the way back through the level (this is a failed breakout, now a bull trap or bear trap), the retest happens more than 5 to 10 candles later (momentum is gone), or volume is dead during the retest pullback.
When to take this trade — Volatility Breakout (best for options)
Setup
The Bollinger Bands have been squeezing tight for at least 6 to 10 candles (price is barely moving). Implied Volatility on the option chain is at the lowest reading of the last 5 trading days. Volume has been dropping (the calm before the storm).
Entry
Buy a slightly Out of the Money option (one or two strikes away from the current spot price) the moment price closes outside the upper or lower Bollinger Band with volume at least 2 times the recent average.
Stop Loss
If you bought a Call Option, exit if Nifty closes back inside the Bollinger Bands. For the option premium, set a hard stop at 30 to 40 percent loss of the option price.
Target
Aim for the option premium to double (a 100 percent gain). Volatility breakouts often produce 100 to 200 percent option moves in just 1 to 3 candles because both the price move AND the rise in Implied Volatility help your position.
Skip if
The squeeze is happening close to a major event (Reserve Bank of India meeting, Federal Reserve announcement, results day) because the breakout direction can flip after the news, or the squeeze happens during the lunch hour when most expansions are fake.
Strike selection, expiry choice, and option leg setup for breakout trades is covered in Futures and Options Playbook → Buying Rules. Stop loss and target placement is in Futures and Options Playbook → Stop Loss and Targets.

5-STEP BREAKOUT PLAYBOOK

  • 1 · IDENTIFY — Mark the level or pattern before price breaks it. No drawing lines after the move has already happened.
  • 2 · WAIT FOR COMPRESSION — Real breakouts come out of narrowing ranges, tight Bollinger Band squeezes, or a series of smaller-than-usual candles (Narrow Range 4 or Narrow Range 7 patterns).
  • 3 · CONFIRM — Check the 5 confirmation signs: volume 1.5 times average, decisive close past the level, follow-through on the next candle, broader market alignment, and Open Interest agreement. You need at least 3 out of 5.
  • 4 · ENTER — Use the hybrid approach: 50 percent of your position on the breakout candle, 50 percent on the retest. Or use the conservative retest-only entry if you want a higher success rate.
  • 5 · MANAGE — Place your stop loss just back inside the broken level. Move the stop to your entry price (breakeven) once price has moved 1 times your risk in your favor. Book half the position at 2 times your risk, and trail the stop on the rest.

BEGINNER PRIORITY — MASTER THESE FIRST

  • Previous Day High and Low breakout — The simplest, most reliable breakout. Works on almost every trading day.
  • Opening Range Breakout — A high-probability intraday setup using the high and low of the first 15 to 30 minutes. The full playbook is in the PICK STRATEGY tab.
  • Triangle and Flag breakouts — Classic chart patterns where price gives you a clear target measured from the pattern's height.
  • Avoid trendline breakouts for the first 3 months — They fail most often for beginners. You need experience to draw trendlines correctly without bias.
The breakout trader's paradox: The obvious breakouts — the ones where everyone on social media is shouting "BREAKOUT!" — fail more often than they succeed. Quiet breakouts that emerge from boring sideways ranges are the ones that win. If a breakout feels exciting and crowded, it is probably a trap.

RETRACEMENT & PULLBACKS HIGHEST-EV ENTRY IN THE BOOK

What is a retracement? A temporary counter-move within a trend that is already established. Price "takes a breath" by retracing back over a portion of the prior leg, and then it resumes moving in the original trend direction. A retracement is NOT a reversal — the trend structure stays intact.

Why this is the single best entry for option buyers: Breakouts enter at extreme prices (expensive premium, late timing). Pullbacks enter during the pause (cheap premium, early timing). A well-timed pullback entry in a trending instrument gives you the best risk-to-reward of any setup — often 1 to 3 or better. This tab teaches you how to time them.
RETRACEMENT vs REVERSAL — THE CRITICAL DISTINCTION
Mistaking a reversal for a retracement is the #1 way pullback traders blow up. Use these 5 tests to distinguish — if 3+ fail, it's no longer a pullback; it's a new trend forming.
RETRACEMENT (BUY THE DIP)
· The trend structure is intact (higher lows are still holding)
· The counter-move is shallower and faster than the impulse move
· The volume is lower on the pullback
· Momentum (the Relative Strength Index) stays above 40 in an uptrend (or below 60 in a downtrend)
· Price respects a prior support level or a Fibonacci level
REVERSAL (TREND IS OVER)
· The structure is broken (a lower low has formed, or a higher high has been lost)
· The counter-move equals or exceeds the impulse in both size and speed
· The volume is higher on the counter-move
· Momentum crosses the mid-line (the Relative Strength Index goes below 40 from an uptrend)
· Price breaks through the previous swing level
PULLBACK vs THROWBACK — THE POST-BREAKOUT RETURN MOVE
After a valid breakout, price very often returns to retest the broken level before continuing. This return is NOT a failed breakout — it is a second-chance entry. Kirkpatrick's research: ~50–60% of all breakouts produce one of these two return moves within 5–10 bars. Knowing which one you're looking at determines the option (CE vs PE) and the direction of the trade.
THROWBACK (AFTER UP-BREAKOUT)
BULL CONTINUATION
What it is: After price breaks above a resistance, it dips back down to test that same level (now support). The candle bounces off and trend resumes up.

Statistics (Kirkpatrick & Bulkowski):
· Occurs in ~55% of upside breakouts
· Happens within 30 days (usually 3–10 bars)
· Successful throwback → higher probability of reaching target
· But patterns WITH throwback average slightly smaller moves than those that run without — because some energy is consumed

When to buy CE: Wait for reversal candle (hammer / bullish engulfing / pin bar) at the broken resistance. Enter on the NEXT candle open.
→ BUY a Call Option at the retest bounce
PULLBACK (AFTER DOWN-BREAKOUT)
BEAR CONTINUATION
What it is: After price breaks below a support, it rallies back up to test that same level (now resistance). The candle rejects and trend resumes down.

Statistics (Kirkpatrick & Bulkowski):
· Occurs in ~60% of downside breakouts
· Happens within 30 days (usually 3–10 bars)
· Even more common than throwbacks — fear rallies fade faster
· Successful pullback → high probability of full measured decline
· Same energy-consumption effect applies

When to buy PE: Wait for rejection candle (shooting star / bearish engulfing / pin bar) at the broken support. Enter on the NEXT candle open.
→ BUY a Put Option at the retest rejection

REMEMBER THIS MNEMONIC

  • THROW-back → thrown UP — market threw price up past resistance, then it drops back to test. Direction of trend: UP.
  • PULL-back → pulled DOWN — market pulled price down past support, then it rallies up to test. Direction of trend: DOWN.
  • Both are RETESTS after a successful break — NOT reversals. The broken level MUST hold for the retest to qualify. If it doesn't hold, you're looking at a failed breakout (see TRAPS tab), not a pullback/throwback.
  • Key distinction from "retracement": A retracement is a pause WITHIN a trend. A pullback/throwback is the first dip or rally AFTER a valid pattern breakout. The concepts overlap but the trigger is different.
ENTRY RULES — PULLBACK / THROWBACK TRADE
RULE 1 · CONFIRM THE BREAK FIRST
The original break must be valid: closing candle beyond the level + volume > 1.3× 20-bar average. No break-confirmation = no pullback/throwback trade.
RULE 2 · WAIT FOR THE RETEST
Price must return to (within 0.3× ATR of) the broken level — not exceed it. A retest that closes back through = failed breakout, skip the trade.
RULE 3 · REQUIRE A REVERSAL CANDLE
Hammer, engulfing, or pin bar AT the broken level, in the direction of the original break. No candle = coin-flip. Wait.
RULE 4 · VOLUME PROFILE
Ideal: volume declines on the retest (weak counter-move) then expands on the reversal candle. Opposite volume pattern = suspect.
RULE 5 · TIME WINDOW
Retests that happen within 3–10 bars of the break are the most reliable. Beyond 15–20 bars, the original breakout thesis weakens — re-evaluate before trading.
RULE 6 · STOP & TARGET
SL: just beyond the retest extreme (opposite side of the broken level). Target: measured-move target from the ORIGINAL pattern, because energy lost in retest is offset by higher probability.
Why traders LOVE pullbacks & throwbacks: They solve the two biggest problems with breakout trading — late entry at expensive premium, and uncertainty about whether the break is real. By the time the retest prints, you already know the break worked (price held). And you enter deeper, at cheaper option premium, with a tight, structural stop at the retest low/high. It's the single most under-used entry by retail option buyers in India.
THREE PULLBACK ZONES — WHAT TO DO IN EACH
SHALLOW · 23–38%
AGGRESSIVE ENTRY
Signals very strong trend. Quick, shallow dips. Enter aggressively with smaller size; expect fast continuation. Ideal for momentum / flag-breakout setups.
MODERATE · 38–61.8%
OPTIMAL ENTRY
The sweet spot. Full-size entries, best risk-reward. Reversal candle at 50%–61.8% with volume = near-textbook high-EV pullback trade.
DEEP · > 78.6%
CAUTION
Trend in danger. Skip unless you have overwhelming confluence (key S/R + reversal candle + divergence). Reduce size. Quick exit plan essential.
CONFLUENCE — STACK MULTIPLE SIGNALS AT THE PULLBACK
A single Fibonacci level alone is a 50-50 bet. Stack 3+ signals at the same price zone and your hit-rate jumps above 70%.
FIB + PRIOR S/R
Fib 50% / 61.8% coincides with a previous resistance that became support. Highest-EV confluence — textbook continuation entry.
FIB + MOVING AVERAGE
Fib aligns with 20 / 50 EMA. Dynamic support confirms the Fib zone. Very common in trending equities.
FIB + TRENDLINE
Rising trend-line meets Fib retracement. Two independent supports converging — operators love these setups.
FIB + CPR / PIVOT
Fib coincides with CPR mid / pivot S1 / TC-BC level. See CPR tab for pivot-level nuances.
FIB + VOLUME POC
Fib lines up with a high-volume node (volume profile POC / value-area edge). Heavy prior trading = strong support.
FIB + ROUND NUMBER
Fib near a psychological level (NIFTY 22,000, RELIANCE ₹2,500). Round numbers anchor price; confluence amplifies.
PULLBACK RULE OF THIRDS
1st PULLBACK
HIGHEST EV
After the first strong trend leg. Most reliable entry of any pullback. Smallest SL, biggest remaining move.
2nd PULLBACK
GOOD
Still high probability. Slightly tighter stop; slightly smaller move left. Use confluence to confirm.
3rd+ PULLBACK
CAUTION
Trend maturity warning. Late-stage — likely exhaustion ahead. Reduce size or skip; next pullback may become a reversal.
Strike, expiry & option-leg setup for pullback trades is covered in F&O Playbook → Buying Rules. Stop-loss & targets in F&O Playbook → SL & Targets.

6-STEP PULLBACK PLAYBOOK

  • 1 · IDENTIFY THE TREND — daily + 1-hour must show higher highs / higher lows (or opposite for shorts).
  • 2 · MARK THE IMPULSE LEG — draw Fibonacci from the swing low to the latest swing high.
  • 3 · WATCH THE 38–61.8% ZONE — this is the primary entry band.
  • 4 · WAIT FOR REVERSAL CANDLE — hammer, bullish engulfing, or morning-star at the Fib level. Entry on next candle open.
  • 5 · CONFIRM VOLUME & STRUCTURE — volume on reversal, higher low holding, RSI still >40. 3 of 3 required.
  • 6 · MANAGE — SL below the pullback low. Trail to breakeven at 1:1. Partial at 1:2, ride the rest to prior swing high / Fib extension.

BEGINNER PRIORITY — MASTER THESE FIRST

  • First pullback after a fresh breakout — simplest, highest probability, textbook setup.
  • 20 EMA pullback in a clean trend — beginners can spot it with one indicator; works on most liquid stocks.
  • 50%–61.8% Fib in trend direction — the golden-zone pullback; scale into it with a reversal candle.
  • Avoid the 78.6% zone for the first 3 months — too close to reversal territory; requires experience to trade safely.
The single biggest pullback-trader mistake: entering without a reversal candle at the level. Buying just because price "reached Fib 50%" is a coin-flip — wait for the market to confirm the level is holding (a hammer, engulfing, or morning star printing AT the zone). Patience here separates profitable pullback traders from everyone else.
FIBONACCI RETRACEMENT & EXTENSION — FULL PLAYBOOK
Fibonacci levels are where retail traders, algos, and institutions all watch for bounces. They're self-fulfilling — so many eyes on 61.8% that it often reacts just because everyone expects it to.
FIBONACCI RETRACEMENT — KEY LEVELS
PULLBACK ENTRY LEVELS
The 6 key levels:
• 23.6% → shallow pullback (strong trends)
• 38.2% → normal pullback
• 50% KEY → psychological midpoint
• 61.8% GOLDEN RATIO → THE most-watched level
• 78.6% → deep pullback, last chance
• >100% → retracement failed, trend over
HOW TO DRAW FIB CORRECTLY
In UPTREND (looking for CE entry):
Draw from swing LOW to swing HIGH of the impulse move. Retracements fall BETWEEN the extremes — buy on bounce from 50–61.8%.

In DOWNTREND (looking for PE entry):
Draw from swing HIGH to swing LOW. Sell on rejection at 50–61.8% bounce.

Timeframe to draw on: Match your trading TF — 15-min Fib for intraday, daily Fib for swing.
THE GOLDEN ZONE (50%–61.8%)
A+ ENTRY ZONE
The 50–61.8% zone is where 70%+ of healthy retracements reverse. If a candle pattern (hammer, engulfing, morning star) forms inside this zone AT a prior S/R level = highest-probability trade in the book.
FIBONACCI EXTENSION (TARGETS)
PROFIT TARGET LEVELS
Used to project how far price will move after a successful retracement bounce.
• 1.272 / 1.414 → conservative T1
• 1.618 KEY → primary target (most common reaction point)
• 2.618 → extended move, for runner positions

Rule: Book 50% at 1.272–1.414, trail rest to 1.618.
FIB + S/R CONFLUENCE = GOLD
The magic combo: When a Fibonacci level (especially 61.8%) lines up with a pre-existing horizontal S/R level OR a moving average → treat this as confluence. Statistically, confluence zones react ~80% of the time.

Example: 15-min Fib 61.8% retracement = 26,080. Daily support = 26,075. 50 EMA = 26,082. → Strong CE entry zone.
FIB MISTAKES TO AVOID
• Drawing too many Fibs — use only the last major swing, not every wiggle
• Trading Fib level alone — always require candle confirmation
• Ignoring trend direction — only trade Fib WITH higher-TF trend
• Obsessing over exact price — treat levels as ±0.1% zones
• Using sub-5-min Fib — noise-level, meaningless
HOW TO DRAW A FIBONACCI RETRACEMENT — STEP BY STEP
The retracement tool answers: "after a strong move, where is price likely to pause and reverse?" Drawing it correctly is 80% of the work — wrong anchors = wrong levels = wrong trades.
THE 5 STEPS
STEP 1 — identify the trend direction
Look at the higher timeframe (1-hour or daily). Is price in an uptrend, downtrend, or sideways? Never draw a Fib in a sideways market.

STEP 2 — find the IMPULSE leg
Pick the latest clean, strong, one-directional move — multiple green candles with volume (uptrend) or multiple red candles (downtrend). Avoid choppy swings.

STEP 3 — select the Fibonacci Retracement tool
On your broker chart, select the Fib Retracement tool (keyboard shortcut on TradingView / Upstox: Alt + F).

STEP 4 — click your two anchor points
• UPTREND: click at the swing LOW first, then drag to the swing HIGH.
• DOWNTREND: click at the swing HIGH first, then drag to the swing LOW.

STEP 5 — read the retracement levels
The tool auto-plots horizontal lines at 23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8%, 78.6%. Price will pull back into these. Focus on the golden zone: 50–61.8%.
WORKED EXAMPLE — NIFTY UPTREND
REAL NUMBERS, HAND-CALCULATED
Impulse leg (uptrend):
Swing LOW = 23,800 · Swing HIGH = 24,300
⇒ Impulse range = 500 pts

Retracement formula (uptrend):
Level = HIGH − (range × X%)

Compute each level:
• 23.6% → 24,300 − (500 × 0.236) = 24,182
• 38.2% → 24,300 − (500 × 0.382) = 24,109
• 50.0% → 24,300 − (500 × 0.500) = 24,050
• 61.8% → 24,300 − (500 × 0.618) = 23,991
• 78.6% → 24,300 − (500 × 0.786) = 23,907

GOLDEN ZONE = 23,991 – 24,050
Trade logic: if price pulls back into 23,991–24,050 AND prints a bullish candle (hammer / engulfing) AND volume spikes → high-probability CE entry. For a downtrend, flip all signs: swing HIGH is 0%, swing LOW is 100%, and you are looking to short a rally into the golden zone with a bearish candle.
HOW TO DRAW A FIBONACCI EXTENSION — PROJECTING YOUR TARGET
The extension tool answers: "if the trend continues after the pullback, where is the next profit target?" Extensions project levels beyond the impulse high (uptrend) or low (downtrend).
THE 4 STEPS (2-POINT METHOD — EASIEST)
STEP 1 — draw the Fib retracement first
Use the same anchors (swing LOW → swing HIGH for uptrend). Most Fib tools show extension levels automatically once retracement is drawn.

STEP 2 — enable extension levels
In the Fib tool settings, tick the boxes for 1.272, 1.414, 1.618, and 2.618. These auto-plot above the swing high (uptrend).

STEP 3 — read the target ladder
• 1.272 / 1.414 → first profit target (book 50% here)
• 1.618 (golden target) → primary profit target
• 2.618 → stretch target for runners

STEP 4 — confirm target with context
Always check if the extension level aligns with a prior horizontal S/R, pivot, or round number. Alignment = confluence → highest-probability reaction point.
WORKED EXAMPLE — NIFTY TARGET LADDER
FROM THE SAME 500-PT IMPULSE
Same impulse as before:
Swing LOW = 23,800 · Swing HIGH = 24,300 · Range = 500 pts

Extension formula (uptrend):
Target = LOW + (range × X)

Compute each target:
• 1.272 → 23,800 + (500 × 1.272) = 24,436
• 1.414 → 23,800 + (500 × 1.414) = 24,507
• 1.618 (golden target) → 23,800 + (500 × 1.618) = 24,609
• 2.618 → 23,800 + (500 × 2.618) = 25,109

YOUR PROFIT LADDER: T1 = 24,436 · T2 = 24,609 · T3 = 25,109

Execution plan (after a valid golden-zone entry near 24,000):
• Book 50% at 1.272 = 24,436
• Book 30% at 1.618 = 24,609
• Trail remaining 20% with a moving average; exit on trend break or at 2.618 = 25,109.
The 3-point method is more accurate because it uses the actual retracement low instead of assuming one. Use it once a clean pullback has confirmed in the golden zone (50–61.8%).
3-POINT METHOD (TREND-BASED FIB EXTENSION)
When to use: after a clear retracement has already happened. This is the more accurate method because it uses the actual completed pullback as an anchor, instead of assuming where one will end.

The 3 anchors (uptrend):
• Point A = swing LOW (start of impulse)
• Point B = swing HIGH (end of impulse)
• Point C = pullback LOW (after retracement, ideally in the 50–61.8% zone)

What it measures: the projected continuation move from C, scaled to the original A→B impulse. Ratios (1.272, 1.618, 2.618) are calculated from C, not from A.

In TradingView / Upstox: select the "Trend-Based Fib Extension" tool. Click 3 times in sequence (A → B → C). Levels auto-plot above C.

For downtrend: A = swing HIGH, B = swing LOW, C = pullback HIGH. Levels project below C.
WORKED EXAMPLE — 3-POINT EXTENSION (NIFTY)
CONTINUATION TARGETS FROM PULLBACK
Setup (uptrend):
• A = LOW 23,800
• B = HIGH 24,300
• C = pullback LOW 24,000 (clean 60% retracement — golden zone)

Impulse range (A→B): 500 pts

Extension formula (3-point, uptrend):
Target = C + (range × X)

Compute targets from C:
• 1.000 → 24,000 + (500 × 1.000) = 24,500
• 1.272 → 24,000 + (500 × 1.272) = 24,636
• 1.618 (golden) → 24,000 + (500 × 1.618) = 24,809
• 2.618 → 24,000 + (500 × 2.618) = 25,309

2-point vs 3-point compared: 2-point gave 24,436 / 24,609 / 25,109. 3-point gives 24,636 / 24,809 / 25,309 (~200 pts higher because the pullback is "given back"). Use 3-point only AFTER a confirmed reversal candle in the retracement zone.
FIBONACCI EXTENSION — KEY CONCEPTS YOU MUST KNOW
Drawing the tool is mechanical — understanding which level matters in which context is the actual edge. These cards cover everything else you need to know about extensions.
EACH EXTENSION LEVEL EXPLAINED
1.000: the original swing high/low. Re-test target after a deep retracement.

1.272: √1.618. First profit target — book 30–50% here. Often coincides with prior resistance / round numbers.

1.414: √2. Conservative T1 used by some traders. Same role as 1.272.

1.618 (golden target): THE most-watched extension. Phi (φ) — the golden ratio. ~60%+ of strong continuation moves stop at or just past this level. Primary book-profit zone.

2.000: exactly 2× the impulse. Round-number magnet for psychological reasons.

2.618: φ-squared. Stretch target for strong trend days — trail the last 20% of position here.

3.618 / 4.236: "blow-off" levels. Only relevant on rare parabolic moves. Most option buyers will never touch these.
WHY 1.618 IS THE GOLDEN TARGET
THE GOLDEN RATIO TARGET
Phi (φ = 1.618) is hard-wired into nature, art, architecture — and into market psychology. Algos, retail, and institutions all watch this level. Result: massive resting orders cluster around 1.618 ⇒ price reacts there with statistical significance.

Practical rule: set your primary book-profit zone at 1.618. If price stalls there with a reversal candle → close the trade. Don't get greedy waiting for 2.618.
EXTENSION + CONFLUENCE = HIGH-PROBABILITY TARGET
A single Fib level is suggestive. Fib + 1 other system = strong. Fib + 2 other systems = jackpot.

Confluence sources to overlay on extensions:
• Prior swing high / swing low (horizontal S/R)
• Round numbers (24,000 / 24,500 / 25,000)
• CPR pivot R1, R2, S1, S2
• Daily / weekly classical pivots
• 50 / 200 EMA on higher timeframe
• VWAP (especially weekly VWAP for swing targets)

Example: 1.618 extension = 24,605. Daily R1 = 24,610. Round number = 24,600. Three-way confluence → very high probability of reaction. Book aggressively.
RETRACEMENT vs EXTENSION vs PROJECTION
Beginners confuse these three. Quick reference:

RETRACEMENT (entry tool): drawn between two points; levels fall between them. Answers "where will price pause and reverse?"

EXTENSION (target tool): drawn between two or three points; levels project beyond them. Answers "how far will price move after the pullback?"

PROJECTION: a 3-point variant projecting a similar-sized leg forward. In TradingView this is the "Trend-Based Fib Extension" tool. Effectively the same thing for option-buyer use.

Rule of thumb: use retracement to ENTER, use extension to EXIT. Together they form a complete trade plan from entry to target.
WHEN NOT TO USE EXTENSIONS
• Sideways / range market — no clean impulse to anchor to
• After a fake / failed breakout — the impulse was a trap, not a real move
• Sub-5-min charts — price noise dominates the projection
• Against higher-TF trend — counter-trend extensions rarely complete
• Low-volatility days (ATR contracted) — price won't have fuel to reach 1.618
EXTENSION MISTAKES TO AVOID
• Targeting only 2.618 — greedy; miss the safer 1.618 exit
• No partial booking — book 50% at 1.272, trail rest
• Holding past time-stop — if extension stalls, theta eats premium fast
• Drawing extension during the retracement — premature; wait for confirmed reversal candle in golden zone first
• Ignoring confluence — a Fib level alone is suggestive; with confluence it's actionable
FIBONACCI — COMPLETE TRADE PLAYBOOK
THE 8-POINT FIBONACCI PLAYBOOK
WHY IT MATTERS: Fibonacci levels are self-fulfilling because retail, algos, and institutions all watch them. The 61.8% golden ratio is the single most-respected retracement level in all of technical analysis. Drawing correctly removes guesswork about where to enter pullbacks and where to book profits.

HOW TO READ:
• Shallow pullback (23.6 / 38.2%) → trend is very strong; expect continuation
• Golden zone (50 / 61.8%) → healthy pullback; best entry zone
• Deep pullback (78.6%) → trend weakening; last-chance entry
• Break beyond 100% → retracement failed, trend is over — stand aside

BUY a Call Option WHEN: The higher-timeframe trend is up + price pulls back into the 50 to 61.8 percent golden zone + a bullish reversal candle (hammer / bullish engulfing / morning star) prints at the zone + a volume spike. Best if the zone overlaps with a horizontal support / resistance level or a moving average (confluence).
BUY a Put Option WHEN: The higher-timeframe trend is down + price rallies up into the 50 to 61.8 percent zone + a bearish reversal candle (shooting star / bearish engulfing) prints + a volume spike. Confluence with resistance increases the edge.

STOP LOSS: Just beyond the 78.6 percent level (uptrend: below 78.6 percent; downtrend: above 78.6 percent). If price takes out the 78.6 percent level, the Fibonacci setup is invalidated — the trend is breaking.
TARGET: Use the extension ladder: Target 1 = 1.272 / 1.414 (book 50 percent here) · Target 2 = 1.618 (book 30 percent here) · Target 3 = 2.618 (trail the last 20 percent).

TIMEFRAME: 15-minute / 1-hour Fibonacci for intraday option buyers · daily Fibonacci for swing / positional traders. Never draw Fibonacci levels on sub-5-minute charts — those swings are just noise.
AVOID: (1) Sideways markets — there is no real impulse to anchor to. (2) Fibonacci drawn on a choppy leg — garbage in, garbage out. (3) Entering at a Fibonacci level without a candle trigger. (4) Drawing multiple Fibonacci sets across every wiggle — stick to the one most recent clean impulse move.
When to take this trade — The Fibonacci Golden-Zone Pullback Entry (the highest risk-to-reward setup in this app)
Setup
On the daily chart, Nifty is in a clear uptrend (higher highs and higher lows over the last 4 to 8 weeks). The 60-minute and 15-minute trends both also point UP. There has just been a clean impulse move (a green candle or sequence of green candles covering at least 1.2 percent in less than 4 hours). Now price has started a pullback. Draw a Fibonacci retracement from the impulse low to the impulse high. The pullback should be approaching the 50 to 61.8 percent zone. Volume on the pullback is lower than on the impulse. The Relative Strength Index stays above 40.
Entry
Wait for a bullish reversal candle (hammer, bullish engulfing, or morning star) to close INSIDE the 50 to 61.8 percent zone, with volume above the recent average. BUY one lot of an At The Money Call Option of the current-week or current-month expiry (current-month gives more time and lower Theta decay).
Stop Loss
10 to 15 points below the 78.6 percent Fibonacci level on the spot index. On the option premium itself, set a hard stop at 30 to 35 percent loss. Use a Stop-Loss-Market order on the broker.
Target
Target 1 = the 1.272 or 1.414 Fibonacci extension level (book 50 percent here). Target 2 = the 1.618 extension (book 30 percent here). Target 3 = the 2.618 extension (trail the last 20 percent with a stop at the previous swing low). Hold for 1 to 5 trading days.
Skip if
The pullback exceeds the 78.6 percent Fibonacci level (the trend is breaking, this is now a reversal not a retracement), OR the volume on the pullback is HIGHER than the volume on the impulse (a reversal warning, not a healthy pullback), OR the higher-timeframe trend is sideways (no impulse to anchor the Fibonacci to), OR the India Volatility Index is above 22 (an inflated premium plus the post-pullback Implied Volatility crush will hurt your option).

TIMEFRAME STRATEGY MULTI-TF

What is a "timeframe"? A timeframe is the time each candle on your chart represents. A 5-minute timeframe means each candle = 5 minutes of price action. A 1-hour timeframe means each candle = 1 hour. The chart itself is the same Nifty — only the "zoom level" changes.

Why this page matters: Most beginners stare at ONE chart (usually the 5-minute or 1-minute) and lose money because they cannot SEE the bigger picture. The fix is to look at THREE charts together — a big-picture chart, a signal chart, and an entry chart. Pros call this "multi-timeframe analysis". Sounds fancy, but the idea is simple: zoom OUT to find direction, zoom IN to find entry.
THE 4 TIMEFRAMES — WHAT EACH ONE IS FOR
60 MIN (1 HOUR)
TREND DIRECTION
This is your TREND timeframe. Identify whether the market is bullish, bearish, or sideways. Only trade in this direction on lower timeframes.
15 MIN
SIGNAL TIMEFRAME
Look for candle patterns here. This is your primary signal timeframe. Identify Support and Resistance levels, spot the patterns, confirm with volume.
5 MIN
ENTRY TIMEFRAME
Fine-tune your entry here. After the 15-minute timeframe gives a signal, wait for the 5-minute confirmation candle to enter with a tighter stop loss.
1 MIN
AVOID FOR OPTIONS
Too much noise. False signals everywhere. 1-minute patterns are unreliable for option buying. Use only for scalping futures.
THE 3-SCREEN SYSTEM (ELDER'S METHOD)
SCREEN 1 — 60 MIN
Ask: What is the TREND?
Price above the 20-period Exponential Moving Average → Uptrend → Only buy Call Options.
Price below the 20-period Exponential Moving Average → Downtrend → Only buy Put Options.
Price at the 20-period Exponential Moving Average → Sideways → Avoid trading.
SCREEN 2 — 15 MIN
Ask: What is the SIGNAL?
Look for candle pattern at S&R
Must align with 60-min trend
Volume should confirm
SCREEN 3 — 5 MIN
Ask: Where to ENTER?
Wait for confirmation candle
Enter on next candle open
Place SL below/above signal candle wick
BEST INTRADAY TIME WINDOWS
Time Session Action Why
9:15 AM to 9:30 AM Opening Chaos OBSERVE ONLY Wild swings, no patterns reliable. Just mark the Opening Range Breakout high and low.
9:30 AM to 11:30 AM Best Session MOST ACTIVE TRADING Highest volume, cleanest moves, best patterns. Your primary trading window.
11:30 AM to 1:00 PM Lunch Lull REDUCE SIZE Low volume, choppy, fakeouts are common. Trade smaller positions or skip.
1:00 PM to 2:30 PM Afternoon Session SELECTIVE TRADING The second-best window. Good for breakout trades if the morning trend is continuing.
2:30 PM to 3:15 PM Power Hour THETA DANGER ZONE Avoid buying options. Theta destroys premium rapidly. Exit existing trades.
3:15 PM to 3:30 PM Closing EXIT ALL POSITIONS Mandatory exit. Never carry intraday positions overnight.
