WHICH TIMEFRAME SHOULD YOU TRADE OPTIONS ON?
The #1 mistake option buyers make: trading on a timeframe that doesn't match their style, attention span, or capital. Match the timeframe to YOU, not the other way around.
1-MIN CHART — SCALPING
DO NOT USE FOR OPTIONS
Hold time: 1–5 minutes
Target premium move: ₹3–8
Problem: Option bid-ask spread (₹1–3) + STT + brokerage eats ₹15–25 of your ₹5 target. Mathematically losing.
Noise ratio: Extreme — 70% of patterns are fake.

Verdict: Only for futures scalpers with co-location. Options on 1-min = gambling.
5-MIN CHART — INTRADAY SCALP
ONLY FOR EXPERIENCED
Hold time: 10–45 minutes
Target premium move: ₹15–40
Best for: Breakout trades AFTER a 15-min signal. Fine-tuning entry.
Use case: You've spotted a 15-min bullish engulfing at support → zoom to 5-min → wait for a bullish confirmation candle → enter.

Verdict: Tactical support tool, NOT your primary decision TF.
15-MIN CHART — SWEET SPOT
BEST FOR OPTION BUYERS
Hold time: 45 min – 3 hours
Target premium move: ₹40–120
Why best: Enough candles for patterns to be statistically meaningful. Enough movement to clear costs comfortably. Enough time between candles to think clearly.
Theta impact: Manageable — most trades complete before decay accelerates.

Verdict: Start here. 80% of your intraday option trades should come from 15-min signals.
60-MIN CHART — SWING STYLE
POSITIONAL INTRADAY
Hold time: 2 hours – full day / overnight*
Target premium move: ₹100–300
Best for: Strong trend days (e.g. after RBI policy, major news), breakouts from multi-day ranges, ITM option swing trades.
Theta warning: Holding options overnight near weekly expiry = dangerous. Use monthly or ITM options.

Verdict: For high-conviction setups only.
DAILY CHART — SWING TRADING
MULTI-DAY HOLDS
Hold time: 2–10 days
Target premium move: ₹200–1000+
Best for: ITM options or next-month expiry. NEVER weekly ATM — theta destroys you overnight.
Position size: Half of intraday size since you're exposed to overnight gaps.

Verdict: For traders with capital + patience.
WEEKLY CHART — MACRO VIEW
TREND READING
Don't trade options on it. Use weekly chart only to understand the macro trend that gives context to your daily / 60-min / 15-min trade.

Rule: Never take a trade against the weekly trend unless it's a proven reversal setup (H&S, Island Reversal, etc.).
MATCH THE TIMEFRAME TO YOUR PROFILE
Your Profile Signal TF Entry TF Hold Time Strike Choice Best Expiry
Beginner (learning) 15-min 15-min 1–3 hrs ATM Current / Next week
Intraday (confident) 15-min 5-min 30 min – 2 hrs ATM or 1 OTM Current week
Breakout trader 60-min 15-min 2–6 hrs ATM Current / Next week
Positional intraday 60-min 15-min 4 hrs – full day 1 ITM Next week / Monthly
Swing (2–10 days) Daily 60-min 2–10 days 1 ITM or 2 ITM Monthly
Scalper (advanced) 5-min 1-min 5–30 min ATM liquid Current week
HOW TO DECIDE YOUR OWN TIMEFRAME (DECISION TREE)
Q1 — HOW MUCH TIME DO YOU HAVE AT THE SCREEN?
• All day (full-time): 15-min signal TF, 5-min entry TF
• 2–3 hours: 15-min signal, 15-min entry (place orders, step away)
• <1 hour (checking phone): Daily chart swing trades only — do NOT intraday
Q2 — HOW DO YOU REACT TO NOISE / CANDLE JIGGLES?
• Panic on every red candle: Go higher TF (60-min or daily). Less noise = less emotion.
• Bored waiting for 15-min candle to close: Either stay with 15-min and build discipline, OR move to 5-min if experienced.
• Calm either way: 15-min is your sweet spot.
Q3 — WHAT'S YOUR CAPITAL? (POST-65-LOT NIFTY)
• < ₹1,00,000: Paper trade — real capital too small after SEBI changes
• ₹1–2 L: 15-min intraday ATM only, 1 lot Nifty
• ₹2–5 L: 15-min intraday + occasional 60-min swings, 1–2 lots
• ₹5 L+: Can use any TF. Scale lot with edge proven over 6 months.
Q4 — WHAT'S YOUR LOSS TOLERANCE PER TRADE?
• ₹500–2000 per trade: 15-min, ATM, current week
• ₹2000–5000: 15-min or 60-min, ATM / 1 ITM
• ₹5000+: You need a 60-min or daily TF with room to breathe, otherwise SL hits noise
• Rule: SL distance (in points) must be ≥ 1.5× ATR of your signal TF. If your SL is tighter, move to a smaller TF.

THE DEFINITIVE TIMEFRAME ANSWER FOR 90 PERCENT OF READERS

  • Use the 60-minute chart to read the trend — is the market bullish, bearish, or sideways today?
  • Use the 15-minute chart to find your signal — a candle pattern + volume + support/resistance confluence + Volume Weighted Average Price alignment.
  • Use the 5-minute chart to refine the entry — wait for the confirmation candle on the 5-minute chart after the 15-minute signal candle completes.
  • Hold for 30 minutes to 3 hours — most 15-minute signal option trades resolve in this window.
  • Stop looking at the 1-minute chart — it will only make you panic-exit a good trade, or enter a bad one.
  • Exit by 3:00 PM regardless of the trade — Theta decay accelerates sharply in the last 30 minutes.
When to take this trade — Multi-Timeframe Confluence Entry (the highest-probability intraday setup)
Setup
The 60-minute chart shows Nifty trending up (price above the 20-period Exponential Moving Average). The 15-minute chart shows a Bullish Engulfing candle at a key support level (Previous Day High, the Volume Weighted Average Price, or the top of the Central Pivot Range), with volume above 1.5 times the 20-period average. The 5-minute chart shows a clean follow-through candle confirming the move.
Entry
Buy an At The Money Nifty Call Option of the current week or next week's expiry, on the open of the next 5-minute candle. Use a limit order at the mid-price.
Stop Loss
5 points below the 15-minute Bullish Engulfing candle's low. On the option premium, set a hard stop at 30 percent loss.
Target
Book 50 percent of the position at the next 15-minute swing high. Trail the rest with a 5-minute Volume Weighted Average Price stop. Exit the entire position by 3:00 PM — no exceptions.
Skip if
The 60-minute trend disagrees with your trade direction (you must NOT fight the higher timeframe), OR the time is during the lunch-hour lull (11:30 AM to 1:00 PM IST), OR the 5-minute confirmation candle is a Doji (signals indecision, not direction).

CPR & PIVOT POINTS INDIA'S FAVOURITE INTRADAY TOOL

What is the Central Pivot Range (CPR)? It is the most popular intraday tool among Indian option buyers. More than 60 percent of active intraday traders use it. Every major Indian broker (Zerodha, Upstox, Dhan, Angel One) plots it automatically. Set it up ONCE on your chart, and you will never have to draw a support / resistance line by hand again.

Why traders love it: CPR uses just YESTERDAY’s prices to predict TODAY’s important levels — before the market even opens. No charts to study, no patterns to spot. Just three lines that show up automatically.
WHAT IS THE CENTRAL PIVOT RANGE (in plain English)?
THE 3 LINES OF THE CENTRAL PIVOT RANGE
Think of the Central Pivot Range as a shaded band drawn across your chart. It is made of THREE lines that come from yesterday’s High, Low, and Close. That is it — pure math, no opinion.

The three lines explained:
· Top Central (TC) — the upper edge of the band.
· Pivot Point (PP) — the centre line (the most important level of the day).
· Bottom Central (BC) — the lower edge of the band.

The Top Central and Bottom Central together create a SHADED BAND on your chart. The Pivot Point cuts the band in half. That whole shaded zone is the "Central Pivot Range".
WHY DOES IT WORK? (THE SIMPLE LOGIC)
The simple idea: Yesterday’s High, Low and Close show where the market already AGREED on price. Today, the market is likely to start its discussion from roughly the same area.

Think of it like this:
· The Central Pivot Range is a magnet — price keeps coming back to the band.
· The R1 / R2 / R3 levels above are resistance walls.
· The S1 / S2 / S3 levels below are support floors.

Price does not HAVE to follow these levels. But it usually does. And when it does NOT, that breakaway move is itself a strong signal.
HOW THE CENTRAL PIVOT RANGE CHANGES YOUR INTRADAY CHART
Once you plot the Central Pivot Range on your 5-minute or 15-minute chart, it completely changes your decision-making during the day. Below are the 6 BIG things it does for you.
1 • PREDICTS TRENDING vs SIDEWAYS DAY (BEFORE MARKET OPENS)
The width of the Central Pivot Range band (the gap between Top Central and Bottom Central) tells you what KIND of day to expect — even before the first candle prints.

· Narrow band = compressed energy = expect a TRENDING day. (Big move coming.)
· Wide band = energy already spent = expect a SIDEWAYS / range day.

What this changes for you: You pick your strategy in advance. Narrow band → use Opening Range Breakout setups. Wide band → fade the extremes, stay inside the R1 / S1 range.
2 • TELLS YOU WHEN TO BUY CALL vs BUY PUT
The Central Pivot Range is a direction filter, not an entry signal. Where price SITS relative to the band tells you which side to take:

· Nifty trading ABOVE the band → only BUY a Call Option setups today.
· Nifty trading BELOW the band → only BUY a Put Option setups today.
· Nifty trading INSIDE the band → no trade. Wait for price to break out.

What this changes for you: It cuts out HALF of your bad setups. Even if you spot a bullish candlestick pattern, you skip it if price is below the Central Pivot Range.
3 • AUTOMATIC SUPPORT & RESISTANCE LADDER
Above the band: R1 → R2 → R3 are your resistance targets. Below the band: S1 → S2 → S3 are your support targets. No need to draw anything manually — these levels plot themselves the moment market opens.

What this changes for you: Your profit TARGETS and stop loss ANCHORS are pre-decided. On a trending day breaking above the Top Central → R1 is your first target. On a sideways day rejecting at R1 → fade back to the Pivot Point.
4 • PRICE BEHAVES LIKE A MAGNET (Predictable Pullbacks)
Price keeps coming back to the Central Pivot Range like a magnet, OR it keeps bouncing off its edges. Once price BREAKS OUT sharply, it almost ALWAYS comes back to test the band at least ONCE before moving away — this pullback is the safest entry.

What this changes for you: You get a clear "expected pullback" zone after every breakout. Breakout above Top Central with volume → WAIT for the pullback to the Top Central → enter on the bullish reversal candle. Much safer than chasing.
5 • THE NOISE FILTER (FEWER BAD TRADES)
Without the Central Pivot Range, every hammer candle on every 5-minute chart looks tradable. With it, you only take a trade when the pattern prints AT a meaningful level — the Top Central, Bottom Central, R1, S1, or Pivot Point.

What this changes for you: Your number of "tradable" setups drops by about 60 percent — but the hit rate of the remaining setups goes UP. Fewer trades, bigger edge per trade. Exactly what beats brokerage costs in Indian option buying.
6 • ZERO OPINIONS — PURE MATH
The Central Pivot Range is just simple math on three numbers (yesterday’s High, Low and Close). No personal opinion. No subjective drawing. No hindsight bias. Every trader using any broker sees the EXACT same lines. That is also WHY these levels work — everyone is watching the same level.

What this changes for you: When you backtest old trades or write a journal, your levels are reproducible. You cannot "cheat" by drawing lines that fit after-the-fact.
HOW CPR IS CALCULATED & READ
HOW CPR IS CALCULATED (DAILY)
Based on PREVIOUS DAY'S High, Low, Close.

Pivot (PP) = (H + L + C) ÷ 3
BC (Bottom Central) = (H + L) ÷ 2
TC (Top Central) = (PP × 2) − BC

CPR = area between TC and BC

Plus support/resistance pivots:
R1 = PP × 2 − L · R2 = PP + (H − L) · R3 = H + 2(PP − L)
S1 = PP × 2 − H · S2 = PP − (H − L) · S3 = L − 2(H − PP)

Your broker plots these automatically — no manual maths needed.
CPR WIDTH — THE MOST IMPORTANT SIGNAL
DAY-TYPE FORECAST
Width = |TC − BC| — the distance between the two central lines. It predicts the type of day before market opens.

• Narrow (<0.2% of spot) → trending day likely. Trade breakouts aggressively.
• Normal (0.2–0.5%) → mixed. Wait for direction.
• Wide (>0.5%) → sideways / range day. Avoid breakout trades, fade extremes.

Full worked example, thresholds per index, and the "why" are in the CPR WIDTH — CALCULATION IN DETAIL block below.
PRICE VS CPR BIAS
DIRECTIONAL FILTER
• Price consistently above CPR → Bullish bias. Only take CE setups.
• Price consistently below CPR → Bearish bias. Only take PE setups.
• Price oscillating inside CPR → Don't trade. Wait for a sustained break above or below.
VIRGIN CPR — ULTRA-HIGH PROBABILITY
A CPR is called Virgin if price did NOT touch it during the entire previous trading day.

Why it matters: Virgin CPRs act as ultra-strong magnets. Price reaches them ~80% of the time within the next 1–2 sessions.

How to trade: Identify virgin CPR from prior day → wait for price to approach it → trade bounce (with candle + volume confirmation) back toward prior direction.
STANDARD PIVOT S/R LEVELS
Beyond CPR, the pivot set gives you automatic S/R levels for the day:

Resistances: R1 (most tested) · R2 (target for trending days) · R3 (exhaustion)
Supports: S1 (first bounce) · S2 (trend-day target) · S3 (panic low)

Use as: Profit targets when trading breakouts (R1 from CPR break, then R2), and stop-loss anchors.
OTHER PIVOT TYPES
Most platforms offer multiple pivot formulas — default Classical is fine.

• Classical / Standard → default, what most use
• Fibonacci Pivot → uses 38.2/61.8% of range for R1/S1. Better for volatile stocks.
• Camarilla → 8 intraday levels (H1–H4, L1–L4). Popular for scalping.
• Woodie's → weights prior close more. Less used.

Recommendation: Stick with Classical + CPR for 95% of use cases.
CPR WIDTH — CALCULATION IN DETAIL
CPR width is the single most predictive signal on this tool. Before the market opens, it tells you whether to expect a trending day (narrow) or a range-bound day (wide). Below is the exact maths with a worked example — once you do this twice by hand, you'll read CPR width at a glance.
STEP-BY-STEP FORMULA
Inputs — previous day's:
• High (H) · Low (L) · Close (C)

Step 1 — Pivot Point (PP):
PP = (H + L + C) ÷ 3

Step 2 — Bottom Central (BC):
BC = (H + L) ÷ 2

Step 3 — Top Central (TC):
TC = (PP × 2) − BC

Step 4 — CPR Width (absolute):
Width = |TC − BC|

Step 5 — CPR Width (normalised):
Width % = (Width ÷ Close) × 100

The % is what you compare across days and indices — 20 pts on Nifty is not the same as 20 pts on a ₹500 stock.
WORKED EXAMPLE — NIFTY
ONE FULL CALCULATION
Previous day's Nifty:
H = 26,250 · L = 26,050 · C = 26,180

PP = (26,250 + 26,050 + 26,180) ÷ 3
    = 78,480 ÷ 3 = 26,160

BC = (26,250 + 26,050) ÷ 2
    = 52,300 ÷ 2 = 26,150

TC = (26,160 × 2) − 26,150
    = 52,320 − 26,150 = 26,170

Width = |26,170 − 26,150| = 20 pts
Width % = (20 ÷ 26,180) × 100 = 0.076%

< 0.2% → NARROW CPR → expect a trending day. Look for a clean break above TC or below BC with volume; trade in that direction toward R1/S1.
THRESHOLDS BY INSTRUMENT (QUICK REFERENCE)
Convert the % thresholds to raw points once and keep them in your pre-market notes. Values below assume approximate recent index levels — recalculate if your index is materially higher/lower.
INDEX APPROX. SPOT NARROW (<0.2%) NORMAL (0.2–0.5%) WIDE (>0.5%) DAY-TYPE
NIFTY 50 ~26,000 < 52 pts 52 – 130 pts > 130 pts Narrow → TREND
Wide → RANGE
BANKNIFTY ~57,000 < 114 pts 114 – 285 pts > 285 pts Narrow → TREND
Wide → RANGE
SENSEX ~85,000 < 170 pts 170 – 425 pts > 425 pts Narrow → TREND
Wide → RANGE
WHY IT WORKS — THE INTUITION
NARROW CPR → TRENDING DAY
A narrow CPR means yesterday's close was near the midpoint of the day's range — buyers and sellers finished balanced. That balance is a compressed spring: when today's open tips the scale, positioning follows in one direction and the market runs.

Rule of thumb: if today's open is noticeably above TC with volume, the day usually trends up; noticeably below BC, it trends down. Breakout playbooks (ORB, supply/demand break) have their highest edge on these days.
WIDE CPR → RANGE DAY
A wide CPR means yesterday's close was far from the midpoint — one side got exhausted. Today, the most likely behaviour is mean reversion: price oscillates inside TC–BC or between R1 and S1.

Rule of thumb: fade extremes rather than chase them. Breakout trades fail the most on wide-CPR days — stick to reversion setups at R1/S1 with candle confirmation, or simply sit out.
Two things the width does NOT tell you: (1) direction — you still need price vs CPR bias plus a candle trigger; (2) certainty — big-event days (RBI, Fed, results) can flip a narrow CPR into a gap-and-reverse trap. CPR width is a conditional prior, not a forecast.
NORMAL vs INVERTED CPR — THE SHAPE SIGNAL
Width tells you the type of day. Shape tells you the bias of the day. When TC sits below BC on the chart, the CPR is inverted / flipped — a genuine bearish structural signal that most beginners miss because their broker's script labels lines by formula, not by visual position.
NORMAL CPR — TC ABOVE BC
PREV-DAY CLOSED IN UPPER HALF
What it is: TC plots above BC (conventional layout).

Why it forms: yesterday's Close ≥ (H + L) / 2 — the session closed in the upper half of its range. Buyers held control at the bell.

Bias it broadcasts: neutral with a mild bullish tilt for today.

How to read: treat TC as first resistance, BC as first support, PP as the pivot. Use the normal price-vs-CPR rules — long above, short below, no-trade inside.
INVERTED / FLIPPED CPR — TC BELOW BC
PREV-DAY CLOSED IN LOWER HALF
What it is: TC plots below BC — the lines appear visually flipped.

Why it forms: yesterday's Close < (H + L) / 2 — the session closed in the lower half of its range. Sellers had the last word. The formula TC = 2·PP − BC mechanically pushes TC under BC.

Bias it broadcasts: structurally bearish for today — a continuation lean, not a forecast.

How to read: treat the upper line (BC) as the harder resistance, lower line (TC) as the softer resistance. Above the entire band → bias flips and you stop shorting.
HOW TO SPOT INVERSION ON YOUR BROKER CHART
Watch the values, not the labels. Upstox / Dhan / Zerodha scripts label the lines by formula role (Top Pivot = TC, Bottom Pivot = BC) even when the visual order flips. If the line named "Top Pivot" has a smaller number than the one named "Bottom Pivot", the CPR is inverted — regardless of which line sits higher on the chart.
WORKED EXAMPLE — INVERTED CPR (NIFTY, LIVE READING)
Broker shows:
• Daily Top Pivot = 24,184.21 → this is TC
• Daily Central Pivot = 24,190.77 → this is PP
• Daily Bottom Pivot = 24,197.33 → this is BC

Check #1 — is it inverted? TC (24,184) < BC (24,197) → YES, inverted. Bearish tone.
Check #2 — width? |24,184.21 − 24,197.33| = 13.12 pts. On Nifty at ~24,043, that is 0.055% → ultra-narrow. Strong trending day.
Check #3 — where is price? Spot 24,043 is ~150 pts below the band → trend already down; CPR band is now stacked resistance.

Combined read: strong bearish trend day. Primary trade = fade rallies into TC (24,184) with a bearish candle trigger; buy PE; SL above BC (24,197); targets S1 → S2. Flip condition = clean 5-min close above 24,197 with volume.
HOW TO TRADE A NORMAL CPR
Above the band: CE bias. Buy pullbacks into TC with a bullish candle trigger. SL = below BC. Targets R1 → R2.

Below the band: PE bias. Sell rallies into BC with a bearish candle trigger. SL = above TC. Targets S1 → S2.

Inside the band: no trade. Let price pick a side.

Best when paired with: ORB + volume confirmation + narrow width.
HOW TO TRADE AN INVERTED CPR
Default bias: PE. Sell rallies into the lower edge of the band (TC) with a bearish candle trigger. SL = above the upper edge (BC). Targets S1 → S2.

Invalidation → switch to CE: a clean 5-min close above BC with expanding volume flips intraday structure. Wait for a retest of BC as support; only then take CE.

Avoid: aggressive long trades just because price is bouncing — the CPR shape is telling you sellers had the last word yesterday. Respect that until structure proves otherwise.
Inverted CPR is not "wrong" or rare — it's just a bearish-tone day. Most books skip this distinction and retail beginners end up long-biased even when the structure screams weakness. Checking inversion is a 2-second habit that pays for itself on every trending-down day.
CPR + CANDLE CONFIRMATION — THE ENTRY TRIGGER
CPR alone is only a bias filter, not an entry signal. You still need a candle pattern + volume at the level. CPR tells you where to trade; candles tell you when.
BULL SETUP EXAMPLE
PULLBACK TO TC
Condition: price pulls back to TC from above.
Trigger: bullish engulfing / hammer + above-average volume.
Action: buy ATM CE. SL: below BC. Target: R1 (first), R2 (trend day).
BEAR SETUP EXAMPLE
RALLY TO BC
Condition: price rallies to BC from below.
Trigger: bearish engulfing / shooting star + volume spike.
Action: buy ATM PE. SL: above TC. Target: S1 (first), S2 (trend day).
BREAKOUT SETUP
NARROW CPR BREAK
Condition: narrow CPR, price consolidates near TC for 30–60 min.
Trigger: breakout candle closes above TC with 1.5× average volume.
Action: buy CE. SL: back below TC. Target: R1 → R2.
USING PIVOT S/R LEVELS (R1, R2, R3 / S1, S2, S3)

HOW TO USE PIVOT LEVELS AS TARGETS AND STOPS

  • R1 / S1 → first profit target after a CPR break. Usually reached on normal-volatility days.
  • R2 / S2 → extended target for trend days. Typically hit only when momentum is strong and volume expands.
  • R3 / S3 → exhaustion zone — reached on fewer than 10% of days. If price tags R3/S3, book profits; don't expect more.
  • Stop-loss anchors: place SL 5–10 points beyond the next pivot level, never exactly on it — operators hunt round levels.
CPR DAILY ROUTINE — WHAT TO DO WHEN
Time (IST) Action with CPR Why it matters
8:45 AM Note today's CPR width (narrow / normal / wide) and location vs expected open. Decide day-type before the open — breakout strategy vs fade strategy.
9:15 AM Observe opening location: above TC, below BC, or inside CPR. Sets directional bias for the whole session.
9:15–9:30 Do NOT trade the opening 15 min. Let CPR "digest" the gap. First 15 min has maximum noise — operators sweep liquidity around CPR.
9:30 AM onward Trade only in direction of CPR bias + candle confirmation + volume. Highest probability window is 9:30–11:30.
12:00–1:30 CPR levels often re-tested. Good for adding to running trades on pullback. Lunch session — slow momentum, respect of levels is cleanest.
2:00 PM onward Tighten SL. Avoid fresh CPR breakouts. Late-day breakouts often fail — operators trap late entries and hunt stops into close.
COMMON CPR MISTAKES
TRADING INSIDE CPR
Price inside CPR is no-man's land. Theta bleeds your option and moves are small. Wait for a clean break above TC or below BC.
IGNORING CPR WIDTH
Trading breakouts on a wide CPR = losing money. Trading fades on a narrow CPR = missed trends. Always match strategy to width.
USING CPR ALONE
CPR is a filter, not a trigger. Without candle + volume, you're guessing. Combine CPR with price action for a real edge.
EXACT SL AT A PIVOT
Operators run stops parked at R1/S1. Place SL 5–10 points beyond the pivot, never on it.
WEEKLY/MONTHLY PIVOTS INTRADAY
Intraday trading uses daily pivots. Weekly pivots are for swing traders. Always confirm your reference timeframe.
IGNORING VIRGIN CPR
If yesterday's CPR was untouched, today's target is very likely to be it. Missing this setup is leaving free probability on the table.
CPR GREEN-LIGHT CHECKLIST

BEFORE EVERY CPR TRADE

  • Did I note today's CPR width (narrow / normal / wide)?
  • Is price CLEANLY above TC or below BC (not inside CPR)?
  • Is there a candle pattern at the pivot level (not just price touching)?
  • Is volume ≥ 1.5× the 20-candle average?
  • Is my SL placed beyond the next pivot, not exactly at it?
  • Is my target at least R1/S1 (minimum 1:1.5 risk-reward)?
  • Is this trade aligned with the day-type (breakout on narrow, fade on wide)?
  • Is it between 9:30 AM and 2:00 PM (the high-probability window)?
Rule of thumb: if the Central Pivot Range is narrow and the volume is expanding, the break will run — stay with it. If the Central Pivot Range is wide and price chops inside it, do not trade — fight the urge. Discipline at the Central Pivot Range level is the 80/20 of intraday edge.
When to take this trade — The Narrow Central Pivot Range Breakout (the highest-edge intraday setup)
Setup
It is the night before, or before the market opens. Your charting platform shows today’s Central Pivot Range and it is NARROW (the width is less than 0.2 percent of the spot price — so under 50 points on Nifty at 25,000). Yesterday’s Central Pivot Range was also narrow (a sign of compressed energy). The India Volatility Index is between 12 and 18. There is no major event scheduled today.
Entry
Wait for a 15-minute candle to CLOSE above the Top Central level (this is the bullish trigger) OR a 15-minute candle to CLOSE below the Bottom Central level (this is the bearish trigger). The volume during that candle must be greater than 1.5 times the recent average. Wait for ONE retest of the broken level, then BUY one lot of an At The Money Call Option (for a bullish break) or an At The Money Put Option (for a bearish break) of the current-week expiry.
Stop Loss
10 to 15 points back inside the Central Pivot Range, on the spot index (so for a Call Option, the stop is below the Top Central level by 10 to 15 points). On the option premium itself, set a hard stop at 30 percent loss. Use a Stop-Loss-Market order on the broker.
Target
Target 1 = the Resistance 1 level for a Call Option (or the Support 1 level for a Put Option) — book 50 percent here. Target 2 = the Resistance 2 / Support 2 level — trail the stop loss to break-even for the remainder. Exit by 2:30 PM IST regardless.
Skip if
The Central Pivot Range is wide (greater than 0.5 percent of spot — that means yesterday spent the energy already), OR price was rejected at the Top Central / Bottom Central levels twice already today (that is two failed attempts — it is no longer high probability), OR there was no volume on the breakout candle (no institutional commitment), OR the breakout happens after 2:00 PM IST (not enough time left for the move to develop and Theta will eat your premium).

COMPLETE STRATEGY GUIDE MASTER TABLE

How to read the tables below:
· BUY Call Option means buy a Call Option of the index (also written as "BUY CE" in some places — the same thing).
· BUY Put Option means buy a Put Option of the index (also written as "BUY PE" in some places — the same thing).
· TF means timeframe (the chart period — 5-minute, 15-minute, 60-minute, daily).
· S/R means support and resistance — horizontal price levels where past buying or selling was strong.
· VWAP means Volume Weighted Average Price — the average traded price of the day, used as a fair-value reference.
Each row shows: the candle / chart pattern, where it appears, the signal it gives, the action to take, and the timeframe to use.
SINGLE CANDLE → ACTION
Pattern Where to Find It Signal Type Option TF
Bullish Marubozu Breakout / trend Strong Bull Momentum BUY CE 5m/15m
Bearish Marubozu Breakdown / trend Strong Bear Momentum BUY PE 5m/15m
Bullish Belt Hold Gap-up session open Strong Bull Open BUY CE 5m
Bearish Belt Hold Gap-down session open Strong Bear Open BUY PE 5m
Hammer At key support Bullish Reversal BUY CE 5m/15m
Hanging Man At key resistance Bearish Reversal BUY PE 5m/15m
Inverted Hammer After downtrend at support Bullish Reversal BUY CE 15m
Shooting Star At key resistance top Bearish Reversal BUY PE 5m/15m
Dragonfly Doji At support level Strong Bull Reversal BUY CE 15m
Gravestone Doji At resistance level Strong Bear Reversal BUY PE 15m

10 GOLDEN RULES — QUICK CHEAT SHEET

Quick pointers only. Each rule has a dedicated tab with the full playbook.

  • Pattern + Level: A pattern alone means nothing — it must sit AT support or resistance.
  • Volume is mandatory: No volume spike = no conviction = skip the trade.
  • Trend alignment: Trade WITH the higher-timeframe trend.
  • Doji = pause: Always wait for the next candle to confirm before acting.
  • Trap awareness: Failed breakouts and liquidity sweeps flip the direction.
  • Strike, expiry, sizing, stop loss: Covered in and
  • When to trade: The best time windows, the Theta zones, the expiry-day rules — see
When to take this trade — The Universal Pattern + Level + Volume Setup (the only formula that works across every table above)
Setup
You spot a candle pattern from any table above (for example, a hammer, a bullish engulfing, or a morning star). The pattern is forming AT a major level (the previous day’s low, the daily Volume Weighted Average Price, the Central Pivot Range Top Central or Bottom Central, the 200-day Exponential Moving Average, or a horizontal support / resistance from the daily chart). The volume on the pattern candle is greater than 1.5 times the recent average. The higher-timeframe trend (the daily chart) agrees with your trade direction.
Entry
Wait for the NEXT candle after the pattern to confirm the direction (a bullish confirmation candle for a Call Option, a bearish confirmation candle for a Put Option). BUY one lot of an At The Money Call Option or Put Option of the current-week expiry on the next candle’s open. Use a Limit order at the planned entry price (NOT a Market order).
Stop Loss
Place the stop loss 5 to 10 points beyond the wick of the pattern candle on the spot index (below the wick low for a Call Option, above the wick high for a Put Option). On the option premium itself, set a hard stop at 30 percent loss. Place a Stop-Loss-Market order on the broker IMMEDIATELY after your buy order is filled.
Target
Target 1 = the next clear support / resistance level on the chart (book 50 percent here AND move the stop loss to your entry / break-even). Target 2 = the level after that, OR a 1 to 3 risk-to-reward (book another 25 percent). Trail the rest with a stop at the previous swing low (for a Call Option) or swing high (for a Put Option). Be flat by 3:00 PM IST.
Skip if
The pattern is NOT at a major level (it is just floating in mid-range — low edge), OR the volume is below the recent average (no institutional commitment), OR the higher-timeframe trend is against you (you would be fighting the daily flow), OR the pattern is from the "trap" table above (those need the OPPOSITE action), OR the India Volatility Index is above 22 (the Implied Volatility crush will damage your premium even if you are right on direction).

TREND INDICATORS 3 CORE TOOLS

What is a trend indicator? A trend indicator is a small mathematical tool that you add to your chart to answer TWO simple questions:
· Which DIRECTION is price moving (up, down, or sideways)?
· How STRONGLY is it moving?

Why this matters: Trading AGAINST a strong trend means fighting the big-money players. You will lose. Trading WITH the trend means the big players are on your side. You win more often.

The 3 trend tools every Indian trader should know:
· Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP) — the "fair price line" that institutions use for intraday trades.
· Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs) — smoothed price lines that show if the trend is strong or weak.
· Supertrend indicator — a coloured line that flips green / red when the trend changes.

Use them in this order: VWAP for direction, EMAs for strength, Supertrend for trend flips.

HOW TO READ EACH INDICATOR CARD BELOW

  • WHY IT MATTERS — What edge it gives you, and why professional traders use it.
  • HOW TO READ — The 2 to 3 actual signals you watch for.
  • BUY CALL WHEN / BUY PUT WHEN — The exact trigger conditions for taking a trade.
  • STOP LOSS / TARGET — Where the stop loss and profit-taking levels go.
  • TIMEFRAME — The chart timeframe where the indicator works best.
  • AVOID — The market condition that breaks the signal.
VOLUME WEIGHTED AVERAGE PRICE
MOST IMPORTANT INTRADAY TOOL
WHY IT MATTERS: The Volume Weighted Average Price is the "fair price" benchmark used by big institutions. Mutual funds, Foreign Institutional Investors, and trading algorithms execute their large orders around this line. Trading against it means trading against the day's smart-money flow.

HOW TO READ:
• Price above the Volume Weighted Average Price line means buyers are in control for the day.
• Price below the Volume Weighted Average Price line means sellers are in control.
• The slope of the line tells you the direction of the trend. The distance of price from the line tells you whether the move is overextended.

BUY CALL WHEN: Price pulls back DOWN to a rising Volume Weighted Average Price line, AND a bullish rejection candle forms (Hammer or Bullish Engulfing), AND there is a volume spike on that rejection candle.
BUY PUT WHEN: Price rallies UP to a falling Volume Weighted Average Price line, AND a bearish rejection candle forms (Shooting Star or Bearish Engulfing), AND there is a volume spike on that rejection candle.

STOP LOSS: 10 to 15 points beyond the Volume Weighted Average Price line on the wrong side, for Nifty. Scale this with the Average True Range for BankNifty.
TARGET: Nearest pivot level (Resistance 1 or Support 1) or the previous session's high or low. Minimum 1 to 2 risk-to-reward ratio.
TIMEFRAME: 5-minute chart only (the line resets at the start of every trading day).
AVOID: Flat, sideways days when the Volume Weighted Average Price line itself is flat (no edge to trade). Also avoid the first 15 minutes of the day (the line is unstable then).
→ Pullback to VWAP + candle + volume
20 / 50 / 200 PERIOD EXPONENTIAL MOVING AVERAGES
MOVING SUPPORT & RESISTANCE
WHY IT MATTERS: Exponential Moving Averages smooth out the price noise and reveal the real underlying trend. The way the moving averages are stacked (their order top to bottom) tells you whether the trend is strong or weakening.

HOW TO READ:
• The 20 period Exponential Moving Average shows the short-term pulse (use it for scalping support and resistance).
• The 50 period Exponential Moving Average shows the intraday swing trend.
• The 200 period Exponential Moving Average is the major regime filter.
• If the 20 is above the 50 which is above the 200, you have a strong uptrend. The reverse order means a strong downtrend.

BUY CALL WHEN: Price pulls back to a rising 20 period Exponential Moving Average on the 5-minute chart (or the rising 50 period on the 15-minute chart), AND a Bullish Engulfing or Hammer candle forms there, AND the moving average stack order is 20 above 50 above 200.
BUY PUT WHEN: Price rallies up to a falling 20 period Exponential Moving Average, AND a bearish candle forms there, AND the stack order is 20 below 50 below 200.

STOP LOSS: 10 to 15 points beyond the moving average you used as your entry trigger.
TARGET: The previous swing high or swing low. Minimum 1 to 2 risk-to-reward ratio.
TIMEFRAME: 5-minute chart for 20 period scalping. 15-minute chart for 50 period intraday. Daily chart for 200 period regime check.
AVOID: Choppy, sideways days where the moving averages are flat and tangled together. Also avoid news gaps that jump straight through the moving averages.
→ Pullback to aligned EMA + candle
SUPERTREND
TREND FOLLOWING
WHY IT MATTERS: The simplest visual trend filter ever invented. One line, one colour, one rule: when the line is green, only take long trades; when the line is red, only take short trades. Removes any uncertainty in your bias.

HOW TO READ:
• The line is below the price and green: an uptrend is active.
• The line is above the price and red: a downtrend is active.
• A colour flip means a structural change in the trend.
• Default settings: 10 periods, 3 multiplier.

BUY CALL WHEN: Supertrend flips from red to green, AND the very next candle closes above the high of the flip candle, AND there is a volume spike. Use the 15-minute chart.
BUY PUT WHEN: Supertrend flips from green to red, AND the next candle closes below the low of the flip candle, AND there is a volume spike.

STOP LOSS: The opposite side of the Supertrend line at the time of entry (this trails automatically as price moves).
TARGET: Trail your stop with the Supertrend line and exit only when the colour flips back.
TIMEFRAME: 15-minute or 1-hour chart. Avoid timeframes less than 5-minute (too many false signals).
AVOID: Range-bound or choppy markets (Supertrend gives constant whipsaw signals). Check the Central Pivot Range width first — if it is wide, skip Supertrend signals for the day.
→ Wait for flip + next-candle close + volume
When to take this trade — VWAP Pullback (the most important intraday setup)
Setup
It is between 10:00 AM and 2:00 PM (the best window). The 5-minute chart shows price has been moving in one direction for at least 30 to 60 minutes. The Volume Weighted Average Price line is sloping in the same direction (rising for an uptrend, falling for a downtrend). Now price is pulling back to touch the line.
Entry
For an uptrend pullback: Buy a Call Option (At the Money or one strike Out of the Money) when price touches the rising line and forms a Hammer or Bullish Engulfing candle, AND volume on this candle is 1.5 times the recent average. For a downtrend pullback: Buy a Put Option when price touches the falling line and forms a Shooting Star or Bearish Engulfing.
Stop Loss
10 to 15 points on the wrong side of the Volume Weighted Average Price line. For the option premium, exit if you lose 30 to 35 percent.
Target
The previous swing high (for Calls) or swing low (for Puts). Minimum 1 to 2 risk-to-reward ratio. Trail your stop loss to breakeven once price has moved 1 times your risk in your favor.
Skip if
The Volume Weighted Average Price line is flat (no trend bias to trade), it is the first 15 minutes of the day, the rejection candle has a long wick on the wrong side, or the lunch hour (12:00 PM to 1:30 PM IST) is upon you.

MOMENTUM & VOLATILITY 4 CONFIRMATION TOOLS

What are momentum and volatility indicators?

· Momentum indicators = tools that tell you HOW FAST price is moving. They are like a speedometer in your car — they tell you if the trend is gaining speed or running out of energy.
· Volatility indicators = tools that tell you HOW FAR price typically moves. They are like a weather forecast — they tell you if the day is calm or stormy.

Important warning: Never enter a trade JUST because a momentum indicator gives a signal. They are CONFIRMATION tools, not entry signals. Always start with price action and trend, then use these to CONFIRM.

The 4 tools every trader should know:
· Relative Strength Index (RSI) — measures if the market is overbought (too high, ready to fall) or oversold (too low, ready to bounce).
· Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) — shows trend strength and warns when a trend is about to reverse.
· Bollinger Bands — show how far price has moved from average. Price tends to come back to the middle.
· Average True Range (ATR) — tells you how big a typical move is. Used to set stop loss size correctly.

Simple rule: Price action and trend tell you WHEN to enter. Momentum CONFIRMS the signal. Volatility tells you HOW BIG to size the trade.

HOW TO READ EACH INDICATOR CARD BELOW

  • WHY IT MATTERS — What edge it gives you, and why professional traders use it.
  • HOW TO READ — The 2 to 3 actual signals you watch for.
  • BUY CALL WHEN / BUY PUT WHEN — The exact trigger conditions for taking a trade.
  • STOP LOSS / TARGET — Where the stop loss and profit-taking levels go.
  • TIMEFRAME — The chart timeframe where the indicator works best.
  • AVOID — The market condition that breaks the signal.
RELATIVE STRENGTH INDEX
MOMENTUM OSCILLATOR
WHY IT MATTERS: Measures the speed and strength of price moves. Extreme readings hint at exhaustion. Divergence against price (when price makes a new high but the indicator does not) warns of a weakening trend before price actually reverses.

HOW TO READ:
• Above 70 means overbought (expect a pullback, not necessarily a crash).
• Below 30 means oversold (expect a bounce).
• A cross of the 50 line indicates a shift in trend bias.
• Divergence (price makes a higher high, but the Relative Strength Index makes a lower high) is the strongest reversal warning available.

BUY CALL WHEN: A bullish divergence forms at a support level, AND a bullish candle (Bullish Engulfing or Hammer), AND the Relative Strength Index crosses back above 40, AND volume confirms.
BUY PUT WHEN: A bearish divergence forms at Resistance 1 or Resistance 2, AND a bearish candle, AND the Relative Strength Index crosses below 60, AND volume confirms.

STOP LOSS: Beyond the swing high or low that created the divergence.
TARGET: The nearest support or resistance. Minimum 1 to 2 risk-to-reward ratio.
TIMEFRAME: 5-minute chart with period 9 for intraday. 15-minute or 1-hour chart with period 14 for swing trades.
AVOID: Strong trending markets — the Relative Strength Index can stay overbought or oversold for hours. Never trade against a trending market using only the Relative Strength Index.
→ Divergence + candle + 50-line cross
MOVING AVERAGE CONVERGENCE DIVERGENCE
TREND + MOMENTUM
WHY IT MATTERS: Combines direction (line crosses) with strength (the histogram bars). One of the cleanest trend-confirmation tools you can use — rarely wrong when the trend, the histogram, and the price all agree.

HOW TO READ:
• The Moving Average Convergence Divergence line above the signal line means bullish momentum.
• The Moving Average Convergence Divergence line below the signal line means bearish momentum.
• Histogram bars expanding mean the trend is strengthening. Histogram bars shrinking mean the trend is weakening.
• A cross of the zero line indicates a structural trend shift.
• Default settings: 12, 26, 9.

BUY CALL WHEN: The Moving Average Convergence Divergence line crosses above the signal line, AND the histogram bars turn green and start expanding, AND price is above the Volume Weighted Average Price line, AND a bullish candle confirms.
BUY PUT WHEN: The Moving Average Convergence Divergence line crosses below the signal line, AND the histogram bars turn red and start expanding, AND price is below the Volume Weighted Average Price line, AND a bearish candle confirms.

STOP LOSS: Just below or above the crossover candle's low or high.
TARGET: The nearest support or resistance. Exit on an opposite crossover or a histogram colour flip.
TIMEFRAME: 15-minute or 1-hour for intraday. Daily for swing trades. Lags too much on 1 to 3 minute charts.
AVOID: Range-bound markets (you get false crossovers). Also avoid low-volume sessions like the lunch hour.
→ Cross + histogram expand + candle
BOLLINGER BANDS
VOLATILITY + MEAN REVERSION
WHY IT MATTERS: Visualises volatility. The bands expand when volatility rises and contract when it collapses. A squeeze (when bands tighten significantly) almost always comes before a big directional move.

HOW TO READ:
• The bands are calculated as 20 period Simple Moving Average plus or minus 2 standard deviations.
• A band squeeze means volatility has collapsed, and an explosive move is coming.
• A band walk (price hugging the upper or lower band) signals a strong trend. Do not bet against a band walk.
• A touch of the band during a range-bound day is a mean-reversion opportunity (price will likely move back to the middle).

BUY CALL WHEN:
• Breakout play: After a squeeze, price breaks above the upper band with strong volume AND closes above the middle band.
• Mean-reversion play (range day only): A bullish rejection candle forms at the lower band.
BUY PUT WHEN:
• Breakout play: After a squeeze, price breaks below the lower band with strong volume AND closes below the middle band.
• Mean-reversion play: A bearish rejection candle at the upper band during a range.

STOP LOSS: The opposite band (for mean-reversion plays); the opposite side of the breakout candle (for breakout plays).
TARGET: The opposite band (mean-reversion) or 1 to 2 risk-to-reward ratio (breakout).
TIMEFRAME: 15-minute for intraday. 1-hour or daily for swing trades.
AVOID: Days that opened with a news-driven gap (the bands get distorted). Never short into a band walk.
→ Squeeze break + volume + close beyond mid
AVERAGE TRUE RANGE
STOP LOSS SIZING TOOL
WHY IT MATTERS: Measures volatility in points. This is the only mathematically sound way to set stop loss distance. It removes the guesswork that kills most retail trading accounts (using a fixed 10-point stop loss on a day with 120-point Average True Range will get you stopped out in 30 seconds).

HOW TO READ:
• Average True Range rising means bigger candles, so wider stops are needed.
• Average True Range falling means the market is compressed, and a breakout is brewing.
• This is NOT a signal tool — it is a position sizing tool.

STOP LOSS RULE:
• Intraday Stop Loss = 1.5 times Average True Range from your entry price.
• Swing Stop Loss = 2 to 3 times Average True Range.
TARGET RULE:
• First target = 2 times Average True Range.
• Second target = 3 times Average True Range (1 to 2 or 1 to 3 risk-to-reward).

TIMEFRAME: Match it to your trade horizon. Use the 5-minute chart's Average True Range for intraday trades, daily Average True Range for swing trades.
AVOID: Confusing the Average True Range trend with the price trend. Average True Range tells you about range, not about direction.
→ Use for SL & target distances, not entries
When to take this trade — Bollinger Band Squeeze Breakout (volatility expansion)
Setup
The Bollinger Bands have been narrowing on the 15-minute chart for the past 6 to 10 candles (the bands look pinched together). The Average True Range reading is at its lowest level of the past 5 trading days. Volume has been dropping (the calm before the storm). India Volatility Index is between 12 and 16.
Entry
Buy a Call Option (At the Money or one strike Out of the Money) when a 15-minute candle closes ABOVE the upper Bollinger Band with volume at least 2 times the recent average. For a downward break, buy a Put Option when a candle closes below the lower band.
Stop Loss
The middle Bollinger Band line. If price closes back inside the bands, the breakout has failed. For the option premium, set a hard stop at 30 to 40 percent loss.
Target
Aim for the option premium to double (a 100 percent gain). Volatility breakout trades often produce 100 to 200 percent option moves in just 1 to 3 candles, because both the price move AND the rise in Implied Volatility help your position.
Skip if
The squeeze is happening close to a major event (Reserve Bank of India meeting, Federal Reserve announcement, results day) where the breakout direction can flip after the news, or the squeeze happens during the lunch hour (12:00 PM to 1:30 PM IST).

VOLUME ANALYSIS THE HIDDEN INDICATOR

What is volume? Volume is simply the NUMBER of shares (or contracts) that changed hands in a given time period. It is shown as bars below the price chart on every trading platform.

Why volume matters more than any indicator: Price tells you WHAT happened (it went up or down). Volume tells you WHY — how much real MONEY was actually behind that move.

The simple truth:
· Big move + Big volume = REAL move. Real money moved. Trust it.
· Big move + Small volume = FAKE move. Just a few traders pushing price. Do NOT trust it.

The most honest indicator: Unlike most indicators that can show false signals, volume CANNOT be faked. If money actually moved, the volume bars show it. This page covers the 6 volume tools every serious trader uses.

HOW TO READ EACH INDICATOR CARD BELOW

  • WHY IT MATTERS — What edge it gives you and why professional traders use it.
  • HOW TO READ — The 2 to 3 actual signals you watch for.
  • BUY CALL WHEN / BUY PUT WHEN — The exact trigger conditions for taking a trade.
  • STOP LOSS / TARGET — Where the stop loss and the profit target levels go.
  • TIMEFRAME — The chart timeframe where this indicator works best.
  • AVOID — The market condition that breaks the signal.
PRINCIPLE · PRICE AND VOLUME AGREEMENT
CONFIRMATION
WHY IT MATTERS: Every genuine price move needs real money behind it. Price and volume agreement is the single most reliable confirmation tool. Professional traders confirm everything against this rule before clicking the buy button.

HOW TO READ:
• Price up + Volume up = real buying. Trust the move.
• Price up + Volume down = a weak rally. A pullback is coming.
• Price down + Volume up = real selling (distribution). Trust the fall.
• Price down + Volume down = weak selling. A bounce is likely.

BUY CALL WHEN: A bullish breakout candle forms with volume greater than 1.5 times the 20-candle average, AND price is above the Volume Weighted Average Price line.
BUY PUT WHEN: A bearish breakdown candle forms with volume greater than 1.5 times the average AND price is below the Volume Weighted Average Price line.

STOP LOSS: The opposite extreme of the breakout candle.
TARGET: 1 to 2 risk-to-reward ratio, or the next support / resistance.
TIMEFRAME: Works on every timeframe — always pair it with price action.
AVOID: The last 30 minutes (rollover and settlement distorts volume). Also avoid expiry afternoons.
VOLUME CLIMAX (BLOW-OFF TOP OR SELLING EXHAUSTION)
REVERSAL WARNING
WHY IT MATTERS: The final desperate burst of a trend. Retail traders pile in at the very top, while professional traders exit into all that excitement. Spotting a climax early means catching the best reversal trade of the day.

HOW TO READ:
• A volume bar that is 2.5 to 4 times the recent average.
• This must come after an extended move, never at the start of one.
• The candle is usually large with a big wick on top or bottom (the wick proves exhaustion).

BUY PUT WHEN: A buying climax forms (a big green candle with volume 3 times or more the average) at a resistance level after an extended rally, AND the very next candle closes below the climax candle's low (the confirmation).
BUY CALL WHEN: A selling climax forms (a big red candle with volume 3 times or more the average) at a support level after an extended fall, AND the next candle closes above the climax candle's high.

STOP LOSS: Just beyond the climax candle's extreme (the high for a Put trade, the low for a Call trade).
TARGET: The previous swing level, or 1 to 2 risk-to-reward ratio.
TIMEFRAME: 5-minute or 15-minute for intraday. Daily for swing trades.
AVOID: Never enter on the climax candle itself. Always wait for the next candle's confirmation. About 60 percent of early entries get run over.
VOLUME DRY-UP AT SUPPORT OR RESISTANCE
PROFESSIONAL SIGNAL
WHY IT MATTERS: The absence of volume at a key level is just as informative as its presence. When the big players lose interest, price gets rejected — this is the signature of a high-probability reversal.

HOW TO READ:
• Price approaches a known support or resistance level.
• Volume drops below the 20-candle average (sometimes to less than 50 percent).
• A rejection candle (Pin Bar, Shooting Star, or Hammer) prints at that level.

BUY CALL WHEN: Price tests a known support level, AND volume dries up, AND a bullish Hammer or Bullish Engulfing candle closes above the rejection bar's low.
BUY PUT WHEN: Price tests a known resistance level, AND volume dries up, AND a bearish Shooting Star or Bearish Engulfing candle closes below the rejection bar's high.

STOP LOSS: 5 to 10 points beyond the rejection candle's extreme.
TARGET: The previous swing on the opposite side, or 1 to 2 risk-to-reward ratio.
TIMEFRAME: 5-minute or 15-minute for intraday.
AVOID: The lunch hour (12:00 PM to 1:30 PM IST) — all volume dries up during this time, so it is not meaningful.
ON-BALANCE VOLUME
ACCUMULATION GAUGE
WHY IT MATTERS: Tracks the cumulative buying versus selling pressure over time. Divergence between this indicator and price reveals hidden accumulation (smart money quietly loading up) or hidden distribution (smart money quietly exiting) before price actually shows it.

HOW TO READ:
• The formula is a running total: it adds volume on up-candles, and subtracts volume on down-candles.
• On-Balance Volume rising means the market is in an accumulation phase.
• On-Balance Volume falling means the market is in a distribution phase.
• Divergence between this line and price is the highest-probability reversal signal it gives.

BUY CALL WHEN: Price is in a sideways or downward phase, AND On-Balance Volume is trending up (this is hidden accumulation), AND a breakout candle forms above the range high with volume confirmation.
BUY PUT WHEN: Price is at the highs or sideways, AND On-Balance Volume is trending down (hidden distribution), AND a breakdown candle forms below the range with volume.

STOP LOSS: Just beyond the breakout or breakdown candle's extreme.
TARGET: The range height projected, or 1 to 2 risk-to-reward ratio.
TIMEFRAME: 15-minute up to daily. Too noisy on charts below 5 minutes.
AVOID: Using On-Balance Volume on its own — always pair it with price action at a meaningful support or resistance level.
ACCUMULATION / DISTRIBUTION LINE
SMART-MONEY TRACKER
WHY IT MATTERS: Smarter than On-Balance Volume. The Accumulation / Distribution Line uses where the candle closed within its high-to-low range to weight volume. A close near the high counts as real accumulation; a close near the low counts as real distribution. It catches stealth buying and selling that On-Balance Volume misses.

HOW TO READ:
• The Accumulation line rising while price is flat means silent accumulation (buyers are absorbing all the supply).
• The line falling while price is at the highs means distribution (smart money is exiting).
• A divergence usually resolves within 5 to 10 candles.

BUY CALL WHEN: The Accumulation / Distribution Line shows a bullish divergence at support, AND a bullish candle trigger forms, AND volume confirms. Especially powerful near a key support or resistance.
BUY PUT WHEN: The line shows a bearish divergence at resistance, AND a bearish candle, AND volume confirms.

STOP LOSS: Beyond the swing high or low that created the divergence.
TARGET: 1 to 2 risk-to-reward ratio, or the next major support / resistance.
TIMEFRAME: 15-minute, 1-hour, or daily.
AVOID: News-event days (the line gets distorted by panic flows). Also avoid the first 15 minutes (data is too thin).
VOLUME PROFILE · POINT OF CONTROL / VALUE AREA HIGH AND LOW
PRICE MAGNETS
WHY IT MATTERS: Shows you WHERE volume traded (horizontal axis), not when it traded. This reveals the true support and resistance via actual participation — not subjective lines you draw. The best professional-grade support / resistance tool that exists.

HOW TO READ:
• The Point of Control is the price with the most volume traded (the strongest magnet for price).
• The Value Area High is the upper edge of the zone where 70 percent of volume traded (acts as strong resistance).
• The Value Area Low is the lower edge of the 70 percent volume zone (acts as strong support).
• A Low Volume Node is a thin zone where price travels through fast.

BUY CALL WHEN:
• Breakout play: Price closes above the Value Area High with volume, plus a bullish candle.
• Mean-reversion play: A bullish rejection forms at the Value Area Low, plus a candle trigger.
BUY PUT WHEN:
• Breakout play: Price closes below the Value Area Low with volume, plus a bearish candle.
• Mean-reversion play: A bearish rejection forms at the Value Area High, plus a candle trigger.

STOP LOSS: The opposite side of the Value Area High / Low, or beyond the Point of Control.
TARGET: The Point of Control (for mean-reversion plays); the next Low Volume Node or the prior extreme (for breakout plays).
TIMEFRAME: Overlay yesterday's daily Volume Profile on today's intraday chart.
AVOID: The first 15 minutes (today's profile is still being built — use the prior day's profile until then).
PRICE-VOLUME DIVERGENCE (WEAK TREND)
WEAK RALLY · TRUST THE DIVERGENCE
WHY IT MATTERS: A trend cannot continue without fresh money joining it. When price makes new highs (or new lows) on declining volume, you are watching a trend on fumes — this is one of the most reliable reversal signals in all of technical analysis.

HOW TO READ:
• Price prints progressively higher highs, but each new high bar has less volume than the previous one.
• The opposite for downtrends: new lows on shrinking volume means selling has been exhausted.
• Apply this rule over 3 to 6 consecutive swing points.

BUY PUT WHEN: An uptrend shows a bearish volume divergence (price makes a higher high, but volume makes a lower high) at a resistance level, AND a bearish candle trigger forms, AND the close confirms.
BUY CALL WHEN: A downtrend shows a bullish volume divergence (price makes a lower low, but volume makes a lower low — meaning selling is exhausted) at support, AND a bullish candle trigger forms.

STOP LOSS: Just beyond the divergence's swing extreme.
TARGET: The previous swing on the opposite side, or 1 to 2 risk-to-reward ratio.
TIMEFRAME: 15-minute, 1-hour, or daily. Too noisy on 1-minute or 3-minute charts.
AVOID: Never add positions in the direction of a divergent trend. Wait for the actual reversal candle — divergence tells you that momentum has died, not when price will actually turn.
VOLUME RULES OF THUMB
A breakout needs 1.5 times average volume to be trusted.
A reversal candle needs 2 times average volume to be trusted.
The first 15-minute volume is the strongest signal of the day.
A last 30-minute volume spike is rollover or settlement flow — ignore it.
Lunch-hour (12:00 PM to 1:30 PM IST) low volume is normal — not a signal.
Compare today's volume to the 20-day average, not to yesterday's volume.
When to take this trade — Volume Dry-Up Reversal at Previous Day High (high-probability reversal)
Setup
Nifty rallies up into Previous Day High during the day. As it approaches that level, the volume on each 5-minute candle drops (each new bar has lower volume than the one before). A Shooting Star or Bearish Engulfing pattern forms exactly at Previous Day High.
Entry
Buy a Put Option (At the Money) when a 5-minute candle closes BELOW the rejection candle's low, with that confirmation candle's volume back above the 20-period average.
Stop Loss
10 points above the rejection candle's high (above Previous Day High). On the option premium, set a hard stop at 30 percent loss.
Target
The Volume Weighted Average Price line as the first target (book 50 percent there). Then Previous Day Low or Day Open as the final target. Trail the stop after a 50-point Nifty move.
Skip if
The volume dry-up happens during the lunch hour (12:00 PM to 1:30 PM) — that's normal low volume, not exhaustion, OR there is breaking news pushing price into Previous Day High (the dry-up means nothing in news-driven moves).

OPTIONS BUYING GUIDE STRIKE · EXPIRY · ORDER

Read this first: You can guess the direction RIGHT and still lose money on an option. How? Most beginners pick the wrong strike (too far away), the wrong expiry (too close to expiry day), and they have no exit plan. These three mistakes cost MORE money than wrong direction calls ever do. This page fixes all three.
An eye-opener fact: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) studied Indian retail traders from April 2021 to March 2024. The result? 93 out of every 100 retail option buyers LOST money. The average loss was about ₹2 lakh per trader.

Why? Because two invisible forces work against an option BUYER every single day:
· Time decay (called Theta): The option loses value every day, like ice melting. Even if the market does not move, you LOSE money.
· Volatility crush (called the Implied Volatility drop): When fear in the market drops, option premiums shrink fast. Even if you get the direction RIGHT, the premium can drop.

This page is for buyers who accept this reality and still choose to trade — with tight rules.
WHAT IS AN OPTION? — THINK OF IT LIKE A MOVIE TICKET BOOKING
The simplest way to understand an option: Think of booking a movie ticket online for a show 3 days from now.

· You pay a small booking fee (the premium).
· The fee gives you the right to watch the movie at the locked-in price (the strike price).
· If you decide NOT to go on movie day, you simply forfeit the booking fee. Maximum loss = the small booking fee, nothing more.
· If the movie tickets become very expensive on movie day (a sold-out show), your locked-in booking is now valuable — you can transfer it to someone else for a profit.

That is exactly how an option works. You pay a small premium today for the RIGHT to buy or sell at a fixed price later. If price moves in your favour, the option becomes valuable. If not, you lose only the small premium.

Two parties exist in every option trade:
· The BUYER (you) — pays the premium. Has the RIGHT, not the obligation.
· The SELLER (also called the WRITER) — collects the premium. Has the obligation if the buyer chooses to use the right. Sellers are usually big institutions and high-net-worth individuals (because writing requires lots of margin money).
1 • CALL OPTION (buy this when you think price will GO UP)
A Call Option gives you the right to BUY the index at a fixed price. You buy a Call Option when you EXPECT the index to go UP.

Real example: Nifty is at 24,300 right now. You buy the "NIFTY 24400 Call Option" for a premium of ₹80 per share.
· If Nifty rallies to 24,600 → the premium can jump to ₹210. That is a 162 percent profit.
· If Nifty drops instead → the option loses value FAST and you can lose most of the ₹80.

Memory trick: Call = Calling price UP.
2 • PUT OPTION (buy this when you think price will GO DOWN)
A Put Option gives you the right to SELL the index at a fixed price. You buy a Put Option when you EXPECT the index to go DOWN.

Real example: Nifty is at 24,300 right now. You buy the "NIFTY 24200 Put Option" for a premium of ₹70 per share.
· If Nifty drops to 24,000 → the premium can jump to ₹190. Big profit.
· If Nifty rallies instead → the option loses value.

Memory trick: Put = Putting price DOWN.
3 • STRIKE PRICE (the locked-in price)
The strike price is the fixed price you lock in when you buy the option. You pick a strike from a long list shown in the option chain (24,000, 24,100, 24,200, and so on, in steps of 50 or 100).

Three types of strike (called "moneyness"):
· At The Money (ATM) — the strike is right around today’s spot price. (Most beginner-friendly.)
· In The Money (ITM) — the strike is already profitable. The premium is high but the option moves like the index.
· Out Of The Money (OTM) — the strike is far away. The premium is cheap but most of the time it expires worthless.

Beginner rule: always start with At The Money. Never buy far Out Of The Money because it "looks cheap".
4 • PREMIUM (the price you pay)
The premium is the price you PAY the seller for the option. It is quoted per share — so to know your total cost, multiply it by the lot size.

Real example: The NIFTY 24400 Call Option has a premium of ₹80. The Nifty lot size is 65. So total cost = 80 × 65 = ₹5,200. That is the maximum you can lose.

The premium has two parts:
· Intrinsic Value — how much profit the option already has if you were to use it RIGHT NOW.
· Time Value — the extra amount you pay because there is still time left for price to move in your favour. This time value SHRINKS every single day (this shrinking is called Theta decay).
5 • EXPIRY DATE (the deadline)
The expiry date is the deadline for the option. After this date, the option is finished — it is either worth its intrinsic value or it is worth zero.

Indian index expiry days (current rules):
· Nifty — weekly expiry every Tuesday at 3:30 PM IST.
· Sensex — weekly expiry every Thursday at 3:30 PM IST.
· Bank Nifty, Fin Nifty — only monthly expiry now (last Tuesday / Wednesday of the month). Weekly was discontinued in November 2024.

Important: An option is a "wasting asset". Every option loses time value daily. Holding LONGER does not mean MORE profit — it usually means LESS profit.
BONUS • BUYER vs SELLER (who is on the other side?)
Every option has two sides — like every insurance policy has a buyer and a company.

BUYER (mostly retail traders, like you):
· PAYS the premium upfront.
· Maximum loss = ONLY the premium paid.
· Maximum profit = very large (unlimited for a Call Option).

SELLER (also called WRITER) (mostly big institutions and rich individuals):
· RECEIVES the premium upfront.
· Maximum profit = ONLY the premium received.
· Maximum loss = very large (unlimited for a Call Option).
· Needs huge margin money — that is why retail rarely sells.

Reality check: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) study from 2024 found that 93 out of every 100 retail traders LOST money in Futures and Options. Average loss was around ₹2 lakh per trader. Most retail traders are BUYERS — the side that loses the most.
DECODING AN OPTION SYMBOL
Every option contract has a unique 5-part symbol. Once you can decode one, you can understand them all.
NIFTY  17-NOV-2026  24400  CE  @  ₹80
Part Meaning Explanation
NIFTY Underlying The index (or stock) that the option is based on — the Nifty 50 index in this case.
17-NOV-2026 Expiration Date The day this contract expires and settles. For Nifty weekly options this is always Tuesday. After this date, the option ceases to exist.
24400 Strike Price The pre-decided price at which you have the right to buy (Call Option) or sell (Put Option).
CE Type CE stands for Call European — the right to BUY. PE stands for Put European — the right to SELL. The word "European" means the option can only be exercised on the expiry day, not before.
₹80 Premium (Last Traded Price) The current market price of the option. You pay this amount to buy it. Total cost equals 80 × 65 (lot size) = ₹5,200.
HOW OPTIONS MAKE OR LOSE MONEY — THE SIMPLE PICTURE
FOR CALL OPTION BUYERS (you bet UP)
You MAKE money when: the index goes UP enough — specifically, above (strike price + premium you paid) by the expiry day.

You LOSE money when:
· the index drops, OR
· the index stays flat (time decay eats the premium), OR
· the fear in the market suddenly drops (the volatility crush).

Break-even point: Strike + Premium. So for the 24400 Call Option bought at ₹80 → Nifty must reach 24,480 just to BREAK EVEN by expiry day.

Maximum loss: 100 percent of the premium (so ₹5,200 in this example).
Maximum profit: in theory, unlimited.
FOR PUT OPTION BUYERS (you bet DOWN)
You MAKE money when: the index goes DOWN enough — specifically, below (strike price - premium paid) by expiry.

You LOSE money when:
· the index rises, OR
· the index stays flat (time decay), OR
· the fear in the market suddenly drops.

Break-even point: Strike - Premium. So for the 24200 Put Option bought at ₹70 → Nifty must fall to 24,130 just to BREAK EVEN by expiry day.

Maximum loss: 100 percent of the premium.
Maximum profit: very large (capped only when the index reaches zero).
The melting ice cube reality: An option that costs ₹80 today can be ₹65 tomorrow and ₹40 the day after — even if the index does not move at all. Time is NOT on your side when you are a buyer. The premium melts every day, like an ice cube in the sun.

That is why these two rules matter:
· Trade only the current-week At The Money strikes.
· Never "hold overnight hoping it recovers" — the next morning you will lose more from time decay alone.
STRIKE SELECTION GUIDE
AT THE MONEY (ATM)
BEST
RECOMMENDED
Spot price is roughly equal to the strike. Delta is roughly 0.5. Best balance between cost and price movement. For intraday trading, always start here. These strikes have the most liquidity and the tightest bid-ask spreads.
→ DEFAULT CHOICE
1 STRIKE OUT OF THE MONEY
OK
AGGRESSIVE
One strike above (for Calls) or below (for Puts) the At The Money strike. Cheaper premium, lower Delta. Use only when you expect a strong, fast move. Higher percentage return if you are correct, but a bigger loss if you are wrong.
→ STRONG SIGNAL ONLY
DEEP OUT OF THE MONEY
AVOID
DANGEROUS
Far away from the current spot price. Delta is very low (0.1 to 0.2). Looks cheap, but Theta decay kills it fast. Needs a massive price move to become profitable. Avoid these for intraday option buying.
→ AVOID
IN THE MONEY (ITM)
SAFE
CONSERVATIVE
The strike is already past the spot price. High Delta (0.6 to 0.8). Expensive, but moves almost like the underlying does. Good for high-conviction trades with a tight stop loss.
→ HIGH CONVICTION
When to take this trade — The right strike for your first intraday option trade
Setup
You have a clean entry signal (a candle pattern at support / resistance with volume confirmation), India Volatility Index is between 12 and 18, and the time is between 9:30 AM and 2:00 PM IST.
Entry
Buy the At The Money strike of the current-week expiry with a limit order at the mid-price (the average of the bid and ask). Position size: NEVER risk more than 1 percent of total capital on this single trade.
Stop Loss
30 percent loss on the option premium — this is the hard stop, no exceptions. For a premium of ₹100, the stop is ₹70.
Target
Book 50 percent of your position when the premium gains 30 percent. Trail the rest with a 15-point Volume Weighted Average Price stop on Nifty. Aim for at least a 1 to 2 risk-to-reward ratio after costs.
Skip if
India Volatility Index is above 22 (premiums are too inflated), OR it is the day before expiry (Theta decay accelerates and kills the buyer side), OR the time is after 2:30 PM and you do not have a confirmed trend already in place.
EXPIRY SELECTION
Weekly options are available only on Nifty 50 (NSE, Tuesday expiry) and on Sensex (BSE, Thursday expiry). Bank Nifty, Fin Nifty, and MidCap Nifty have only monthly contracts since November 2024.
Expiry Type Risk Level Theta Decay Best For Avoid When
Same Day (0 Days To Expiry — Nifty Tuesday / Sensex Thursday) VERY HIGH Extreme Experts only, clean breakout trades Beginners, sideways markets, after 1:00 PM
Current Week (Nifty / Sensex) HIGH Fast Intraday trades, strong signals Day before expiry (Monday for Nifty, Wednesday for Sensex)
Next Week (Nifty / Sensex) MEDIUM Moderate The best default for intraday option buying High Implied Volatility environments (above 20)
Monthly (All indices) LOW Slow Swing trades, positional, Bank Nifty traders Pure intraday scalping
ORDER TYPES — EXECUTION MATTERS
LIMIT ORDER
USE THIS FOR OPTIONS
Fills only at your chosen price or better. Avoids the wide bid-ask spread on options, especially at the open. Always use a limit buy at the mid-price — you save ₹3 to ₹10 per trade compared to a market order.
MARKET ORDER
AVOID FOR OPTIONS
Fills at the best available price — meaning the ask price when buying. On slow-moving strikes you can lose ₹10 or more per lot to slippage. Only acceptable for breakout trades that need an instant fill.
BRACKET ORDER
AUTO STOP LOSS + TARGET
One entry order, one stop loss order, and one target order, all placed together. Closes automatically when either is hit. Good for disciplined execution. Note: this has been mostly disabled for option buying since 2020 (the Securities and Exchange Board of India peak margin framework) — check whether your broker still offers it.
COVER ORDER
ENTRY + STOP LOSS
An entry order plus a mandatory stop loss in one order. Provides higher intraday margin on equity, but it is generally not enabled for options after the Securities and Exchange Board of India margin framework changes.
Stop Loss Market vs Stop Loss Limit — the order mechanics (which to use, how to place them on your broker, slippage rules, and worked examples) are covered in depth in the . This tab keeps the focus on entry-order selection.
COSTS & TAXATION — KNOW YOUR BREAK-EVEN
COST BREAKDOWN PER TRADE
Option buying, full round-trip (1 lot Nifty):
• Brokerage: ₹20 × 2 = ₹40
• Securities Transaction Tax (sell side only): 0.10 percent of premium value
• Exchange transaction charges: about ₹3.5
• Goods and Services Tax (18 percent on brokerage): about ₹7
• Securities and Exchange Board of India fee + Stamp duty: ₹1 to ₹2

Total comes to about ₹55 to ₹70, plus 0.10 percent Securities Transaction Tax. For a ₹150 At The Money premium × 65 lot size = ₹9,750 premium value, the Securities Transaction Tax alone comes to about ₹10.
BREAK-EVEN CALCULATION
Entry premium: ₹150
Costs: about ₹70 + Securities Transaction Tax
Lot size: 65 units
Break-even sell price for premium: about ₹151.2

That doesn't sound like much — but if you do 10 trades a month, ₹700 leaks out to costs alone. A 60 percent win rate at 1:1 risk-to-reward equals zero profit after costs. You NEED at least a 1:2 risk-to-reward just to be profitable after fees.
SECURITIES TRANSACTION TAX TRAP — THE IN-THE-MONEY EXPIRY LANDMINE
If you let an In The Money option expire instead of squaring it off, the Securities Transaction Tax jumps to 0.125 percent of the FULL intrinsic settlement value (not just the premium). This is the single biggest silent retail wipe-out cost.

Example: A Nifty 26,000 Call Option, with spot settling at 26,050, lot size 65:
• Sold before 3:30 PM → Securities Transaction Tax on premium is about ₹5 to ₹10.
• Let it expire In The Money → Securities Transaction Tax = 0.125 percent × 26,050 × 65 = about ₹2,117.

Rule: Always square off In The Money options before expiry close. The "do nothing" button is the most expensive button on your broker app.
TAXATION (FUTURES & OPTIONS, INTRADAY & POSITIONAL)
Income from Futures & Options is treated as Non-speculative Business Income under Section 43(5)(d) of the Income Tax Act (it is NOT capital gains, and NOT speculative income).
• Taxed at your applicable slab rate, added to your total income.
• Losses can offset any non-speculative business income, and can be carried forward for 8 years.
• A tax audit (under Section 44AB) is required if turnover exceeds ₹10 crore, or if you opt out of presumptive taxation with profit less than 6 percent of turnover.
• Turnover = the sum of absolute profit or loss on each trade (per the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India Guidance Note).
• Securities Transaction Tax, brokerage, exchange, and Securities and Exchange Board of India charges = all allowable as deductions.

Always consult a qualified Chartered Accountant. The treatment of Section 44AD presumptive taxation for Futures & Options is contested. This note is educational, not tax advice.
COMMON COST MISTAKES
Averaging losing options → doubles your Securities Transaction Tax drain.
Scalping for ₹5 → the costs eat the entire profit.
Chasing deep Out Of The Money options → low Delta combined with high costs equals a mathematically losing strategy.
Over-trading → 10 trades a day × ₹70 = a ₹700 daily toll on your account.
Take 2 to 3 trades a day at 1:2 risk-to-reward → costs become noise.

OPTION GREEKS THE FORCES THAT MOVE PREMIUM

What are "the Greeks"? The Greeks are 4 simple numbers that explain how the option premium moves. They are called "Greeks" because they are named after Greek letters (Delta, Theta, Vega, Gamma).

Why beginners lose money: Most retail traders look at only ONE Greek — Delta (the direction). They forget that THREE other forces are working AGAINST them:
· Theta — the option loses value every day, like an ice cube melting.
· Vega — the option loses value when fear in the market drops.
· Gamma — the option becomes more sensitive close to expiry day (small moves cause big premium swings).

Understand these 4 numbers, and you stop losing money to forces you cannot even see.
THINK OF THE 4 GREEKS LIKE THIS — A SIMPLE CAR ANALOGY
Imagine your option premium is a CAR moving on a road. The 4 Greeks are different forces affecting that car:
· Delta = the SPEED of the car (how fast premium moves with the index).
· Theta = a slow PUNCTURE in the tyre (the car loses speed every day, even when standing still).
· Vega = the WEATHER (when fear / volatility changes, the road conditions change).
· Gamma = the ACCELERATION (how fast the speed itself can change — sudden braking or sudden burst).
THE 4 GREEKS YOU MUST KNOW — ONE BY ONE
Δ DELTA — THE SPEED
0.5
AT THE MONEY OPTION
Plain English: If Nifty moves ₹1, how much will the option premium move?

· At The Money option: Delta is around 0.5 → if Nifty moves ₹1, the premium moves ₹0.50.
· Deep In The Money option: Delta is around 1 → premium moves rupee-for-rupee with Nifty.
· Deep Out Of The Money option: Delta is only 0.1 → premium barely moves.

Beginner rule: Always buy options with Delta above 0.4. Anything below moves too slowly to be worth your time.
Θ THETA — THE TIME LEAK
-ve
YOUR DAILY ENEMY
Plain English: How much premium does your option LOSE every day, EVEN if Nifty does not move?

Theta is always NEGATIVE for buyers. It is like a slow leak in your tyre — you are losing money every day you hold.

· Day 1 of the week: Theta is small.
· Day before expiry: Theta is HUGE — the premium can drop 30-40 percent in a single afternoon.

Beginner rule: Never hold an At The Money weekly option overnight on the day before expiry. Theta will destroy it.
ν VEGA — THE FEAR FACTOR
IV
WATCH BEFORE EVENTS
Plain English: How much premium does your option lose or gain when fear (volatility) in the market changes?

Think of Vega as the "fear premium". When traders are scared, they pay MORE for options. When fear drops, the premium drops too — even if Nifty moves in your favour.

Real example: Before the Union Budget, the India Volatility Index might be 25 (high fear). After the Budget speech is done, fear drops to 15. Your option premium also drops sharply — this is called "Implied Volatility crush" (or IV crush).

Beginner rule: Never buy options the day BEFORE a big event. The IV crush after the event will hurt you.
Γ GAMMA — THE ACCELERATION
Δ rate
EXPIRY DAY DRAMA
Plain English: How fast does Delta itself change?

If Delta is the speed of the car, Gamma is the acceleration. High Gamma = the speed can change very fast.

· Gamma is HIGHEST when the strike is At The Money AND expiry is close.
· This is why options on expiry day move WILDLY — one moment you are up 100 percent, the next you are down 50 percent.

Beginner rule: Avoid weekly expiry-day options unless you are very experienced. High Gamma cuts both ways — quick wins, but quicker losses.
DELTA: CALL OPTION IS POSITIVE, PUT OPTION IS NEGATIVE
Confused by the minus sign? When you open the option chain on Zerodha, Upstox, or Sensibull, you see Delta as a positive number for Call Options and a NEGATIVE number for Put Options.

The minus sign is NOT a loss indicator. It just means "this option moves in the OPPOSITE direction to Nifty". A Put Option goes UP when Nifty goes DOWN — that is what the minus sign is showing you.

Read the two cards below once and you will never confuse it again.
Δ CALL OPTION DELTA
0 to +1
POSITIVE — MOVES WITH NIFTY
A Call Option goes UP when Nifty goes UP. So its Delta is POSITIVE.

Typical Delta values:
· At The Money Call Option: +0.5 (premium moves ₹0.5 for every ₹1 move in Nifty)
· Deep In The Money Call Option: +0.9 (almost rupee-for-rupee)
· Deep Out Of The Money Call Option: +0.1 (barely moves)

Bonus tip: The Delta number also tells you the rough chance that the option will be profitable at expiry. So an At The Money option (Delta 0.5) has roughly a 50 percent chance, and a deep Out Of The Money option (Delta 0.1) has only a 10 percent chance.
Δ PUT OPTION DELTA
−1 to 0
NEGATIVE — MOVES OPPOSITE TO NIFTY
A Put Option goes UP when Nifty goes DOWN. So its Delta is NEGATIVE (the minus sign just shows the opposite direction).

Typical Delta values:
· At The Money Put Option: -0.5
· Deep In The Money Put Option: -0.9
· Deep Out Of The Money Put Option: -0.1

Ignore the minus sign for the chance calculation. A Put Option with Delta -0.5 also has roughly a 50 percent chance of being profitable at expiry. The size of the number is what matters — the sign just tells you direction.
WORKED EXAMPLE — SAME NIFTY MOVE, OPPOSITE P&L
SETUP
Nifty spot: 24,000  ·  Lot size: 65 (current Nifty lot)
Trade A: Buy 24,000 CE — ATM, Delta = +0.50, Premium ₹120
Trade B: Buy 24,000 PE — ATM, Delta = −0.50, Premium ₹115
